title: Information Systems Operations and Business Resilience

questions.question: An organization is considering using a new IT service provider. From an audit perspective, which of the following is the MOST important item to review?

options.A: References from other clients for the service provider
options.B: The physical security of the service provider site
options.C: The proposed service level agreement (SLA) with the service provider
options.D: Background checks of the service provider's employees

questions.correct_explanation: An SLA is a guarantee that the provider will deliver the services according to the contract. When contracting with a service provider, it is a good practice to enter into an SLA with the provider. The information systems (IS) auditor will want to ensure that performance and security requirements are clearly stated in the SLA.

wrong_explanations.A: A due diligence activity, such as reviewing references from other clients, is a good practice, but the service level agreement (SLA) is most critical because it defines what specific levels of performance are required and makes the provider contractually obligated to deliver what was promised.
wrong_explanations.B: A due diligence activity, such as reviewing physical security controls, is a good practice, but the SLA is most critical because it defines what specific levels of security are required and makes the provider contractually obligated to deliver what was promised.
wrong_explanations.D: A due diligence activity, such as the use of background checks for the service provider's employees, is a good practice, but the SLA is most critical because it defines what specific levels of security and labor practices are required and makes the provider contractually obligated to deliver what was promised.

tips: Trap is A 'references' — useful due diligence but not the contractual commitment.
Trap is B 'physical security' — operational concern, ideally validated via SLA terms.
Trap is D 'background checks' — operational, narrow scope.
SLA is the contractual instrument that translates expectations into enforceable performance terms. Audit value: provider can be held accountable to documented commitments.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the function of control self-assessment?

options.A: Quality control
options.B: Quality assessment
options.C: Quality planning
options.D: Quality assurance (QA)

questions.correct_explanation: Quality assurance (QA) is often achieved by the information systems (IS) auditor serving as a consultant, advising and facilitating business areas to participate in process improvement and control. One such approach is through the process of control self-assessment.

wrong_explanations.A: Quality control can be defined as the part of quality management focused on fulfilling quality requirements. Quality control procedures monitor and evaluate the resulting service or product.
wrong_explanations.B: Quality assessment is the data collection and analysis through which the degree of conformity to predetermined standards and criteria are exemplified.
wrong_explanations.C: The role of quality planning is to design a process or service that can meet established goals under operating conditions.

tips: Trap is A 'quality control' — focuses on inspecting outputs; CSA is broader.
Trap is B 'quality assessment' — measures quality, doesn't ensure it.
Trap is C 'quality planning' — designs how quality will be achieved; CSA is operational.
Quality assurance = systematic activities that ensure quality requirements are met. CSA institutionalizes assurance by making business owners responsible for ongoing control evaluation.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing a new outsourcing contract with a service provider would be MOST concerned if which of the following was missing?

options.A: A clause providing a right to audit the service provider
options.B: A clause defining penalty payments for poor performance
options.C: Predefined service level report templates
options.D: A clause regarding supplier limitation of liability

questions.correct_explanation: The absence of a right to audit clause or other forms of attestation that the supplier is compliant with a certain standard would potentially prevent the information systems (IS) auditor from investigating any aspect of supplier performance moving forward, including control deficiencies, poor performance, and adherence to legal requirements. The absence of this clause would be a major concern for the IS auditor because it would be difficult for the organization to assess whether the appropriate controls were implemented.

wrong_explanations.B: Although a clear definition of penalty payment terms is desirable, not all contracts require the payment of penalties for poor performance. When performance penalties are required, these penalties are often subject to negotiation on a case-by-case basis. Therefore, the absence of this information is not as significant as a lack of right to audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Although the inclusion of service level report templates is desirable, if the requirement for service level reporting is included in the contract, the absence of predefined templates for reporting is not a significant concern.
wrong_explanations.D: The absence of a limitation of liability clause for the service provider exposes the provider to unlimited liability. This is to the advantage of the outsourcing organization so, although the IS auditor might highlight the absence of such a clause, it does not constitute a major concern.

tips: Trap is B 'penalty payments' — important but not as foundational as audit access.
Trap is C 'service level reports' — measurement, doesn't permit verification.
Trap is D 'limitation of liability' — legal protection, doesn't enable audit.
Right-to-audit is the IS auditor's primary tool for outsourced services. Without it, the auditor cannot verify controls, performance, or compliance — defeating the audit's purpose.

questions.question: When reviewing the desktop software compliance of an organization, the information systems (IS) auditor should be MOST concerned if the installed software:

options.A: is installed, but not documented in the IT department records.
options.B: is being used by users not properly trained in its use.
options.C: is not listed in the approved software standards document.
options.D: has a license that will expire in the next 15 days.

questions.correct_explanation: Installing software not allowed by policy is a serious violation and can put the organization at security, legal and financial risk. Any software that is allowed should be part of a standard software list. This is the first thing to review because this would also indicate compliance with policies.

wrong_explanations.A: All software, including licenses, should be documented in IT department records, but this is not as serious as the violation of policy in installing unapproved software.
wrong_explanations.B: Discovering that users have not been formally trained in the use of a software product is common, and, although not ideal, most software includes help files and other tips that can assist in learning how to use the software effectively.
wrong_explanations.D: A software license that is about to expire is not a risk if there is a process in place to renew it.

tips: Trap is A 'not documented in IT records' — bookkeeping issue, addressable.
Trap is B 'users not trained' — operational concern, training gap.
Trap is D 'license expiring in 15 days' — administrative, addressable.
Software not on the approved list = unvetted security/legal risk. Could be unlicensed, vulnerable, or incompatible. Most serious compliance and security concern.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor of a health care organization is reviewing contractual terms and conditions of a third-party cloud provider being considered to host patient health information. Which of the following contractual terms is the GREATEST risk to the customer organization?

options.A: Data ownership is retained by the customer organization.
options.B: The third-party provider reserves the right to access data to perform certain operations.
options.C: Bulk data withdrawal mechanisms are undefined.
options.D: The customer organization is responsible for backup, archiving and restoration.

questions.correct_explanation: Organizations must review the regulatory environment in which the cloud provider operates because it may have requirements or restrictions of its own. Some service providers reserve the right to access customer information (third-party access) to perform certain transactions and provide certain services. In the case of protected health information, regulations may restrict certain access. Organizations must then determine whether the cloud provider provides appropriate controls to ensure data security.

wrong_explanations.A: The customer organization would want to retain data ownership and, therefore, this would not be a risk.
wrong_explanations.C: An organization may eventually wish to discontinue its service with a third-party cloud-based provider. The organization would then want to remove its data from the system and ensure that the service provider clears the system (including any backups) of its data. Some providers do not offer automated or bulk data withdrawal mechanisms, which the organization needs to migrate its data. These aspects should be clarified prior to using a third-party provider.
wrong_explanations.D: An organization may need to plan its own data recovery processes and procedures if the service provider does not make this available or the organization has doubts about the service provider's processes. This would only be a risk if the customer organization could not perform these activities.

tips: Trap is A 'data ownership retained' — that's the customer's preferred term, not a risk.
Trap is C 'bulk data withdrawal undefined' — exit-strategy concern, manageable.
Trap is D 'customer responsible for backup' — clear allocation, not a risk.

Provider reserved access to PHI = HIPAA/regulatory exposure. Provider personnel may access protected health information for 'operations' but the customer owns the regulatory risk. GREATEST concern in healthcare cloud.

questions.question: Which recovery strategy is MOST appropriate for a business with multiple offices within a region and a limited recovery budget?

options.A: Hot site maintained by the business
options.B: Commercial cold site
options.C: Reciprocal arrangement between its offices
options.D: Third-party hot site

questions.correct_explanation: A reciprocal arrangement among its offices would be most appropriate for a business with many offices within a region. Each office can be designated as a recovery site for some other office. This would be the least expensive approach and would provide an acceptable level of confidence.

wrong_explanations.A: A hot site maintained by the business would be costly but would provide a high degree of confidence.
wrong_explanations.B: Multiple cold sites leased for the multiple offices would lead to an ineffective solution with poor availability.
wrong_explanations.D: A traditional hot site provides a third-party facility for recovery. This would be a costly approach providing a high degree of confidence.

tips: Trap is A 'hot site by the business' — costly; large investment for limited budget.
Trap is B 'commercial cold site' — third-party costs add up; many sites needed.
Trap is D 'third-party hot site' — still costly per site.

Multiple offices in one region = built-in mutual recovery capability. Each office serves as recovery site for another at minimal incremental cost. Best fit for distributed orgs with budget constraints.

questions.question: During an application audit, an information systems (IS) auditor is asked to provide assurance of the database's referential integrity. Which of the following should be reviewed?

options.A: Field definition
options.B: Master table definition
options.C: Composite keys
options.D: Foreign key structure

questions.correct_explanation: Referential integrity in a relational database refers to consistency between coupled (linked) tables. Referential integrity is usually enforced by the combination of a primary key or candidate key (alternate key) and a foreign key. For referential integrity to hold, any field in a table that is declared a foreign key should contain only values from a parent table's primary key or a candidate key.

wrong_explanations.A: Field definitions describe the table layout but are not directly related to referential integrity.
wrong_explanations.B: Master table definition describes the database structure but is not directly related to referential integrity.
wrong_explanations.C: Composite keys describe how the keys are created but are not directly related to referential integrity.

tips: Trap is A 'field definition' — describes individual fields, not relationships.
Trap is B 'master table definition' — single table, doesn't show inter-table integrity.
Trap is C 'composite keys' — primary key construct within a table.
Foreign keys enforce referential integrity by linking rows across tables. Reviewing foreign key structure verifies that relationships between tables are consistently maintained.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing database security for an organization. Which of the following is the MOST important consideration for database hardening?

options.A: The default configurations are changed.
options.B: All tables in the database are denormalized.
options.C: Stored procedures and triggers are encrypted.
options.D: The service port used by the database server is changed.

questions.correct_explanation: Default database configurations, such as default passwords and services, need to be changed; otherwise, the database can be easily compromised by malicious code and by intruders.

wrong_explanations.B: The denormalization of a database is related more to performance than to security.
wrong_explanations.C: Limiting access to stored procedures is a valid security consideration but not as critical as changing default configurations.
wrong_explanations.D: Changing the service port used by the database is a component of the configuration changes that can be made to the database, but other more critical configuration changes should be made first.

tips: Trap is B 'denormalize tables' — performance optimization, not security.
Trap is C 'encrypt stored procedures' — protects code, doesn't address default vulnerabilities.
Trap is D 'change service port' — security through obscurity, low effectiveness.
Default configurations (default passwords, services, permissions) are publicly documented. Attackers know them. Changing defaults is the foundational hardening step before everything else.

questions.question: When auditing a database environment, an information systems (IS) auditor will be MOST concerned if the database administrator (DBA) is performing which of the following functions?

options.A: Performing database changes according to change management procedures
options.B: Installing patches or upgrades to the operating system
options.C: Sizing table space and consulting on table join limitations
options.D: Performing backup and recovery procedures

questions.correct_explanation: Installing patches or upgrades to the operating system is a function that should be performed by a systems administrator, not by a DBA. If a DBA is performing this function, there is risk based on inappropriate separation of duties.

wrong_explanations.A: Performing database changes according to change management procedures is a normal function of the database administrator (DBA) and is compliant with the organization's procedures.
wrong_explanations.C: A DBA is expected to support the business by helping design, create and maintain databases and the interfaces to the databases.
wrong_explanations.D: The DBA often performs or supports database backup and recovery procedures.

tips: Trap is A 'database changes per change management' — that's the DBA's job.
Trap is C 'sizing tablespace, table joins' — DBA expertise area.
Trap is D 'backup and recovery' — DBA responsibility for database recovery.
OS patching is sysadmin work, not DBA. DBA installing OS patches = SoD violation; DBA controls both database AND underlying OS, with no independent oversight.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST reasonable option for recovering a noncritical system?

options.A: Warm site
options.B: Mobile site
options.C: Hot site
options.D: Cold site

questions.correct_explanation: Generally, a cold site is contracted for a longer period at a lower cost. It is generally used for noncritical applications because it requires more time to make a cold site operational.

wrong_explanations.A: A warm site is generally available at a medium cost, requires less time to become operational and is suitable for sensitive operations that should be recovered in a moderate amount of time.
wrong_explanations.B: A mobile site is a vehicle ready with all necessary computer equipment that can be moved to any location, depending upon the need. The need for a mobile site relies on the scale of operations.
wrong_explanations.C: A hot site is contracted for a shorter time period at a higher cost, and it is better suited for recovery of vital and critical applications.

tips: Trap is A 'warm site' — over-provisioned for noncritical systems.
Trap is B 'mobile site' — situational, not the most reasonable for noncritical.
Trap is C 'hot site' — significantly more expensive, used for critical systems.
Cold site = empty space + utilities. Cheapest, longest activation time. Appropriate for systems where extended downtime is acceptable.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor evaluates the effectiveness of the change management process in an organization. What is the MOST important control that the IS auditor should look for to ensure system availability?

options.A: Changes are authorized by IT managers at all times.
options.B: User acceptance testing (UAT) is performed and properly documented.
options.C: Test plans and procedures exist and are closely followed.
options.D: Capacity planning is performed as part of each development project.

questions.correct_explanation: The most important control for ensuring system availability is to implement a sound test plan and procedures that are followed consistently.

wrong_explanations.A: Changes are usually required to be signed off by a business analyst, member of the change control board or other authorized representatives, not necessarily by IT management.
wrong_explanations.B: User acceptance testing (UAT) is important but not a critical element of change control and does not usually address the topic of availability as asked in the question.
wrong_explanations.D: While capacity planning should be considered in each development project, it will not ensure system availability, nor is it part of the change control process.

tips: Trap is A 'authorized at all times' — addresses approval, not availability impact.
Trap is B 'UAT performed' — addresses functionality, not availability.
Trap is D 'capacity planning per project' — operational good practice but specific to capacity, not change-related availability.
Test plans + procedures followed = changes don't break production. Skipping testing is the #1 cause of change-induced outages. Availability flows from disciplined testing.

questions.question: Data flow diagrams are used by information systems (IS) auditors to:

options.A: identify key controls.
options.B: highlight high-level data definitions.
options.C: graphically summarize data paths and storage.
options.D: portray step-by-step details of data generation.

questions.correct_explanation: Data flow diagrams are used as aids to graph or chart data flow and storage. They trace data from their origination to their destination, highlighting the paths and storage of data.

wrong_explanations.A: Identifying key controls is not the focus of data flow diagrams. The focus is the flow of data.
wrong_explanations.B: A data dictionary may be used to document data definitions, but the data flow diagram is used to document how data move through a process.
wrong_explanations.D: The purpose of a data flow diagram is to track the movement of data through a process and is not primarily to document or indicate how data are generated.

tips: Trap is A 'identify key controls' — possible side effect, not the primary purpose.
Trap is B 'highlight high-level data definitions' — vocabulary, not flow.
Trap is D 'step-by-step generation details' — too granular; that's a process diagram.
Data flow diagrams answer: where does data come from, where does it go, where does it stop? Visual map of paths and storage. Foundational for understanding system architecture.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is useful while drafting a disaster recovery plan (DRP)?

options.A: Downtime costs decrease as the recovery point objective (RPO) increases.
options.B: Downtime costs increase with time.
options.C: Recovery costs are independent of time.
options.D: Recovery costs can only be controlled on a short-term basis.

questions.correct_explanation: Downtime costs-such as loss of sales, idle resources and salaries-increase with time. A disaster recovery plan (DRP) should be drawn up to achieve the lowest downtime costs possible.

wrong_explanations.A: Downtime costs are not related to the recovery point objective (RPO). The RPO defines the data backup strategy, which is related to recovery costs rather than to downtime costs.
wrong_explanations.C: Recovery costs decrease with the time allowed for recovery. For example, recovery costs to recover business operations within two days will be higher than recovery costs within seven days. The essence of an effective DRP is to minimize uncertainty and increase predictability.
wrong_explanations.D: With good planning, recovery costs can be predicted and contained.

tips: Trap is A 'downtime decreases as RPO increases' — RPO doesn't drive downtime cost.
Trap is C 'recovery costs independent of time' — false; recovery costs DECREASE with longer time available.
Trap is D 'recovery costs only short-term' — false; long-term planning controls recovery cost.
Downtime costs (lost revenue, idle staff, customer impact) accumulate with every hour. The longer the outage, the higher the cost. DRP design must minimize this duration.

questions.question: Although management has stated otherwise, an information systems (IS) auditor has reasons to believe that the organization is using software that is not licensed. In this situation, the IS auditor should FIRST:

options.A: include the statement from management in the audit report.
options.B: verify that the software is in use through testing.
options.C: include the item in the audit report.
options.D: discuss the issue with senior management because it could have a negative impact on the organization.

questions.correct_explanation: When there is an indication that an organization might be using unlicensed software, the information systems (IS) auditor should obtain sufficient evidence before including it in the report.

wrong_explanations.A: The statement from management may be included in the audit report, but the auditor should independently validate the statements made by management to ensure completeness and accuracy.
wrong_explanations.C: With respect to this matter, representations obtained from management cannot be independently verified.
wrong_explanations.D: If the organization is using software that is not licensed, the IS auditor must include this in the report to maintain objectivity and independence, but the IS auditor should verify that this is the case before presenting it to senior management.

tips: Trap is A 'include management statement' — shifts responsibility but doesn't validate the concern.
Trap is C 'include in audit report' — premature; finding not yet validated.
Trap is D 'discuss with senior management' — escalation without evidence.
Auditor concern + management denial = need independent verification through testing. Don't report unconfirmed findings; gather evidence first.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY role of the information systems (IS) auditor in controlling self-assessment programs?

options.A: Assessor
options.B: Participant
options.C: Facilitator
options.D: Manager

questions.correct_explanation: When CSA programs are established, auditors become internal control professionals and assessment facilitators.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor leads and guides the auditees in assessing their environment by providing insights about the objectives of controls based on risk assessment.
wrong_explanations.B: The IS auditor is the facilitator, and the management client participates in the control self-assessment (CSA) program.
wrong_explanations.D: The business unit managers take responsibility for and ownership of internal control systems under their authority.

tips: Trap is A 'assessor' — auditor evaluates controls, but CSA flips that to business ownership.
Trap is B 'participant' — auditor not directly participating; preserves independence.
Trap is D 'manager' — operational role, compromises independence.
CSA = business owns control assessment. Auditor's role is to facilitate the business's self-assessment process — provide guidance, not perform the assessment.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST critical element to execute a disaster recovery plan (DRP) effectively?

options.A: Off site storage of backup data
options.B: Up-to-date list of key disaster recovery contacts
options.C: Availability of a replacement data center
options.D: Clearly defined recovery time objective

questions.correct_explanation: Remote storage of backups is the most critical disaster recovery plan (DRP) element of the items listed because access to backup data is required to restore systems.

wrong_explanations.B: Having a list of key contacts is important but not as important as having adequate data backup.
wrong_explanations.C: A DRP may use a replacement data center or some other solution, such as a mobile site, reciprocal agreement, or outsourcing agreement.
wrong_explanations.D: Having a clearly defined recovery time objective is especially important for business continuity planning, but the core element of disaster recovery (the recovery of IT infrastructure and capability) is data backup.

tips: Trap is B 'contact list' — useful but useless without backup data.
Trap is C 'replacement data center' — provides hardware but no data without backups.
Trap is D 'defined RTO' — target without backups can't be met.
Backup data is the irreplaceable foundation of recovery. Hardware can be procured, contacts can be reached, but lost data cannot be reconstructed without backups. Most critical DRP element.

questions.question: While reviewing the process for continuous monitoring of the capacity and performance of IT resources, an information systems (IS) auditor should PRIMARILY ensure that the process is focused on which of the following?

options.A: Adequately monitoring service levels of IT resources and services
options.B: Providing data to enable timely planning for capacity and performance requirements
options.C: Providing accurate feedback on IT resource capacity
options.D: Properly forecasting performance, capacity and throughput of IT resources

questions.correct_explanation: Accurate capacity monitoring of IT resources is a critical element of a continuous monitoring process.

wrong_explanations.A: Continuous monitoring helps to ensure that service level agreements (SLAs) are met, but this is not the primary focus of monitoring. It is possible that even if a system were oftline, it would meet the requirements of an SLA. Therefore, accurate availability monitoring is more important.
wrong_explanations.B: data gained from capacity and performance monitoring is an input to the planning process, the primary focus is to monitor availability.
wrong_explanations.D: Although continuous monitoring helps management to predict likely IT resource capabilities, the more critical issue is that availability monitoring is accurate.

tips: Trap is A 'monitoring service levels' — output of monitoring, not the monitoring itself.
Trap is B 'data for capacity planning' — use of data, not the monitoring focus.
Trap is D 'forecasting performance' — secondary use, not primary monitoring focus.
Continuous monitoring's primary value: ACCURATE feedback on capacity. Without accuracy, planning fails, service levels drift, forecasts are wrong. Accuracy is the foundation.

questions.question: Which of the following groups is the BEST source of information for determining the criticality of application systems as part of a business impact analysis (BIA)?

options.A: Business processes owners
options.B: IT management
options.C: Senior business management
options.D: Industry experts

questions.correct_explanation: Business process owners have the most relevant information to contribute because the business impact analysis (BIA) is designed to evaluate criticality and recovery timelines, based on business needs.

wrong_explanations.B: Although IT management must be involved, it may not be fully aware of the business processes that need to be protected.
wrong_explanations.C: Although senior management must be involved, it may not be fully aware of the criticality of applications that need to be protected.
wrong_explanations.D: The BIA depends on the organization's unique business needs, and the advice of industry experts is of limited value.

tips: Trap is B 'IT management' — knows technical impact, not business impact.
Trap is C 'senior business management' — strategic view, but process owners know operational criticality.
Trap is D 'industry experts' — external benchmarks, not the org's specific reality.
BIA measures business impact of system loss. Process owners run the processes that depend on the systems — they know what hurts most when systems fail. Best source for criticality.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing an organization's disaster recovery plan (DRP) implementation. The project was completed on time and on budget. During the review, the auditor uncovers several areas of concern. Which of the following presents the GREATEST risk?

options.A: Testing of the DRP has not been performed.
options.B: The disaster recovery strategy does not specify the use of a hot site.
options.C: The business impact analysis (BIA) was conducted, but the results were not used.
options.D: The disaster recovery project manager for the implementation has recently left the organization.

questions.correct_explanation: The risk of not using the business impact analysis (BIA) results for disaster recovery planning means that the DRP may not be designed to recover the most critical assets in the correct order. As a result, the plan may not be adequate to allow the organization to recover from a disaster.

wrong_explanations.A: Although testing a disaster recovery plan (DRP) is a critical component of a successful disaster recovery strategy, this is not the biggest risk; the biggest risk comes from a plan that is not properly designed.
wrong_explanations.B: The use of a hot site is a strategic determination based on tolerable downtime, cost and other factors. Although using a hot site may be considered a good practice, this is a very costly solution that may not be required for the organization.
wrong_explanations.D: If the DRP is designed and documented properly, the loss of an experienced project manager should have minimal impact. The risk of a poorly designed plan that may not meet the requirements of the business is much more significant than the risk posed by the loss of the project manager.

tips: Trap is A 'no DRP testing' — concerning but the plan may still be sound.
Trap is B 'no hot site' — strategic choice based on RTO/RPO, not necessarily wrong.
Trap is D 'project manager left' — personnel risk, addressable through documentation.
BIA conducted but not used = the plan was built without business input. The DRP may recover the wrong systems first or miss critical ones. Foundational design failure.

questions.question: A vendor released several critical security patches over the past few months, which put a strain on the ability of the administrators to keep the patches tested and deployed in a timely manner. The administrators asked if they could reduce the testing of the patches. What approach should the organization take?

options.A: Continue the current process of testing and applying patches.
options.B: Reduce testing and ensure that an adequate back-out plan is in place.
options.C: Delay patching until resources for testing are available.
options.D: Rely on the vendor's testing of the patches.

questions.correct_explanation: Applying security software patches promptly is critical to maintaining the security of the servers; further, testing the patches is important because the patches may affect other systems and business operations. Because the vendor recently released several critical patches in a short time, the organization may choose to wait to see if this is a temporary problem before making a revision to policy or procedures.

wrong_explanations.B: Reduced testing increases the risk of business operation disruption due to a faulty or incompatible patch. Although a back-out plan does help mitigate this risk, a thorough testing up front is the more appropriate option.
wrong_explanations.C: Applying security software patches promptly is critical to maintaining the security of the servers. Delaying patching increases the risk of a security breach due to system vulnerability.
wrong_explanations.D: The testing done by the vendor may not be applicable to the systems and environment of the organization that needs to deploy the patches.

tips: Trap is B 'reduce testing + back-out plan' — back-out doesn't compensate for skipped testing.
Trap is C 'delay patching' — security risk; vulnerabilities exposed longer.
Trap is D 'rely on vendor testing' — vendor doesn't know your environment; their testing isn't sufficient.

Testing patches before deployment is non-negotiable. Patches can break systems and introduce new bugs. Continuing the process — even under strain — is correct; the answer is to find more resources, not skip testing.

questions.question: Which of the following issues should be a MAJOR concern to an information systems (IS) auditor who is reviewing a service level agreement (SLA)?

options.A: A service adjustment resulting from an exception report took a day to implement.
options.B: The complexity of application logs used for service monitoring made the review difficult.
options.C: Key performance indicators (KPls) were not included in the SLA.
options.D: The document is updated on an annual basis.

questions.correct_explanation: Lack of service measures, such as key performance indicators (KPls), makes it difficult to gauge the efficiency and effectiveness of the IT services being provided. Although KPls can vary based on the nature of the service and the agreement between parties, commonly included KPis in SLAs include response time, uptime, service reliability, etc.

wrong_explanations.A: Resolving issues related to exception reports is an operational issue that should be addressed in the service level agreement (SLA); however, a response time of one day may be acceptable, depending on the terms of the SLA.
wrong_explanations.B: The complexity of application logs is an operational issue, which is not related to the SLA.
wrong_explanations.D: Although it is important that the document be current, depending on the term of the agreement, it may not be necessary to change the document more frequently than annually.

tips: Trap is A 'service adjustment took a day' — operational metric, may meet SLA.
Trap is B 'logs complex' — review difficulty, not SLA quality issue.
Trap is D 'updated annually' — may be appropriate, not necessarily a concern.
SLA without KPIs = unmeasurable performance commitment. Provider can't be held accountable to vague targets. KPIs make commitments operational and verifiable.

questions.question: During an information systems (IS) audit of the disaster recovery plan of a global enterprise, the auditor observes that some remote offices have very limited local IT resources. Which of the following observations is the MOST critical for the IS auditor?

options.A: A test has not been made to ensure that local resources can maintain security and service standards when recovering from a disaster or incident.
options.B: The corporate business continuity plan (BCP) plan does not accurately document the systems that exist at remote offices.
options.C: Corporate security measures have not been incorporated into the test plan.
options.D: A test has not been made to ensure that backups from the remote offices are usable.

questions.correct_explanation: Regardless of the capability of local IT resources, the most critical risk is the lack of testing that would identify quality issues in the recovery process.

wrong_explanations.B: The corporate business continuity plan (BCP) may not include disaster recovery plan (DRP) details for remote offices. It is important to ensure that the local plans have been tested.
wrong_explanations.C: Security is an important issue because many controls may be missing during a disaster. However, not having a tested plan is more important.
wrong_explanations.D: The backups cannot be trusted until they have been tested. However, this should be done as part of the overall tests of the DRP.

tips: Trap is B 'BCP doesn't document remote systems' — documentation gap, addressable.
Trap is C 'security not in test plan' — narrow concern.
Trap is D 'backups not tested' — important but narrow; the broader recovery process matters more.

Without testing, recovery process for remote sites is theoretical. Quality issues, missing dependencies, integration gaps go undiscovered until disaster strikes. Testing surfaces problems while they're fixable.

questions.question: Which of the following reports should an information systems (IS) auditor use to check compliance with a service level agreement's requirement for uptime?

options.A: Utilization reports
options.B: Hardware error reports
options.C: System logs
options.D: Availability reports

questions.correct_explanation: information systems (IS) inactivity, such as downtime, is addressed by availability reports. These reports provide the time periods during which the computer was available for utilization by users or other processes.

wrong_explanations.A: Utilization reports document the use of computer equipment, and can be used by management to predict how, where and/or when resources are required.
wrong_explanations.B: Hardware error reports provide information to aid in detecting hardware failures and initiating corrective action. These error reports may not indicate actual system uptime.
wrong_explanations.C: System logs are used for recording system's activities. They may not indicate availability.

tips: Trap is A 'utilization reports' — measure usage, not availability.
Trap is B 'hardware error reports' — error frequency, not uptime metric.
Trap is C 'system logs' — granular events, not summary uptime.
Availability reports specifically measure system uptime — direct match to SLA uptime requirements. Other reports require interpretation; availability reports are the answer.

questions.question: Which of the following would an information systems (IS) auditor use to determine if unauthorized modifications were made to production programs?

options.A: System log analysis
options.B: Compliance testing
options.C: Forensic analysis
options.D: Analytical review

questions.correct_explanation: To determine that only authorized modifications are made to production programs requires the change management process to be reviewed to evaluate the existence of a trail of documentary evidence. Compliance testing helps to verify that the change management process has been applied consistently.

wrong_explanations.A: System log analysis identifies changes and activity on a system but does not identify whether the change was authorized unless conducted as a part of a compliance test.
wrong_explanations.C: Forensic analysis is a specialized technique for criminal investigation.
wrong_explanations.D: An analytical review assesses the general control environment of an organization.

tips: Trap is A 'system log analysis' — captures activity but doesn't validate authorization.
Trap is C 'forensic analysis' — incident response, not change verification.
Trap is D 'analytical review' — pattern analysis, not authorization check.
Compliance testing = does what happened match what was authorized? Comparing change tickets to actual production changes verifies the change management process worked.

questions.question: During a production system change control audit, an information systems (IS) auditor finds that the change management process is not formally documented and that some migration procedures failed. What should the IS auditor do next?

options.A: Recommend redesigning the change management process.
options.B: Gain more assurance on the findings through root cause analysis.
options.C: Recommend that program migration be stopped until the change process is documented.
options.D: Document the finding and present it to management.

questions.correct_explanation: A change management process is critical to IT production systems. Before recommending that the organization take any other action (e.g., stopping migrations or redesigning the change management process), the information systems (IS) auditor should gain assurance that the incidents reported are related to deficiencies in the change management process and not caused by some process other than change management.

wrong_explanations.A: Although it may be necessary to redesign the change management process, this cannot be done until a root cause analysis is conducted to determine why the current process is not being followed.
wrong_explanations.C: A business relies on being able to make changes when necessary, and security patches must often be deployed promptly. It is not feasible to halt all changes until a new process is developed.
wrong_explanations.D: The audit results, including the findings of noncompliance, will be delivered to management after a root cause analysis of the issue has been completed.

tips: Trap is A 'redesign change management' — premature without root cause.
Trap is C 'stop migrations' — overreaction without analysis.
Trap is D 'document and present' — incomplete; needs root cause first.
Audit finding requires understanding WHY, not just WHAT. Root cause analysis distinguishes 'process flaw' from 'one-time deviation' from 'training gap'. Recommendations follow analysis.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor evaluating the resilience of a high-availability network should be MOST concerned if:

options.A: the setup is geographically dispersed.
options.B: the servers are clustered in one site.
options.C: a hot site is ready for activation.
options.D: diverse routing is implemented for the network.

questions.correct_explanation: A clustered setup in one site makes the entire network vulnerable to natural disasters or other disruptive events.

wrong_explanations.A: Dispersed geographic locations provide backup if a site has been destroyed.
wrong_explanations.C: A hot site is also a good alternative for a single-point-of-failure site.
wrong_explanations.D: Diverse routing provides telecommunications backup if a network is not available.

tips: Trap is A 'geographically dispersed' — that's RESILIENT, not a concern.
Trap is C 'hot site ready' — readiness is good, not a concern.
Trap is D 'diverse routing' — also resilient, not a concern.
Clustering in one site = single point of failure for the entire cluster. Natural disaster, fire, or facility outage takes down the whole HA setup. Defeats the purpose of high availability.

questions.question: Management considered two projections for its disaster recovery plan (DRP): plan A with two months to fully recover and plan B with eight months to fully recover. The recovery point objectives (RPOs) are the same in both plans. It is reasonable to expect that plan B projected higher:

options.A: downtime costs.
options.B: resumption costs.
options.C: recovery costs.
options.D: walk-through costs.

questions.correct_explanation: Because management considered a longer time window for recovery in plan B, downtime costs included in the plan are likely to be higher.

wrong_explanations.B: Because the recovery time for plan B is longer, resumption costs can be expected to be lower.
wrong_explanations.C: Because the recovery time for plan B is longer, recovery costs can be expected to be lower.
wrong_explanations.D: Walk-through costs are not a part of disaster recovery.

tips: Trap is B 'resumption costs' — costs of restarting; lower with longer recovery time (more planning).
Trap is C 'recovery costs' — also lower for longer recovery (less expensive solutions feasible).
Trap is D 'walk-through costs' — testing cost, unrelated to recovery duration.
Longer downtime = more lost revenue, customers, productivity. Plan B with 8-month recovery accumulates 4x the downtime costs of Plan A's 2-month recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following would an information systems (IS) auditor consider to be MOST helpful when evaluating the effectiveness and adequacy of a preventive computer maintenance program?

options.A: System downtime log
options.B: Vendor reliability figures
options.C: Regularly scheduled maintenance log
options.D: Written preventive maintenance schedule

questions.correct_explanation: A system downtime log provides evidence regarding the effectiveness and adequacy of computer preventive maintenance programs. The log is a detective control, but because it is validating the effectiveness of the maintenance program, it is validating a preventive control.

wrong_explanations.B: Vendor reliability figures are not an effective measure of a preventive maintenance program.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing the log is a good detective control to ensure that maintenance is being done; however, only the system downtime will indicate whether the preventive maintenance is actually working well.
wrong_explanations.D: A schedule is a good control to ensure that maintenance is scheduled and that no items are missed in the maintenance schedule; however, it is not a guarantee that the work is actually being done.

tips: Trap is B 'vendor reliability figures' — vendor self-reported data, less reliable.
Trap is C 'maintenance log' — records what was done, not what it prevented.
Trap is D 'maintenance schedule' — plan, not actual results.
System downtime log measures the OUTCOME of preventive maintenance: did it prevent downtime? Direct evidence of program effectiveness.

questions.question: An organization implemented an online customer help desk application using a software as a service (SaaS) operating model. An information systems (IS) auditor is asked to recommend the best control to monitor the service level agreement (SLA) with the SaaS vendor regarding availability. What is the BEST recommendation that the IS auditor can provide?

options.A: Ask the SaaS vendor to provide a weekly report on application uptime.
options.B: Implement an online polling tool to monitor the application and record outages.
options.C: Log all application outages reported by users and aggregate the outage time weekly.
options.D: Contract an independent third party to provide weekly reports on application uptime.

questions.correct_explanation: Implementing an online polling tool to monitor and record application outages is the best option for an organization to monitor the software as a service application availability. Comparing internal reports with the vendor's service level agreement (SLA) reports ensures that the vendor's monitoring of the SLA is accurate and that all conflicts are appropriately resolved.

wrong_explanations.A: Weekly application availability reports are useful, but these reports represent only the vendor's perspective. While monitoring these reports, the organization can raise concerns of inaccuracy; however, without internal monitoring, such concerns cannot be substantiated.
wrong_explanations.C: Logging the outage times reported by users is helpful but does not give a true picture of all outages of the online application. Some outages may go unreported, especially if the outages are intermittent.
wrong_explanations.D: Contracting a third party to implement availability monitoring is not a cost-effective option. Additionally, this results in a shift from monitoring the software as a service (SaaS) vendor to monitoring the third party.

tips: Trap is A 'vendor weekly report' — vendor self-reported, biased.
Trap is C 'log user-reported outages' — users may not report; incomplete data.
Trap is D 'third-party weekly reports' — useful but expensive and indirect.
Online polling tool independently measures availability — same metric SaaS vendor reports, but verified directly. Independent + automated + continuous = best monitoring.

questions.question: Applying a retention date on a file will ensure that:

options.A: data cannot be read until the date is set.
options.B: data will not be deleted before that date.
options.C: backup copies are not retained after that date.
options.D: datasets having the same name are differentiated.

questions.correct_explanation: A retention date ensures that a file cannot be overwritten or deleted before that date has passed.

wrong_explanations.A: The retention date does not affect the ability to read the file.
wrong_explanations.C: Backup copies would be expected to have a different retention date and, therefore, may be retained after the file has been overwritten.
wrong_explanations.D: The creation date, not the retention date, differentiates files with the same name.

tips: Trap is A 'data unreadable until date' — file IS readable; date controls deletion.
Trap is C 'backups not retained after date' — opposite; retention date PROTECTS retention.
Trap is D 'differentiate same-name datasets' — that's a different metadata concern.
Retention date = preservation guarantee. File cannot be deleted, overwritten, or destroyed before the retention date passes. Ensures regulatory and legal retention compliance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a network diagnostic tool that monitors and records network information?

options.A: Online monitor
options.B: Downtime report
options.C: Help desk report
options.D: Protocol analyzer

questions.correct_explanation: Protocol analyzers are network diagnostic tools that monitor and record network information from packets traveling in the link to which the analyzer is attached.

wrong_explanations.A: Online monitors measure telecommunication transmissions and determine whether transmissions were accurate and complete.
wrong_explanations.B: Downtime reports track the availability of telecommunication lines and circuits.
wrong_explanations.C: Help desk reports are prepared by the help desk, which is staffed or supported by information systems (IS) technical support personnel trained to handle problems occurring during the course of IS operations.

tips: Trap is A 'online monitor' — monitors transmission accuracy, not network packets broadly.
Trap is B 'downtime report' — summary tool, not diagnostic.
Trap is C 'help desk report' — incident summary, not network diagnostic.
Protocol analyzer captures and decodes network packets in real time. Tells you exactly what's flowing on the wire — most powerful network diagnostic tool.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor needs to review the procedures used to restore a software application to its state prior to an upgrade. Therefore, the auditor needs to assess the following:

options.A: Problem management procedures
options.B: Software development procedures
options.C: Back-out procedures
options.D: Incident management procedures

questions.correct_explanation: Back-out procedures are used to restore a system to a previous state and are an important element of the change control process. The other choices are not related to the change control process, which specifies what procedures should be followed when software is being upgraded but does not work and requires a Callback to its former state.

wrong_explanations.A: Problem management procedures are used to track user feedback and issues related to the operation of an application for trend analysis and problem resolution.
wrong_explanations.B: Software development procedures, such as the software development life cycle (SDLC), are used to manage the creation or acquisition of new or modified software.
wrong_explanations.D: Incident management procedures are used to manage errors or problems with system operation. A help desk usually uses them. One of the incident management procedures may be how to follow a fallback plan.

tips: Trap is A 'problem management' — incident-driven, not change-rollback.
Trap is B 'software development procedures' — too broad; rollback is specific.
Trap is D 'incident management' — handles disruption events, not planned rollback.
Back-out procedures: documented steps to UNDO a change. Critical when an upgrade fails or causes problems. Required element of change management.

questions.question: Which of the following is a MAJOR concern during a review of help desk activities?

options.A: The help desk team could not resolve certain calls.
options.B: A dedicated line is not assigned to the help desk team.
options.C: Resolved incidents are closed without reference to end users.
options.D: The help desk instant messaging has been down for more than six months.

questions.correct_explanation: The help desk function is a service-oriented unit. The end users must be advised before an incident can be regarded as closed.

wrong_explanations.A: Although this is of concern, it should be expected. A problem escalation procedure should be developed to handle such scenarios.
wrong_explanations.B: Ideally, a help desk team should have dedicated lines, but this exception is not as serious as the technical team unilaterally closing an incident.
wrong_explanations.D: Instant messaging is an add-on to improve the effectiveness of the help desk team. Its absence cannot be seen as a major concern if calls can still be made.

tips: Trap is A 'unresolved calls' — escalation triggers exist for this; not necessarily a problem.
Trap is B 'no dedicated line' — communication channel issue, manageable.
Trap is D 'IM down 6 months' — operational tool gap, addressable.
Closing tickets without user confirmation = users don't know status of their issues. Trust in help desk erodes. Service-oriented function violates its core purpose.

questions.question: The MAIN purpose for periodically testing offsite disaster recovery facilities is to:

options.A: protect the integrity of the data in the database.
options.B: eliminate the need to develop detailed contingency plans.
options.C: ensure the continued compatibility of the contingency facilities.
options.D: ensure that program and system documentation remains current.

questions.correct_explanation: The main purpose of offsite hardware testing is to ensure the continued compatibility of the contingency facilities so that assurance can be gained that the contingency plans will work in an actual disaster.

wrong_explanations.A: The testing of an offsite facility does nothing to protect the integrity of the database. It may test the validity of backups but does not protect their integrity.
wrong_explanations.B: Testing an offsite location validates the value of the contingency plans and is not used to eliminate detailed plans.
wrong_explanations.D: Program and system documentation should be reviewed continuously to ensure that content is up-to-date. A test of an offsite facility may ensure that the documentation for that site is current, but this is not the purpose of testing an offsite facility.

tips: Trap is A 'protect data integrity' — testing doesn't directly protect data.
Trap is B 'eliminate need for plans' — testing doesn't eliminate planning.
Trap is D 'documentation current' — side effect of testing, not the main purpose.

Testing offsite facilities ensures they're STILL COMPATIBLE with current production environment. Hardware/software change over time; without testing, the contingency facility may not actually work when needed.

questions.question: A large chain of shops with electronic funds transfer at point-of-sale devices has a central communications processor for connecting to the banking network. Which of the following is the BEST disaster recovery plan (DRP) for the communications processor?

options.A: Offsite storage of daily backups
options.B: Alternative standby processor onsite
options.C: Installation of duplex communication links
options.D: Alternative standby processor at another network node

questions.correct_explanation: Having an alternative standby processor at another network node is the best solution. The unavailability of the central communications processor disrupts all access to the banking network, disrupting operations for all of the shops. This can be caused by failure of equipment, power or communications.

wrong_explanations.A: Off site storage of backups does not help, because electronic funds transfer tends to be an online process and offsite storage will not replace the dysfunctional processor.
wrong_explanations.B: The provision of an alternate processor onsite is fine for an equipment problem but does not help in the case of a power outage and may require technical expertise to cutover to the alternate equipment.
wrong_explanations.C: Installation of duplex communication links is most appropriate if only the communication link fails.

tips: Trap is A 'offsite daily backups' — protects data but doesn't restore EFT processing.
Trap is B 'standby onsite' — same site = same disaster impact.
Trap is C 'duplex communication links' — addresses link failure, not processor failure.
Standby processor at ANOTHER network node = geographically separate redundancy. Survives processor failure AND site disasters. Best comprehensive DRP solution for the central processor.

questions.question: The database administrator (DBA) suggests that database efficiency can be improved by denormalizing some tables. This will result in:

options.A: loss of confidentiality.
options.B: increased redundancy.
options.C: unauthorized accesses.
options.D: application malfunctions.

questions.correct_explanation: Normalization is a design or optimization process for a relational database that increases redundancy. Redundancy, which is usually considered positive for resource availability, is negative In a database environment because it demands additional and otherwise unnecessary data handling efforts. Denormalization is sometimes advisable for functional reasons.

wrong_explanations.A: Denormalization should not cause loss of confidentiality even though confidential data may be involved. The database administrator (DBA) should ensure that access controls to the databases remain effective.
wrong_explanations.C: Denormalization pertains to the structure of the database, not the access controls. It should not result in unauthorized access.
wrong_explanations.D: Denormalization may require some changes to the calls between databases and applications but should not cause application malfunctions.

tips: Trap is A 'loss of confidentiality' — confidentiality is access-control concern, not denormalization.
Trap is C 'unauthorized accesses' — unrelated to denormalization.
Trap is D 'application malfunctions' — denormalization is transparent to applications.
Denormalization stores the same data in multiple tables to speed reads. The cost: increased redundancy. Updates must propagate to all copies; storage grows.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor has been assigned to conduct a test that compares job run logs to computer job schedules. Which of the following observations would be the GREATEST concern to the IS auditor?

options.A: There are a growing number of emergency changes.
options.B: There were instances when some jobs were not completed on time.
options.C: There were instances when some jobs were overridden by computer operators.
options.D: Evidence shows that only scheduled jobs were run.

questions.correct_explanation: The overriding of computer processing jobs by computer operators can lead to unauthorized changes to data or programs. This is a control concern; thus, it is always critical.

wrong_explanations.A: Emergency changes are acceptable if they are properly documented as part of the process.
wrong_explanations.B: Instances of jobs not being completed on time are a potential issue and should be investigated, but it is not the greatest concern.
wrong_explanations.D: The audit should find that all scheduled jobs were run and that any exceptions were documented. This is not a violation.

tips: Trap is A 'emergency changes growing' — concerning but separate process issue.
Trap is B 'jobs not on time' — operational issue, addressable.
Trap is D 'only scheduled jobs ran' — that's the desired state, not a concern.
Operator overrides bypass scheduled controls — could change data or programs without authorization. Compromises integrity AND audit trail. Most serious operations finding.

questions.question: A new business requirement required changing database vendors. Which of the following areas should the information systems (IS) auditor PRIMARILY examine concerning this implementation?

options.A: Integrity of the data
options.B: Timing of the cutover
options.C: Authorization level of users
options.D: Normalization of the data

questions.correct_explanation: Critical issues when migrating data from one database to another is the integrity of the data and ensuring that the data are migrated completely and correctly.

wrong_explanations.B: The timing of the cutover is important, but because the data are being migrated to a new database, duplication should not be an issue.
wrong_explanations.C: The authorization of the users is not as relevant as the authorization of the application, because the users will interface with the database through an application and not directly interface with the database.
wrong_explanations.D: Normalization is used to design the database and is not necessarily related to database migration.

tips: Trap is B 'timing of cutover' — operational concern, addressable.
Trap is C 'authorization level of users' — access control concern, separate from migration.
Trap is D 'normalization of data' — design concern, addressable through schema work.
Database migration's PRIMARY risk: data integrity. If data is corrupted, lost, or transformed incorrectly during migration, business operations fail. Integrity verification is essential.

questions.question: The objective of concurrency control in a database system is to:

options.A: restrict updating of the database to authorized users.
options.B: ensure integrity when two processes attempt to update the same data simultaneously.
options.C: prevent inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of data in the database.
options.D: ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of data.

questions.correct_explanation: Concurrency controls prevent data integrity problems, which can arise when two update processes access the same data item simultaneously.

wrong_explanations.A: Access controls restrict updating of the database to authorized users.
wrong_explanations.C: Controls, such as passwords, prevent the inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of data from the database.
wrong_explanations.D: Quality controls, such as edits, ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of data maintained in the database.

tips: Trap is A 'restrict updating to authorized users' — that's access control, not concurrency.
Trap is C 'prevent unauthorized disclosure' — confidentiality control.
Trap is D 'accuracy/completeness/consistency' — broader integrity concept.

Concurrency control specifically handles SIMULTANEOUS updates. Without it, two transactions modifying the same data can corrupt each other (lost updates, dirty reads). Locks and timestamps maintain integrity.

questions.question: Which of the following controls provides the GREATEST assurance of database integrity?

options.A: Audit log procedures
options.B: Table link/reference checks
options.C: Query/table access time checks
options.D: Rollback and roll-forward database features

questions.correct_explanation: Performing table link/reference checks serves to detect table linking errors (such as completeness and accuracy of the contents of the database) and, thus, provides the greatest assurance of database integrity.

wrong_explanations.A: Audit log procedures enable recording of all events that have been identified and help in tracing the events. However, they only point to the event and do not ensure completeness or accuracy of the database contents.
wrong_explanations.C: Querying/monitoring table access time checks helps designers improve database performance but not integrity.
wrong_explanations.D: Rollback and roll-forward database features ensure recovery from an abnormal disruption. They ensure the integrity of the transaction that was being processed at the time of disruption, but do not provide assurance on the integrity of the contents of the database.

tips: Trap is A 'audit log procedures' — detective; logs activities but doesn't ensure integrity directly.
Trap is C 'query/access time checks' — performance concern, not integrity.
Trap is D 'rollback/roll-forward' — recovery feature, fixes problems after the fact.

Table link/reference checks verify referential integrity — relationships between tables remain consistent. Detects orphaned records, broken links, or invalid references. Direct integrity verification.

questions.question: Which of the following is widely accepted as one of the critical components in networking management?

options.A: Configuration and change management
options.B: Topological mappings
options.C: Application of monitoring tools
options.D: Proxy server troubleshooting

questions.correct_explanation: Configuration management is widely accepted as one of the key components of any network because it establishes how the network will function internally and externally. It also deals with the management of configuration and monitoring performance. Change management ensures that the setup and management of the network are done properly, including managing changes to the configuration, removing default passwords and possibly hardening the network by disabling unneeded services.

wrong_explanations.B: Topological mappings provide outlines of the components of the network and its connectivity. This is important to address issues such as single points of failure and proper network isolation, but it is not the most critical component of network management.
wrong_explanations.C: Application monitoring is not a critical part of network management.
wrong_explanations.D: Proxy server troubleshooting is used for troubleshooting purposes, and managing a proxy is only a small part of network management.

tips: Trap is B 'topological mappings' — documentation tool, not management.
Trap is C 'monitoring tools' — operational tool, not foundational management.
Trap is D 'proxy server troubleshooting' — narrow operational task.

Configuration + change management = the foundation of network management. Defines how the network is built (configuration) and how it changes safely (change management). Everything else operates within this framework.

questions.question: In evaluating programmed controls over password management, which of the following is the information systems (IS) auditor MOST likely to rely on?

options.A: Size check
options.B: Hash total
options.C: Validity check
options.D: Field check

questions.correct_explanation: A validity check is the most useful check for the verification of passwords because it verifies that the required format has been used-for example, not using a dictionary word and including nonalphabetical characters. An effective password must have several different types of characters: alphabetical, numeric and special.

wrong_explanations.A: A size check is useful because passwords should have a minimum length, but it is not as strong of a control as validity.
wrong_explanations.B: Passwords are not typically entered in a batch mode, so a hash total would not be effective. More important, a system should not accept incorrect values of a password, so a hash total as a control will not indicate any weak passwords, errors or omissions.
wrong_explanations.D: The implementation of a field check is not as effective as a validity check that verifies that all password criteria have been met.

tips: Trap is A 'size check' — verifies length within range, not format quality.
Trap is B 'hash total' — used for batch totals, not individual password format.
Trap is D 'field check' — generic data type check, less specific.
Validity check verifies password meets complexity rules (length, character mix, dictionary exclusion, etc.). Most relevant programmed control for password management.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the GREATEST risk created by a reciprocal agreement for disaster recovery between two organizations?

options.A: Developments may result in hardware and software incompatibility.
options.B: Resources may not be available when needed.
options.C: The recovery plan cannot be live tested.
options.D: The security infrastructures in each organization may be different.

questions.correct_explanation: If one organization updates its hardware and software configuration, it may mean it is no longer compatible with the other party's systems in the agreement. This may mean that each organization is unable to use the facilities at the other organization to recover their processing following a disaster.

wrong_explanations.B: Resources unavailable when needed are an intrinsic risk in any reciprocal agreement, but this is a contractual matter and not the greatest risk.
wrong_explanations.C: The plan can be tested by paper-based walk-throughs and possibly by agreement between the organizations.
wrong_explanations.D: The difference in security infrastructures, although a risk, is not insurmountable.

tips: Trap is B 'resources unavailable' — possible but addressable through capacity planning.
Trap is C 'cannot live test' — practical limitation, manageable.
Trap is D 'different security' — addressable through agreement terms.

Reciprocal agreements assume the partner's hardware/software match yours. Time passes, both organizations evolve, configurations diverge. The agreement gradually becomes useless without active maintenance — and rarely gets it.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST directly affected by network performance monitoring tools?

options.A: Integrity
options.B: Availability
options.C: Completeness
options.D: Confidentiality

questions.correct_explanation: Network monitoring tools allow observation of network performance and problems. This allows the administrator to take corrective action when network problems are observed. Therefore, the characteristic most directly affected by network monitoring is availability.

wrong_explanations.A: Network monitoring tools can be used to detect errors that are propagating through a network, but their primary focus is on network reliability so that the network is available when required.
wrong_explanations.C: Network monitoring tools do not measure completeness of the communication. This is measured by the end points in the communication.
wrong_explanations.D: A network monitoring tool can violate confidentiality by allowing a network administrator to observe nonencrypted traffic. This requires careful protection and policies regarding the use of network monitoring tools.

tips: Trap is A 'integrity' — network monitoring detects but doesn't ensure integrity.
Trap is C 'completeness' — measured at application level, not network.
Trap is D 'confidentiality' — encryption concern, not monitoring.
Network performance monitoring identifies bottlenecks, congestion, failures. Acting on monitoring data keeps the network AVAILABLE. Direct relationship: monitoring → availability.

questions.question: When auditing the onsite archiving process of emails, the information systems (IS) auditor should pay the MOST attention to which of the following?

options.A: Existence of a data retention policy
options.B: Storage capacity of the archiving solution
options.C: Level of user awareness concerning email use
options.D: Support and stability of the archiving solution manufacturer

questions.correct_explanation: Without a data retention policy that is aligned with the organization's business and compliance requirements, the email archive may not preserve and reproduce the correct information when required.

wrong_explanations.B: The storage capacity of the archiving solution is irrelevant if the proper email messages have not been properly preserved and others have been deleted.
wrong_explanations.C: The level of user awareness concerning email use does not directly affect the completeness and accuracy of the archived email.
wrong_explanations.D: The support and stability of the archiving solution manufacturer is secondary to the need to ensure a retention policy. Vendor support does not directly affect the completeness and accuracy of the archived email.

tips: Trap is B 'storage capacity' — operational concern, manageable.
Trap is C 'user awareness' — process concern, separate.
Trap is D 'manufacturer support' — vendor concern.

Email retention policy aligned with business AND regulatory requirements is foundational. Without it, the archive may keep too much (storage cost, privacy risk) or too little (legal exposure). Policy drives everything.

questions.question: Vendors have released patches fixing security flaws in their software. Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor recommend in this situation?

options.A: Assess the impact of patches prior to installation.
options.B: Ask the vendors for a new software version with all fixes included.
options.C: Install the security patch immediately.
options.D: Decline to deal with these vendors in the future.

questions.correct_explanation: The effect of installing the patch should be immediately evaluated, and installation should occur based on the results of the evaluation. There are numerous cases where a patch from one vendor has affected other systems; therefore, testing the patches as much as possible before rolling them out to the entire organization is necessary.

wrong_explanations.B: New software versions with all fixes included are not always available, and a full installation can be time consuming.
wrong_explanations.C: To install the patch without knowing what it might affect can easily cause problems. The installation of a patch may also affect system availability; therefore, the patch should be rolled out at a time that is acceptable to the business.
wrong_explanations.D: Declining to deal with vendors does not take care of the flaw and may severely limit service options.

tips: Trap is B 'new software version with all fixes' — vendor controls release timing; can't demand on-demand.
Trap is C 'install immediately' — risky; patches can break things.
Trap is D 'decline to deal with vendors' — overreaction; all software has vulnerabilities.
Patch impact assessment first: does this patch affect us? Will it break anything in our environment? Risk-based decision drives whether and when to install.

questions.question: Which of the following controls is MOST effective in ensuring that production source code and object code are synchronized?

options.A: Release-to-release source and object comparison reports
options.B: Library control software restricting changes to source code
options.C: Restricted access to source code and object code
options.D: Date and time-stamp reviews of source and object code

questions.correct_explanation: Date and time-stamp reviews of source and object code ensures that the source code, which has been compiled, matches the production object code. This is the most effective way to ensure that the approved production source code is compiled and is the one being used.

wrong_explanations.A: Using version control software and comparing source and object code is a good practice but may not detect a problem where the source code is a different version than the object code.
wrong_explanations.B: All production libraries should be protected with access controls, and this may protect source code from tampering. However, this will not ensure that source and object codes are based on the same version.
wrong_explanations.C: Protecting all source and object code-even in development-s a good practice. However, this will not ensure the synchronization of source and object code.

tips: Trap is A 'release-to-release reports' — useful but specific to release events.
Trap is B 'library control software' — controls changes but doesn't verify synchronization.
Trap is C 'restricted access' — preventive but doesn't verify match.
Date/time-stamp comparison directly verifies that source and object code came from the same compilation. Most direct synchronization check.

questions.question: A database administrator (DBA) who needs to make emergency changes to a database after normal working hours should log in:

options.A: with their named account to make the changes.
options.B: with the shared DBA account to make the changes.
options.C: to the server administrative account to make the changes.
options.D: to the user's account to make the changes.

questions.correct_explanation: Logging in using the named user account before using the database administrator (DBA) account provides accountability by noting the person making the changes.

wrong_explanations.B: The DBA account is typically a shared user account. The shared account makes it difficult to establish the identity of the support user who is performing the database update.
wrong_explanations.C: The server administrative accounts are shared and may be used by multiple support users. In addition, the server privilege accounts may not have the ability to perform database changes.
wrong_explanations.D: The use of a normal user account does not have sufficient privileges to make changes on the database.

tips: Trap is B 'shared DBA account' — no individual accountability.
Trap is C 'server administrative account' — different role; SoD concern and no DB-specific accountability.
Trap is D 'user account' — insufficient privileges for emergency DB changes.
Named account = individual accountability. Even for emergency changes, the audit trail must identify WHO made each change. Shared accounts make accountability impossible.

questions.question: During an assessment of software development practices, an information systems (IS) auditor finds that open-source software components were used in an application designed for a client. What is the GREATEST concern that the auditor has about the use of open-source software?

options.A: The client did not pay for the open-source software components.
