options.B: The organization and client must comply with open-source software license terms.
options.C: Open-source software has security vulnerabilities.
options.D: Open-source software is unreliable for commercial use.

questions.correct_explanation: There are many types of open-source software licenses and each has different terms and conditions. Some open-source software licensing allows use of the open-source software component freely but requires that the completed software product must also allow the same rights. This is known as viral licensing, and if the development organization is not careful, its products can violate licensing terms by selling the product for profit. The information systems (IS) auditor should be most concerned with open-source software licensing compliance to avoid unintended intellectual property risk or legal consequences.

wrong_explanations.A: A major benefit of using open-source software is that it is free. The client is not required to pay for the open-source software components; however, both the developing organization and the client should be concerned about the licensing terms and conditions of the open source software components that are being used.
wrong_explanations.C: Open-source software, just like any software code, should be tested for security flaws and should be part of the normal system development life cycle (SDLC) process. This is not more of a concern than licensing compliance.
wrong_explanations.D: Open-source software does not inherently lack quality. Like any software code, it should be tested for reliability and should be part of the normal SDLC process. This is not more of a concern than licensing compliance.

tips: Trap is A 'client did not pay' — open-source is free; non-issue.
Trap is C 'security vulnerabilities' — true but applies to all software.
Trap is D 'unreliable for commercial use' — overstated; many enterprise systems use open-source successfully.

Open-source licenses (GPL, MIT, BSD, Apache, AGPL, etc.) have very different requirements. Some require sharing modifications; some restrict commercial use; some require attribution. License compliance is a real legal risk.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing database controls discovered that changes to the database during normal working hours were handled through a standard set of procedures. However, changes made after normal hours required only an abbreviated number of steps. In this situation, which of the following is considered an adequate set of compensating controls?

options.A: Allow changes to be made only with the database administrator (DBA) user account.
options.B: Make changes to the database after granting access to a normal user account.
options.C: Use the DBA user account to make changes, log the changes and review the change log the following day.
options.D: Use the normal user account to make changes, log the changes and review the change log the following day.

questions.correct_explanation: The use of a DBA user account is normally set up to log all changes made and is most appropriate for changes made outside of normal hours. The use of a log, which records the changes, allows· changes to be reviewed. Because an abbreviated number of steps are used, this represents an adequate set of compensating controls.

wrong_explanations.A: The use of the database administrator (DBA) user account without logging pennits uncontrolled changes to be made to databases after access to the account was obtained.
wrong_explanations.B: A normal user account should not have access to a database. This pennits uncontrolled changes to any of the databases.
wrong_explanations.D: Users should not be able to make changes. Logging only provides information on changes made but does not limit changes to only those who were authorized.

tips: Trap is A 'DBA account only' — doesn't address the after-hours abbreviated process.
Trap is B 'normal user account changes' — normal users shouldn't make DB changes.
Trap is D 'normal user account + log' — see above; user shouldn't be making DB changes.
After-hours DBA access + log + next-day review = compensating controls preserve emergency capability while maintaining audit trail. Logged DBA changes get reviewed for appropriateness.

questions.question: Which of the following tests performed by an information systems (IS) auditor is the MOST effective in determining compliance with organizational change control procedures?

options.A: Review software migration records and verify approvals.
options.B: Identify changes that have occurred and verify approvals.
options.C: Review change control documentation and verify approvals.
options.D: Ensure that only appropriate staff can migrate changes into production.

questions.correct_explanation: The most effective method is to determine what changes have been made (check logs and modified dates) and then verify that they have been approved.

wrong_explanations.A: Software migration records may not have all changes listed-changes could have been made that were not included in the migration records.
wrong_explanations.C: Change control records may not have all changes listed.
wrong_explanations.D: Ensuring that only appropriate staff can migrate changes into production is a key control process but, alone, does not verify compliance.

tips: Trap is A 'review software migration records' — depends on recordkeeping; could miss changes never recorded.
Trap is C 'review change control documentation' — paper review; doesn't verify actual changes.
Trap is D 'restrict migration access' — preventive control, not a compliance test.
Identifying actual changes from system data, then verifying each had approval = the substance of compliance testing. Catches both unauthorized changes AND changes that bypassed paperwork.

questions.question: When an organization's disaster recovery plan (DRP) has a reciprocal agreement, which of the following risk treatment approaches is being applied?

options.A: Transfer
options.B: Mitigation
options.C: Avoidance
options.D: Acceptance

questions.correct_explanation: A reciprocal agreement in which two organizations agree to provide computing resources to each other in the event of a disaster is a form of risk mitigation. This usually works well if both organizations have similar information processing facilities. Because the intended effect of reciprocal agreements is to have a functional disaster recovery plan (DRP), it is a risk mitigation strategy.

wrong_explanations.A: Risk transfer is the transference of risk to a third party (e.g., buying insurance for activities that pose a risk).
wrong_explanations.C: Risk avoidance is the decision to cease operations or activities that give rise to a risk. For example, an organization may stop accepting credit card payments to avoid the risk of credit card information disclosure.
wrong_explanations.D: Risk acceptance occurs when an organization decides to accept the risk as it is and to do nothing to mitigate or transfer it.

tips: Trap is A 'transfer' — would be insurance or full outsourcing of recovery; not a reciprocal pact.
Trap is C 'avoidance' — would mean discontinuing the activity; opposite of contingency planning.
Trap is D 'acceptance' — would mean no controls; reciprocal IS a control.
Reciprocal agreement = each org provides recovery capacity for the other. That's risk MITIGATION (reducing impact), not transfer (paying someone else's premium) or other treatment.

questions.question: A programmer maliciously modified a production program to change data and then restored the program back to the original code. Which of the following would MOST effectively detect the malicious activity?

options.A: Comparing source code
options.B: Reviewing system log files
options.C: Comparing object code
options.D: Reviewing executable and source code integrity

questions.correct_explanation: Reviewing system log files is the only trail that may provide information about unauthorized activities in the production library.

wrong_explanations.A: Source code comparisons are ineffective because the original programs were restored, and the changed program does not exist.
wrong_explanations.C: Object code comparisons are ineffective because the original programs were restored, and the changed program does not exist.
wrong_explanations.D: Reviewing executable and source code integrity is an ineffective control, because the source code was changed back to the original and will agree with the current executable.

tips: Trap is A 'comparing source code' — won't detect; the source was restored.
Trap is C 'comparing object code' — same; restoration covers tracks.
Trap is D 'reviewing executable/source integrity' — restored integrity matches original.
System logs capture ACTIVITY in real time — the modification, the data change, the restoration. Even when code is restored, the activity record persists as the trail.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing an organization's recovery from a disaster in which not all the critical data needed to resume business operations were retained. Which of the following was incorrectly defined?

options.A: Interruption window
options.B: Recovery time objective
options.C: Service delivery objective
options.D: Recovery point objective

questions.correct_explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) is determined based on the acceptable data loss in the case of a disruption of operations. RPO defines the point in time from which it is necessary to recover the data and quantifies, in terms of time, the permissible amount of data loss in the case of interruption.

wrong_explanations.A: The interruption window is defined as the amount of time during which the organization is unable to maintain operations from the point of failure to the time that the critical services/applications are restored.
wrong_explanations.B: The recovery time objective is determined based on the acceptable downtime in the case of a disruption of operations.
wrong_explanations.C: The service delivery objective (SDO) is directly related to the business needs. SDO is the level of services to be reached during the alternate process mode until the normal situation is restored.

tips: Trap is A 'interruption window' — duration of operations gap, not data loss.
Trap is B 'RTO' — time to recovery, not data preservation.
Trap is C 'SDO' — service level during recovery, not data preservation.
RPO defines acceptable data loss in time. If critical data wasn't retained, the RPO was set wrong (too lax) or controls didn't enforce it. Direct connection to data preservation.

questions.question: The PRIMARY benefit of an IT manager monitoring technical capacity is to:

options.A: identify the need for new hardware and storage procurement.
options.B: determine the future capacity need based on usage.
options.C: ensure that the service level requirements are met.
options.D: ensure that systems operate at optimal capacity.

questions.correct_explanation: Capacity monitoring has multiple objectives; however, the primary objective is to ensure compliance with the internal service level agreement between the business and IT.

wrong_explanations.A: This is one benefit of monitoring technical capacity because it can help forecast future demands, not just react to system failures. However, the primary responsibility of the IT manager is to meet the overall requirement to ensure that IT is meeting the service level expectations of the business.
wrong_explanations.B: Determining future capacity is one definite benefit of technical capability monitoring.
wrong_explanations.D: IT management is interested in ensuring that systems are operating at optimal capacity, but their primary obligation is to ensure that IT is meeting the service level requirements of the business.

tips: Trap is A 'identify hardware needs' — outcome of monitoring, not primary purpose.
Trap is B 'determine future capacity' — also outcome.
Trap is D 'optimal capacity operation' — efficiency goal, secondary to SLA compliance.
Capacity monitoring's PRIMARY purpose: ensure SLA compliance with the business. The business contracted for performance; IT's job is to deliver what was promised.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing an organization's disaster recovery plan (DRP) should PRIMARILY verify that it is:

options.A: tested every six months.
options.B: regularly reviewed and updated.
options.C: approved by the chief executive officer.
options.D: communicated to every department head in the organization.

questions.correct_explanation: The plan should be reviewed at appropriate intervals, depending on the nature of the business and the rate of change of systems and personnel. Otherwise, it may become out-of-date and may no longer be effective.

wrong_explanations.A: The plan must be subjected to regular testing, but the period between tests depends on the nature of the organization, the amount of change in the organization and the relative importance of information systems (IS). Three months, or even annually, may be appropriate in different circumstances.
wrong_explanations.C: Although the disaster recovery plan (DRP) should receive the approval of senior management, it need not be the chief executive officer if another executive officer is equally or more appropriate. For a purely IS-related plan, the executive responsible for technology may approve the plan.
wrong_explanations.D: Although a business continuity plan (BCP) is likely to be circulated throughout an organization, the IS DRP will usually be a technical document and only relevant to IS and communication staff.

tips: Trap is A 'tested every six months' — frequency varies by business needs.
Trap is C 'approved by CEO' — usually approved by CIO or steering committee.
Trap is D 'communicated to every department head' — communication is necessary but not the primary auditor verification.
DRP must remain CURRENT to be effective. Systems change, people change, processes change. An out-of-date DRP is worse than no DRP — false confidence. Regular review and update is foundational.

questions.question: There are several methods of providing telecommunication continuity. The method of routing traffic through split-cable or duplicate-cable facilities is called:

options.A: alternative routing.
options.B: diverse routing.
options.C: long-haul network diversity.
options.D: last-mile circuit protection.

questions.correct_explanation: Diverse routing routes traffic through split-cable facilities or duplicate-cable facilities. This can be accomplished with different and/or duplicate cable sheaths. If different cable sheaths are used, the cable may be in the same conduit and, therefore, subject to the same interruptions as the cable it is backing up. The communication service subscriber can duplicate the facilities by having alternate routes, although the entrance to and from the customer premises may be in the same conduit. The subscriber can obtain diverse routing and alternate routing from the local carrier, including dual-entrance facilities. This type of access is time-consuming and costly.

wrong_explanations.A: Alternative routing is a method of routing information via an alternate medium, such as copper cable or fiber optics. This involves the use of different networks, circuits or end points if the normal network is unavailable.
wrong_explanations.C: Long-haul network diversity is a diverse, long-distance network using different packet switching circuits among the major long-distance carriers. It ensures long-distance access if any carrier experiences a network failure.
wrong_explanations.D: Last-mile circuit protection is a redundant combination oflocal carrier T-ls (E-ls in Europe), microwave and/or coaxial cable access to the local communications loop. This enables the facility to have access during a local carrier communication disaster. Alternate local-carrier routing is also used.

tips: Trap is A 'alternative routing' — different ROUTES, not split/duplicate cables.
Trap is C 'long-haul network diversity' — long-distance carrier diversity.
Trap is D 'last-mile circuit protection' — specifically the local loop.
Diverse routing = same data on physically different cables. If one cable is cut, the other carries traffic. Specifically split/duplicate cable terminology.

questions.question: Recovery procedures for an information processing facility (IPF) are BEST based on:

options.A: recovery time objective (RTO)
options.B: recovery point objective (RPO)
options.C: maximum tolerable outage (MTO)
options.D: information security policy.

questions.correct_explanation: The recovery time objective (RTO) is the amount of time allowed for the recovery of a business function or resource after a disaster occurs; the RTO is the desired recovery time frame based on maximum tolerable outage (MTO) and available recovery alternatives.

wrong_explanations.B: The recovery point objective (RPO) has the greatest influence on the recovery strategies for given data. It is determined based on the acceptable data loss in case of a disruption of operations. The RPO effectively quantifies the permissible amount of data loss in case of interruption.
wrong_explanations.C: MTO is the amount of time allowed for the recovery of a business function or resource after a disaster occurs; it represents the time by which the service must be restored before the organization is faced with the threat of collapse.
wrong_explanations.D: An information security policy does not address recovery procedures.

tips: Trap is B 'RPO' — informs backup frequency, not recovery procedures.
Trap is C 'MTO' — maximum time before unrecoverable; informs RTO.
Trap is D 'security policy' — too broad; doesn't drive recovery procedures.
RTO (recovery time objective) directly drives recovery procedures: how fast must this be back? Determines hot/warm/cold site choice, backup strategy, staffing, etc. Procedure design follows RTO.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is performing an audit in the data center when the fire alarm begins sounding. The audit scope includes disaster recovery, so the auditor observes the data center staff respond to the alarm. Which of the following is the MOST important action for the data center staff to complete in this scenario?

options.A: Notify the local fire department of the alarm condition.
options.B: Prepare to activate the fire suppression system.
options.C: Ensure all persons in the data center are evacuated.
options.D: Remove all backups from the data center.

questions.correct_explanation: In an emergency, safety of life is always the first priority; therefore, the complete and orderly evacuation of the facility staff is the most important activity.

wrong_explanations.A: Life safety is always the first priority, and notifying the fire department of the alarm is not typically necessary because most data center alarms are configured to automatically report to the local authorities.
wrong_explanations.B: Fire suppression systems are designed to operate automatically, and activating the system when staff are not yet evacuated can create confusion and panic, leading to injuries or even fatalities. Manual triggering of the system can be necessary under certain conditions, but only after all other data center personnel are safely evacuated.
wrong_explanations.D: Removal of backups from the data center is not an appropriate action because it can delay the evacuation of personnel. Most organizations have copies of backups in off site storage to mitigate the risk of data loss for this type of disaster.

tips: Trap is A 'notify fire department' — alarms typically auto-notify; secondary to evacuation.
Trap is B 'activate fire suppression' — automatic systems; manual activation comes after evacuation.
Trap is D 'remove backups' — backups can be replaced; people cannot. Backups are stored offsite anyway.
Life safety FIRST. Always. In any emergency, evacuation of personnel takes absolute priority over equipment, data, or property. Foundational principle.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor discovers that the disaster recovery plan (DRP) for an organization does not include a critical application hosted in the cloud. Management response states that the cloud vendor is responsible for disaster recovery (DR) and DR-related testing. What is the NEXT course of action for the IS auditor to pursue?

options.A: Plan an audit of the cloud vendor.
options.B: Review the vendor contract to determine its DR capabilities.
options.C: Review an independent auditor's report of the cloud vendor.
options.D: Request a copy of the DRP from the cloud vendor.

questions.correct_explanation: DR services can only be expected from the vendor when explicitly listed in the contract with well­defined recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives. Without the contractual language, the vendor is not required to provide DR services.

wrong_explanations.A: Auditing the cloud vendor is useful; however, this is only useful if the vendor is contractually required to provide disaster recovery (DR) services.
wrong_explanations.C: An independent auditor's report, such as Statements on Standards for Attestation Engagements 16, on DR capabilities can be reviewed to ascertain the vendor's DR capabilities; however, this is only fruitful if the vendor is contractually required to provide DR services.
wrong_explanations.D: A copy of DR policies can be requested to review their adequacy; however, this will only be useful if the vendor is contractually required to provide DR services.

tips: Trap is A 'plan an audit of cloud vendor' — premature; first verify the contractual basis.
Trap is C 'review independent auditor report' — also premature; depends on contractual rights.
Trap is D 'request DRP from vendor' — vendor isn't obligated to share without contract terms.
Vendor responsibility for DR exists ONLY IF the contract specifies it. Without contractual DR commitment, the customer remains accountable. Verify contract language first.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is performing a review of the disaster recovery hot site used by a financial institution. Which of the following is the GREATEST concern?

options.A: System administrators use shared accounts which never expire at the hot site.
options.B: Disk space utilization data are not kept current.
options.C: Physical security controls at the hot site are less robust than at the main site.
options.D: Servers at the hot site do not have the same specifications as at the main site.

questions.correct_explanation: Not knowing how much disk space is in use and, therefore, how much is needed at the disaster recovery site can create major issues in the case of a disaster.

wrong_explanations.A: Although it is not a good practice for security administrators to share accounts that do not expire, the greater risk in this scenario is running out of disk space.
wrong_explanations.C: Physical security controls are important, and this is a concern, but the more important concern is running out of disk space. The physical characteristics of the disaster recovery site may call for different controls that may appear to be less robust than the main site; however, such a risk can be addressed through policy and procedures or by adding additional personnel if needed.
wrong_explanations.D: If the servers at the hot site are capable of running the programs that are required in a disaster recovery situation, the precise capabilities of the servers at the hot site is not a major risk. It is necessary to ensure that software configuration and settings match the servers at the main site, but it is not unusual for newer and more powerful servers to exist at the main site for everyday production use while the standby servers are less powerful.

tips: Trap is A 'shared accounts at hot site' — security concern but recoverable.
Trap is C 'physical security less robust' — concerning but compensating controls exist.
Trap is D 'specifications differ' — manageable through testing.
Disk space data not current = at recovery time, may not have enough storage to run. System fails to start, recovery is delayed or impossible. Hidden capacity gap.

questions.question: When reviewing system parameters, an information systems (IS) auditor's PRIMARY concern should be that:

options.A: they are set to meet both security and performance requirements.
options.B: changes are recorded in an audit trail and periodically reviewed.
options.C: changes are authorized and supported by appropriate documents.
options.D: access to parameters in the system is restricted.

questions.correct_explanation: The primary concern is to find the balance between security and performance. Recording changes in an audit trail and periodically reviewing them is a detective control; however, if parameters are not set according to business rules, monitoring of changes may not be an effective control.

wrong_explanations.B: Reviewing changes to ensure that they are supported by appropriate documents is also a detective control.
wrong_explanations.C: If parameters are set incorrectly, the related documentation and the fact that these are authorized does not reduce the impact.
wrong_explanations.D: Restriction of access to parameters ensures that only authorized staff can access the parameters; however, if the parameters are set incorrectly, restricting access will still have an adverse impact.

tips: Trap is B 'audit trail of changes' — detective control, important but not the primary review concern.
Trap is C 'authorized and documented' — process control, also detective.
Trap is D 'restricted access' — preventive control.
System parameters balance security AND performance. Too tight = performance degrades; too loose = security risk. The PRIMARY parameter review concern is whether the balance is appropriate.

questions.question: An offsite information processing facility (IPF) with electrical wiring, air conditioning and flooring, but no computer or communications equipment, is a:

options.A: cold site.
options.B: warm site.
options.C: dial-up site.
options.D: duplicate processing facility.

questions.correct_explanation: A cold site is ready to receive equipment but does not offer any components at the site in advance of the need.

wrong_explanations.B: A warm site is an offsite backup facility that is partially configured with network connections and selected peripheral equipment-such as disk units, controllers and central processing units-to operate an information processing facility (IPF).
wrong_explanations.C: A dial-up site is used for remote access, but not for offsite information processing.
wrong_explanations.D: A duplicate IPF is a dedicated, fully developed recovery site that can back up critical applications.

tips: Trap is B 'warm site' — has equipment but not fully operational.
Trap is C 'dial-up site' — connectivity, not facility.
Trap is D 'duplicate processing facility' — fully operational mirror.
Cold site = empty space ready to receive equipment. No computers, no comms, just utilities and physical infrastructure. Cheapest, slowest activation.

questions.question: An optimized disaster recovery plan (DRP) for an organization should:

options.A: reduce the length of the recovery time and the cost of recovery.
options.B: increase the length of the recovery time and the cost of recovery.
options.C: reduce the duration of the recovery time and increase the cost of recovery.
options.D: not affect the recovery time or the cost of recovery.

questions.correct_explanation: One of the objectives of a disaster recovery plan (DRP) is to reduce the duration and cost of recovering from a disaster.

wrong_explanations.B: A DRP increases the cost of operations before and after the disaster occurs.
wrong_explanations.C: A DRP should reduce the time to return to normal operations.
wrong_explanations.D: A DRP should reduce the cost that could result from a disaster.

tips: Trap is B 'increase recovery time AND cost' — opposite of optimization.
Trap is C 'reduce time but increase cost' — partial; both should reduce.
Trap is D 'no effect' — defeats the purpose of optimization.
An optimized DRP balances and REDUCES both recovery time and recovery cost through careful planning. Pre-positioning resources, contracted facilities, tested procedures all save time AND money.

questions.question: A disaster recovery plan (DRP) for an organization's financial system specifies that the recovery point objective (RPO) is zero and the recovery time objective (RTO) is 72 hours. Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective solution?

options.A: A hot site that can be operational in eight hours with asynchronous backup of the transaction logs
options.B: Distributed database systems in multiple locations updated asynchronously.
options.C: Synchronous updates of the data and standby active systems in a hot site
options.D: Synchronous remote copy of the data in a warm site that can be operational in 48 hours

questions.correct_explanation: The synchronous copy of the data storage achieves the RPO, and a warm site operational in 48 hours meets the required RTO.

wrong_explanations.A: A hot site meets the recovery time objective (RTO) but incurs higher costs than necessary.
wrong_explanations.B: Asynchronous updates of the database in distributed locations do not meet the recovery point objective (RPO).
wrong_explanations.C: Synchronous updates of the data and standby active systems in a hot site meet the RPO and RTO requirements but are costlier than a warm site solution.

tips: Trap is A 'hot site 8 hours, async backup' — async fails RPO=zero; some data loss.
Trap is B 'distributed databases async' — async = data loss.
Trap is C 'synchronous + standby active hot site' — meets RPO/RTO but expensive.
RPO=0 requires synchronous data copy (no loss). RTO=72 hrs allows warm site (cheaper than hot). Synchronous data + warm site = cost-effective combo meeting both requirements.

questions.question: A financial institution that processes millions of transactions each day has a central communications processor (switch) for connecting to automated teller machines. Which of the following is the BEST contingency planfor the communications processor?

options.A: Reciprocal agreement with another organization
options.B: Alternate processor in the same location
options.C: Alternate processor at another network node
options.D: Duplex communication links

questions.correct_explanation: The unavailability of the central communications processor disrupts all access to the banking network. This can be caused by an equipment, power or communications failure. Having a duplicate processor in another location that can be used for alternate processing is the best solution.

wrong_explanations.A: Reciprocal agreements make an organization dependent on the other organization and raise privacy, competition and regulatory issues.
wrong_explanations.B: Having an alternate processor in the same location resolves the equipment problem but is not effective if the failure is caused by environmental conditions (e.g., power disruption).
wrong_explanations.D: The installation of duplex communication links is only appropriate if the failure is limited to the communication link.

tips: Trap is A 'reciprocal agreement' — depends on partner availability; high risk for critical processor.
Trap is B 'alternate processor in same location' — same site = same disaster impact.
Trap is D 'duplex communication links' — addresses link failure, not processor failure.
Alternate processor at another network node = geographic and equipment redundancy. Best contingency for critical communications processor.

questions.question: Which of the following provides the BEST evidence of an organization's disaster recovery capability readiness?

options.A: Disaster recovery plan (DRP)
options.B: Customer references for the alternate site provider
options.C: Processes for maintaining the DRP
options.D: Results of tests and exercises

questions.correct_explanation: Only tests and exercises demonstrate the adequacy of the plans and provide reasonable assurance of an organization's disaster recovery capability readiness.

wrong_explanations.A: Having a plan is important, but a plan cannot be considered effective until it has been tested.
wrong_explanations.B: Customer references may aid in choosing an alternate site provider but will not ensure the effectiveness of the plan.
wrong_explanations.C: A disaster recovery plan must be kept up-to-date through a regular maintenance and review schedule, but this is not as important as testing.

tips: Trap is A 'DRP exists' — having a plan ≠ readiness.
Trap is B 'customer references' — third-party endorsement, not direct evidence.
Trap is C 'maintenance processes' — process exists ≠ effective recovery.
Test results = real evidence. Did the DRP actually work? What problems surfaced? Tests are the only objective measure of recovery readiness.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds that database administrators (DBAs) have access to the log location on the database server and the ability to purge logs from the system. What is the BEST audit recommendation to ensure that DBA activity is effectively monitored?

options.A: Change permissions to prevent DBAs from purging logs.
options.B: Forward database logs to a centralized log server to which the DBAs do not have access.
options.C: Require that critical changes to the database are formally approved.
options.D: Back up database logs to magnetic media.

questions.correct_explanation: To protect the availability and integrity of the database logs, it is most feasible to forward the database logs to a centralized log server to which the DBAs do not have access.

wrong_explanations.A: Changing the database administrator (DBA) permissions to prevent DBAs from purging logs may not be feasible and does not adequately protect the availability and integrity of the database logs.
wrong_explanations.C: Requiring that critical changes to the database are formally approved does not adequately protect the availability and integrity of the database logs.
wrong_explanations.D: Backing up database logs to magnetic media does not adequately protect the availability and integrity of the database logs.

tips: Trap is A 'remove DBA permissions' — DBAs need access for legitimate work.
Trap is C 'critical changes formally approved' — process control, doesn't address log integrity.
Trap is D 'backup logs to magnetic media' — preserves logs but DBA could compromise media.
Centralized log server with restricted access enforces log integrity. DBAs can do their job; their activity is recorded somewhere they can't tamper. SoD-compliant monitoring.

questions.question: While performing a review of a critical third-party application, an information systems (IS) auditor is MOST concerned with discovering:

options.A: inadequate procedures for ensuring adequate system portability.
options.B: inadequate operational documentation for the system.
options.C: an inadequate alternate service provider listing.
options.D: an inadequate software escrow agreement.

questions.correct_explanation: The inclusion of a clause in the agreement that requires software code to be placed in escrow helps to ensure that the customer can continue to use the software and/or obtain technical support if a vendor goes out of business.

wrong_explanations.A: Procedures to ensure that systems are developed so that they can be ported to other system platforms help ensure that the system can continue functioning without affecting the business process if changes to the infrastructure occur. This is less important than the availability of the software.
wrong_explanations.B: Inadequate operational documentation is a risk but is less significant than the risk of unavailability of the software.
wrong_explanations.C: Although alternate service providers can be used if a vendor goes out of business, having access to the source code via a software escrow agreement is more important.

tips: Trap is A 'system portability' — concern but specific to migration scenarios.
Trap is B 'operational documentation' — addressable through documentation requests.
Trap is C 'alternate service provider list' — operational concern.

For critical third-party apps, software escrow protects the customer if the vendor fails. Without escrow, vendor failure could permanently end software availability. Existential risk for the customer.

questions.question: Which of the following activities should the business continuity manager perform FIRST after the replacement of hardware at the primary information processing facility (IPF)?

options.A: Verify compatibility with the hot site.
options.B: Review the implementation report .
options.C: Perform a walk-through of the disaster recovery plan (DRP).
options.D: Update the IT assets inventory .

questions.correct_explanation: An IT assets inventory is the basic input for the BCP/disaster recovery plan (DRP), and the plan must be updated to reflect changes in the IT infrastructure.

wrong_explanations.A: Before validating that the new hardware is compatible with the recovery site, the business continuity manager should update the listing of all equipment and IT assets included in the business continuity plan (BCP).
wrong_explanations.B: The implementation report is of limited value to the business continuity manager because the equipment has been installed.
wrong_explanations.C: The walk-through of the plan should only be done after the asset inventory has been updated.

tips: Trap is A 'verify hot site compatibility' — important but follows inventory update.
Trap is B 'review implementation report' — operational, narrow.
Trap is C 'walk-through DRP' — testing activity, follows inventory update.
DRP relies on accurate IT asset inventory. Hardware replacement changes the inventory. Update first; everything downstream depends on accurate inventory.

questions.question: Which of the following would an information systems (IS) auditor consider to be the MOST important to review when conducting a disaster recovery audit?

options.A: A hot site is contracted for and available as needed.
options.B: A business continuity manual is available and current.
options.C: Insurance coverage is adequate and premiums are current.
options.D: Data backups are performed timely and stored offsite.

questions.correct_explanation: Without data to process, all other components of the recovery effort are of no value. Even in the absence of a plan, recovery efforts of any type would not be practical without data to process.

wrong_explanations.A: A hot site is important, but it is of no use if there are no data backups for it.
wrong_explanations.B: A business continuity manual is advisable but not most important in a disaster recovery audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Insurance coverage should be adequate to cover costs but is not as important as having the data backup.

tips: Trap is A 'hot site contracted' — facility availability without data is useless.
Trap is B 'BCP manual current' — documentation without data is useless.
Trap is C 'insurance adequate' — financial protection without data is useless.
Data backups are FOUNDATIONAL. Without data, no recovery is possible regardless of plans, sites, or insurance. Most critical disaster recovery audit subject.

questions.question: Which of the following should the information systems (IS) auditor review to ensure that servers are optimally configured to support processing requirements?

options.A: Benchmark test results
options.B: Server logs
options.C: Downtime reports
options.D: Server utilization data

questions.correct_explanation: Monitoring server utilization identifies underused servers and monitors overall server utilization. Underused servers do not provide the business with optimal cost-effectiveness. By monitoring server usage, IT management can take appropriate measures to raise the utilization ratio and provide the most effective return on investment.

wrong_explanations.A: Benchmark tests are designed to compare system performance using standardized criteria; however, benchmark testing does not provide the best data to ensure the optimal configuration of servers in an organization.
wrong_explanations.B: A server log contains data showing activities performed on the server but does not contain the utilization data required to ensure the optimal configuration of servers.
wrong_explanations.C: A downtime report identifies the elapsed time when a computer is not operating correctly because of machine failure but is not useful in determining optimal server configurations.

tips: Trap is A 'benchmark test results' — comparison data, not utilization.
Trap is B 'server logs' — too detailed; need utilization summary.
Trap is C 'downtime reports' — availability, not capacity.
Server utilization data shows actual capacity use. Underutilized = wasted resources; overutilized = performance risk. Right-sizing decisions flow from utilization data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a continuity plan test that simulates a system crash and uses actual resources to cost-effectively obtain evidence about the plan's effectiveness?

options.A: Paper test
options.B: Post-test
options.C: Preparedness test
options.D: Walk-through

questions.correct_explanation: A preparedness test is a localized version of a full test, wherein resources are expended in the simulation of a system crash. This test is performed regularly on different aspects of the plan and can be a cost-effective way to gradually obtain evidence about the plan's effectiveness. It also provides a means to improve the plan in increments.

wrong_explanations.A: A paper test is a walk-through of the plan, involving major players who attempt to determine what might happen in a particular type of service disruption in the plan's execution. A paper test usually precedes the preparedness test.
wrong_explanations.B: A post-test is actually a test phase and is comprised of a group of activities, such as returning all resources to their proper place, disconnecting equipment, returning personnel and deleting all organization data from third-party systems.
wrong_explanations.D: A walk-through is a test involving a simulated disaster situation that tests the preparedness and understanding of management and staff rather than the actual resources.

tips: Trap is A 'paper test' — discusses plan, doesn't simulate.
Trap is B 'post-test' — that's an after-test review, not a test type.
Trap is D 'walk-through' — discusses plan elements, doesn't use actual resources.
Preparedness test simulates a system crash AND uses real resources to verify procedures work. Cost-effective because it's localized; tests partial recovery rather than full disaster simulation.

questions.question: While designing the business continuity plan (BCP) for an airline reservation system, the MOST appropriate method of data transfer/backup at an offsite location is:

options.A: shadow file processing.
options.B: electronic vaulting.
options.C: hard-disk mirroring.
options.D: hot-site provisioning.

questions.correct_explanation: In shadow file processing, exact duplicates of the files are maintained at the same site or at a remote site. The two files are processed concurrently. This is used for critical data files, such as airline booking systems.

wrong_explanations.B: Electronic vaulting electronically transmits data either to direct access storage, an optical disc or another storage medium; this is a method used by banks. This method is not usually in real time, unlike a shadow file system.
wrong_explanations.C: Hard-disk mirroring provides redundancy in case the primary hard disk fails. All transactions and operations occur on two hard disks in the same server.
wrong_explanations.D: A hot site is an alternate site ready to take over business operations within a few hours of any business interruption and is not a method for backing up data.

tips: Trap is B 'electronic vaulting' — periodic batch transfer; not real-time.
Trap is C 'hard-disk mirroring' — same-site mirror; doesn't protect against site disaster.
Trap is D 'hot site provisioning' — facility, not data transfer method.

Airline reservations = real-time, can't lose any transaction. Shadow file processing maintains live duplicates at the offsite location, processing concurrently. Highest data protection for live systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST method for determining the criticality of each application system in the production environment?

options.A: Interview the application programmers.
options.B: Perform a gap analysis.
options.C: Review the most recent application audits.
options.D: Perform a business impact analysis (BIA).

questions.correct_explanation: A business impact analysis (BIA) gives the impact of the loss of each application. A BIA is conducted with representatives of the business that can accurately describe the criticality of a system and its importance to the business.

wrong_explanations.A: Interviews with the application programmers provide limited information related to the criticality of the systems.
wrong_explanations.B: A gap analysis is relevant to system development and project management but does not determine application criticality.
wrong_explanations.C: The audits may not contain the required information about application criticality or may not have been done recently.

tips: Trap is A 'interview programmers' — knows technical, not business criticality.
Trap is B 'gap analysis' — comparison, not criticality.
Trap is C 'recent application audits' — audit findings, not criticality assessment.
BIA is purpose-designed to determine business criticality of each application/process. Quantifies impact of loss; ranks by business need. Foundational input to recovery planning.

questions.question: Code erroneously excluded from a production release was subsequently moved into the production environment, bypassing normal change procedures. Which of the following choices is of MOST concern to the information systems (IS) auditor performing a postimplementation review?

options.A: The code was missed during the initial implementation.
options.B: The change did not have change management approval.
options.C: The error was discovered during the postimplementation review.
options.D: The release team used the same change order number.

questions.correct_explanation: Change management approval of changes mitigates the risk of unauthorized changes being introduced to the production environment. Unauthorized changes might result in disruption of systems or fraud. It is, therefore, imperative to ensure that each change has appropriate change management approval.

wrong_explanations.A: Although missing a component of a release is indicative of a process deficiency, it is of more concern that the missed change was promoted into the production environment without management approval.
wrong_explanations.C: Most release/change control errors are discovered during postimplementation review. Jt is of greater concern that the change was promoted without management approval after it was discovered.
wrong_explanations.D: Using the same change order number is not a relevant concern.

tips: Trap is A 'code missed during release' — symptom; the process failure is what matters.
Trap is C 'discovered during postimplementation review' — discovery is good; the missing approval is the concern.
Trap is D 'same change order number' — administrative, not the substance.

Bypassing change management = unauthorized production change. Could be benign (forgotten code) or malicious (backdoor). Either way, the control failure is the central concern, not the specific instance.

questions.question: A hot site should be implemented as a recovery strategy when the:

options.A: disaster downtime tolerance is low.
options.B: recovery point objective (RPO) is high.
options.C: recovery time objective (RTO) is high.
options.D: maximum tolerable downtime is long.

questions.correct_explanation: Disaster downtime tolerance is the time gap during which the business can accept non-availability of IT facilities. If this time gap is low, recovery strategies that can be implemented within a short period of time, such as a hot site, should be used.

wrong_explanations.B: The recovery point objective (RPO) is the earliest point in time at which it is possible to recover the data. A high RPO means that the process would result in greater losses of data.
wrong_explanations.C: A high recovery time objective (RTO) means that additional time would be available for the recovery strategy, thus making other recovery alternatives-such as warm or cold sites-viable alternatives.
wrong_explanations.D: if the maximum tolerable downtime is long, then a warm or cold site is a more cost-effective solution.

tips: Trap is B 'RPO is high' — high RPO = tolerant of data loss; doesn't dictate hot site.
Trap is C 'RTO is high' — high RTO = lots of recovery time; cold/warm site sufficient.
Trap is D 'maximum tolerable downtime is long' — long downtime = no need for hot site.
Hot site = always-ready replica with running systems. Justified ONLY when downtime tolerance is very low (minutes/hours). Lower tolerance = more expensive recovery = hot site economically justified.

questions.question: In which of the following situations is it MOST appropriate to implement data mirroring as the recovery strategy?

options.A: Disaster tolerance is high.
options.B: The recovery time objective (RTO) is high.
options.C: The recovery point objective (RPO) is low.
options.D: The RPO is high.

questions.correct_explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) indicates the latest point in time at which it is possible to recover the data. This determines how often the data must be backed up to minimize data loss. If the RPO is low, then the organization does not want to lose much data and must use a process such as data mirroring to prevent data loss.

wrong_explanations.A: Data mirroring is a data recovery technique, and disaster tolerance addresses the allowable time for an outage of the business.
wrong_explanations.B: The recovery time objective (RTO) is an indicator of disaster tolerance. Data mirroring addresses data loss, not the RTO.
wrong_explanations.D: If the RPO is high, then a less expensive backup strategy can be used; data mirroring should not be implemented as the data recovery strategy.

tips: Trap is A 'high disaster tolerance' — opposite; tolerance high = mirroring overkill.
Trap is B 'high RTO' — high RTO = lots of time; mirroring's real-time aspect not required.
Trap is D 'high RPO' — high RPO = tolerant of data loss; mirroring not needed.
Data mirroring = real-time replica with zero/minimal lag. Justified ONLY when RPO is low (no data loss tolerable). Drives toward always-current copy.

questions.question: Which of the following stakeholders is the MOST important in terms of developing a business continuity plan (BCP)?

options.A: Process owners
options.B: Application owners
options.C: Board of directors
options.D: IT management

questions.correct_explanation: Process owners are essential in identifying the critical business functions, recovery times and resources needed.

wrong_explanations.B: A business continuity plan (BCP) is concerned with the continuity of business processes, while applications may or may not support critical business processes.
wrong_explanations.C: The board of directors might approve the plan, but they are typically not involved in the details of developingthe BCP.
wrong_explanations.D: IT management identifies the IT resources, servers and infrastructure needed to support the critical business functions as defined by the business process owners.

tips: Trap is B 'application owners' — know specific apps, not the broader business processes.
Trap is C 'board of directors' — strategic governance, doesn't know operational continuity needs.
Trap is D 'IT management' — knows technology, not business processes.
Process owners run the business processes that BCP must protect. They know what activities matter, in what order, with what dependencies. Foundational stakeholders for BCP.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST efficient and sufficiently reliable way to test the design effectiveness of a change control process?

options.A: Test a sample population of change requests.
options.B: Test a sample of authorized changes.
options.C: Interview personnel in charge of the change control process.
options.D: Perform an end-to-end walk-through of the process.

questions.correct_explanation: Observation is the best and most effective method to test changes to ensure that the process is effectively designed.

wrong_explanations.A: Testing a sample population of changes is a test of compliance and operating effectiveness to ensure that users submitted the proper documentation/requests. It does not test the effectiveness of the design.
wrong_explanations.B: Testing changes that have been authorized may not provide sufficient assurance of the entire process because it does not test the elements of the process related to authorization or detect changes that bypassed the controls.
wrong_explanations.C: Interviewing personnel in charge of the change control process is not as effective as a walk-through of the change controls process because people may know the process but not follow it.

tips: Trap is A 'sample of change requests' — tests requests, not actual implementation.
Trap is B 'sample of authorized changes' — tests authorization, not full process design.
Trap is C 'interview personnel' — describes the process; doesn't observe it.
End-to-end walk-through = follow a change from request to production. Most efficient way to test design effectiveness; reveals gaps, handoffs, control points in one pass.

questions.question: During fieldwork, an information systems (IS) auditor experienced a system crash caused by a security patch installation. To provide reasonable assurance that this event will not recur, the IS auditor should ensure that:

options.A: only systems administrators perform the patch process during nonbusiness hours.
options.B: the client's change management and patching processes have proper controls.
options.C: patches are validated using parallel testing in production.
options.D: an approval process of the patch, including a risk assessment, is developed.

questions.correct_explanation: The change management process, which includes procedures regarding implementing changes during production hours, helps to ensure that this type of event does not recur. An information systems (IS) auditor should review the change management process, including patch management procedures, to verify that the process has adequate controls and to make suggestions accordingly.

wrong_explanations.A: Although system administrators normally install patches, it is more important that changes be made according to a formal procedure that includes testing and implementing the change during nonproduction times.
wrong_explanations.C: Although patches normally undergo testing, it is often impossible to test all patches thoroughly. It is more important that changes are made during nonproduction times and that a backout plan is in place in case of problems.
wrong_explanations.D: An approval process alone cannot directly prevent this type of incident from happening. There should be a complete change management process that includes testing, scheduling and approval.

tips: Trap is A 'admins patch during nonbusiness hours' — narrow tactical fix.
Trap is C 'parallel testing in production' — risky; testing in production isn't appropriate.
Trap is D 'patch approval with risk assessment' — partial; doesn't address full process.
Change management + patching processes with proper controls = systemic prevention. Tests in non-production, scheduled deployment, rollback plan. The framework makes single incidents unlikely.

questions.question: A batch transaction job failed in production; however, the same job returned no issues during user acceptance testing (UAT). Analysis of the production batch job indicates that it was altered after UAT. What control provides a mitigation for this risk?

options.A: Improve regression test cases.
options.B: Activate audit trails for a limited period after release.
options.C: Conduct an application user access review.
options.D: Implement a segregation/separation of duties (SoD) policy.

questions.correct_explanation: To ensure proper segregation/separation of duties (SoD), developers should be restricted to the development environment only. If code needs to be modified after user acceptance testing, the process must be restarted in development.

wrong_explanations.A: Improving the quality of the testing is not applicable in this case, because the more important issue is that developers have access to the production environment.
wrong_explanations.B: Activating audit trails or performing additional logging may be useful; however, the more important issue is that developers have access to the production environment.
wrong_explanations.C: Conducting an application user access review does not identify developers' access to code because they are not included in this review.

tips: Trap is A 'improve regression tests' — addresses test coverage, not access to production.
Trap is B 'audit trails post-release' — detective; doesn't prevent the alteration.
Trap is C 'application user access review' — access review, narrow scope.
Code altered after UAT but before production = developer with production access. SoD policy preventing developers from modifying post-UAT code = systemic mitigation.

questions.question: An organization completed a business impact analysis (BIA) as part of business continuity planning. The NEXT step in the process is to develop:

options.A: a business continuity strategy.
options.B: a test and exercise plan.
options.C: a user training program.
options.D: the business continuity plan (BCP).

questions.correct_explanation: A business continuity strategy is the next phase because it identifies the best way to recover. The criticality of the business process, the cost, the time required to recover, and security must be considered during this phase.

wrong_explanations.B: The recovery strategy and plan development precede the test plan.
wrong_explanations.C: Training can only be developed once the business continuity plan (BCP) is in place.
wrong_explanations.D: A strategy must be determined before the BCP is developed.

tips: Trap is B 'test and exercise plan' — comes after the BCP exists.
Trap is C 'user training program' — operational, after BCP and tests.
Trap is D 'BCP itself' — strategy precedes plan; you decide HOW to recover before WRITING the plan.
BIA → Strategy → Plan → Test → Train. Strategy decides recovery approach (hot/warm/cold/reciprocal). Plan operationalizes the strategy.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor performing an application maintenance audit would review the log of program changes for the:

options.A: authorization of program changes.
options.B: creation date of a current object module.
options.C: number of program changes actually made.
options.D: creation date of a current source program.

questions.correct_explanation: The auditor wants to ensure that only authorized changes have been made to the application. The auditor would therefore review the log of program changes to verify that all changes have been approved.

wrong_explanations.B: The creation date of the current object module does not indicate earlier changes to the application.
wrong_explanations.C: The auditor reviews the system to notice the number of changes actually made but then verifies that all the changes were authorized.
wrong_explanations.D: The creation date of the current source program does not identify earlier changes.

tips: Trap is B 'object module creation date' — one data point, not authorization evidence.
Trap is C 'number of changes' — quantity, not authorization.
Trap is D 'source program creation date' — same as B.
Application maintenance audit's PRIMARY question: were changes authorized? Log of changes plus authorization records = the audit trail. Authorization is the central concern.

questions.question: Which of the following assures an enterprise of the existence and effectiveness of internal controls relative to the service provided by a third party?

options.A: Current service level agreement (SLA)
options.B: Recent independent third-party audit report
options.C: Current business continuity plan (BCP) procedures
options.D: Recent disaster recovery plan (DRP) test report

questions.correct_explanation: An independent third-party audit report, such as a Statements on Standards for Attestation Engagements 16, provides assurance of the existence and effectiveness of internal controls at the third party.

wrong_explanations.A: A service level agreement (SLA) defines the contracted level of service; however, it does not provide assurance related to internal controls.
wrong_explanations.C: Although a business continuity plan (BCP) is essential, it does not provide assurance related to internal controls.
wrong_explanations.D: Although a disaster recovery plan (DRP) is essential, it does not provide assurance related to internal controls.

tips: Trap is A 'current SLA' — defines expectations, doesn't verify execution.
Trap is C 'current BCP procedures' — continuity-specific, not internal control assurance.
Trap is D 'recent DRP test report' — DR-specific, not broader internal control.
Independent third-party audit (SSAE 16/SOC 2) = objective verification of provider's internal controls. Reusable assurance: customer doesn't audit each time; relies on independent attestation.

questions.question: When reviewing a disaster recovery plan, an information systems (IS) auditor should be MOST concerned with the lack of:

options.A: process owner involvement.
options.B: well-documented testing procedures.
options.C: an alternate processing facility.
options.D: a well-documented data classification scheme.

questions.correct_explanation: Process owner involvement is a critical part of the business impact analysis (BIA), which is used to create the disaster recovery plan. If the information systems (IS) auditor determines that process owners were not involved, this is a significant concern.

wrong_explanations.B: Although well-documented testing procedures are important, unless process owners are involved there is no way to know whether the priorities and critical elements of the plan are valid.
wrong_explanations.C: An alternate processing facility may be a requirement to meet the needs of the business; however, such a decision needs to be based on the BIA.
wrong_explanations.D: A data classification scheme is important to ensure that controls over data are appropriate; however, this is a lesser concern than a lack of process owner involvement.

tips: Trap is B 'testing procedures' — important but follows from process owner involvement.
Trap is C 'alternate processing facility' — facility choice depends on BIA results.
Trap is D 'data classification' — data concern, separate from DRP.
DRP without process owner involvement = built without business input. Wrong systems prioritized, wrong recovery times, wrong dependencies. Foundational requirement for valid DRP.

questions.question: Which of the following is the PRIMARY critical success factor of a control self-assessment (CSA) program?

options.A: Assigning a knowledgeable and experienced information systems (IS) auditor as a facilitator for the CSA program
options.B: Conducting a meeting with the business unit representatives, including relevant staff and management
options.C: Developing the measures of success for each CSA phase (planning, implementation and monitoring)
options.D: Identifying the actions needed to increase the likelihood of achieving the business unit's objective

questions.correct_explanation: The meeting with the business unit representatives at the beginning of the process is crucial to identify the business unit's primary objective to determine the reliability of the internal control system afterward.

wrong_explanations.A: The assignment of the suitable information systems (IS) auditor to facilitate the CSA program would come after identifying the primary objective of the business unit.
wrong_explanations.C: The development of the measures of success for each CSA phase would be after identifying the primary objective of the business unit and while designing the program itself.
wrong_explanations.D: The identification of the actions needed to increase the likelihood of achieving the primary objective of the business unit would take place through recommendations at the closing up of the CSA program.

tips: Trap is A 'experienced auditor as facilitator' — skill matters but process is more critical.
Trap is C 'measures of success per phase' — metrics, comes after objective is set.
Trap is D 'identify actions for objective' — execution, follows from initial alignment.
Initial meeting with business unit identifies the unit's primary objective. CSA reliability depends on tying control evaluation to that objective. Without the meeting, CSA evaluates wrong things.

questions.question: Which of the following activities performed by a database administrator (DBA) should be performed by a different person?

options.A: Deleting database activity logs
options.B: Implementing database optimization tools
options.C: Monitoring database usage
options.D: Defining backup and recovery procedures

questions.correct_explanation: Because database activity logs record activities performed by the database administrator (DBA), deleting them should be performed by an individual other than the DBA. This is a compensating control to aid in ensuring an appropriate separation of duties and is associated with the DBA's role.

wrong_explanations.B: Implementing database optimization tools is part of the DBA's normal job function.
wrong_explanations.C: Monitoring database usage is part of the DB A's normal job function.
wrong_explanations.D: Defining backup and recovery procedures is part of the DBA's normal job function.

tips: Trap is B 'database optimization' — DBA expertise area.
Trap is C 'monitor database usage' — DBA responsibility.
Trap is D 'backup/recovery procedures' — DBA responsibility.
DBA controlling AND able to delete logs of their own activity = no audit trail. Compensating control: someone else owns log integrity. SoD compliance for high-privilege role.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST reason for integrating the testing of noncritical systems in the disaster recovery plan (DRP) with the business continuity plan (BCP)?

options.A: To ensure that the DRPs is aligned to the business impact analysis (BIA).
options.B: Infrastructure recovery personnel can be assisted by business subject matter experts.
options.C: The BCPs may assume the existence of capabilities that are not in the DRPs.
options.D: To provide business executives with knowledge of disaster recovery capabilities.

questions.correct_explanation: The BCPs may assume the existence of capabilities that are not part of the DRPs, such as allowing employees to work from home during the disaster; however, IT may not have made sufficient provisions for these capabilities (e.g., they cannot support a large number of employees working from home). Although the noncritical systems are important, it is possible that they are not part of the DRPs. For example, an organization may use an online system that does not interface with the internal systems. If the business function using the system is a critical process, the system should be tested, and it may not be part of the DRP. Therefore, DRP and BCP testing should be integrated.

wrong_explanations.A: The disaster recovery plan (DRP) should be aligned with the business impact analysis (BJA); however, this has no impact on integrating the testing of noncritical systems in the DRPs with the business continuity plan (BCP).
wrong_explanations.B: Infrastructure personnel will be focused on restoring the various platforms that make up the infrastructure, and it is not necessary for business subject matter experts to be involved.
wrong_explanations.D: Although business executives may be interested in the benefits of disaster recovery, testing is not the best way to accomplish this task.

tips: Trap is A 'aligned to BIA' — alignment goal but not the specific reason for joint testing.
Trap is B 'subject matter experts assist' — staffing benefit, not the testing rationale.
Trap is D 'business executive knowledge' — informational benefit.
BCP often assumes capabilities not in DRP — like 'employees work from home with VPN access'. Testing both together surfaces these dependencies. Each plan reveals what the other assumes.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds out-of-range data in some tables of a database. Which of the following controls would BEST avoid this situation?

options.A: Log all table update transactions.
options.B: Implement before-and-after image reporting.
options.C: Use tracing and tagging.
options.D: Implement integrity constraints in the database.

questions.correct_explanation: Implementing integrity constraints in the database is a preventive control because data are checked against predefined tables or rules, preventing any undefined data from being entered.

wrong_explanations.A: Logging all table update transactions is a detective control that would not help avoid invalid data entry.
wrong_explanations.B: Implementing before-and-after image reporting is a detective control that would not help avoid the situation.
wrong_explanations.C: Tracing and tagging are used to test application systems and controls and cannot prevent out-of-range data.

tips: Trap is A 'log table updates' — detective; logs after the fact.
Trap is B 'before/after image reporting' — detective.
Trap is C 'tracing and tagging' — testing technique, not preventive control.
Integrity constraints in the database REJECT invalid data at insertion. Preventive control at the source. Out-of-range data never enters the database.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor discovers that some users installed personal software on their PCs. This is not explicitly forbidden by the security policy. The BEST approach for an IS auditor is to recommend that the:

options.A: IT department implement control mechanisms to prevent unauthorized software installation.
options.B: security policy be updated to include the specific language regarding unauthorized software.
options.C: IT department prohibit the download of unauthorized software.
options.D: users obtain approval from an IS manager before installing nonstandard software.

questions.correct_explanation: Lack of specific language addressing unauthorized software in the acceptable use policy is a weakness in administrative controls. The policy should be reviewed and updated to address the issue---and provide authority for the IT department to implement technical controls.

wrong_explanations.A: An information systems (IS) auditor's obligation is to report on observations noted and make the best recommendation, which is to address the situation through policy. The IT department cannot implement controls in the absence of the authority provided through policy.
wrong_explanations.C: Preventing downloads of unauthorized software is not the complete solution. Unauthorized software can be also introduced through compact disks (CDs) and USB drives.
wrong_explanations.D: Requiring approval from the IS manager before installation of the nonstandard software is an exception handling control. It would not be effective unless a preventive control to prohibit user installation of unauthorized software is established first.

tips: Trap is A 'IT prevent unauthorized installation' — would need policy authority first.
Trap is C 'IT prohibit downloads' — same; needs policy basis.
Trap is D 'users obtain IS manager approval' — exception process, not policy correction.
Policy gap = no enforcement basis. The auditor's recommendation must address the policy first; then technical controls can implement and enforce. Policy → procedures → technology, in that order.

questions.question: The purpose of code signing is to provide assurance that:

options.A: the software has not been subsequently modified.
options.B: the application can safely interface with another signed application.
options.C: the signer of the application is trusted.
options.D: the private key of the signer has not been compromised.

questions.correct_explanation: Code signing ensures that the executable code came from a reputable source and has not been modified after being signed.

wrong_explanations.B: The signing of code does not ensure that it will integrate with other applications.
wrong_explanations.C: Code signing provides assurance of the source but does not ensure that the source is trusted. The code signing will, however, ensure that the code has not been modified.
wrong_explanations.D: The compromise of the sender's private key results in a loss of trust and is not the purpose of code signing.

tips: Trap is B 'application can interface with another' — code signing isn't about interface compatibility.
Trap is C 'signer is trusted' — separate concern; certificate validation establishes trust.
Trap is D 'private key not compromised' — separate concern; key management.
Code signing's purpose: post-signing tampering detection. The signature is invalid if the code changes. Confirms 'this is exactly what was signed' — not who or whether the signer is trusted.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor analyzing the audit log of a database management system (DBMS) finds that some transactions were partially executed as a result of an error and have not been rolled back. Which of the following transaction processing features has been violated?

options.A: Consistency
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Durability
options.D: Atomicity

questions.correct_explanation: Atomicity guarantees that either the entire transaction is processed or none of it is.

wrong_explanations.A: Consistency ensures that the database is in a proper state when the transaction begins and ends and that the transaction has not violated integrity rules.
wrong_explanations.B: Isolation means that, while in an intermediate state, the transaction data are invisible to external operations. This prevents two transactions from attempting to access the same data at the same time.
wrong_explanations.C: Durability guarantees that a successful transaction will persist and cannot be undone.

tips: Trap is A 'consistency' — database stays in valid state across transactions; not the property violated.
Trap is B 'isolation' — concurrent transactions don't interfere; not the property violated.
Trap is C 'durability' — committed transactions persist after failure; not the property violated.
Atomicity = all-or-nothing. Partial execution without rollback = atomicity violation. Either complete or roll back; no partial state.

questions.question: Enterprise governance of IT frameworks has been developed MAINLY to help an organization's leaders:

options.A: use resources responsibly and manage information systems risk.
options.B: realize benefits and manage the performance of practices and processes.
options.C: deliver value to stakeholders and preserve the value created.
options.D: establish accountability and manage information security risk.

questions.correct_explanation: Enterprise governance of IT frameworks help an organization's leaders to deliver value to stakeholders by using resources responsibly, realizing value delivered, establishing roles and responsibilities, preserving value through information risk management, and maintaining the required levels of performance.

wrong_explanations.A: Using resources responsibly contributes to value creation, while managing information systems risk helps to preserve value.
wrong_explanations.B: Benefits realization management measures how value is created, and performance management contributes to value preservation.
wrong_explanations.D: Establishing roles and responsibilities helps in value creation, while information assurance is about managing the risk associated with information assets and preserving the value of thosea.

tips: Trap is A 'use resources responsibly + manage IS risk' — partial; doesn't capture value preservation.
Trap is B 'realize benefits + manage performance' — partial; misses delivery.
Trap is D 'establish accountability + manage security risk' — partial; security is a subset.
Enterprise governance of IT = deliver value + preserve value. Both halves matter. Resources, risk, performance, accountability all serve these two outcomes.

questions.question: Which of the following distinguishes a business impact analysis (BIA) from a risk assessment?

options.A: Inventory of critical assets
options.B: Identification of vulnerabilities
options.C: Listing of threats
options.D: Determination of acceptable downtime

questions.correct_explanation: A determination of acceptable downtime is made only in a BIA.

wrong_explanations.A: An inventory of critical assets is completed in a risk assessment and a business impact analysis (BIA).
wrong_explanations.B: The identification of vulnerabilities is relevant in a risk assessment and a BIA.
wrong_explanations.C: A listing of threats is relevant in a risk assessment and a BIA.

tips: Trap is A 'inventory of critical assets' — both BIA and risk assessment do this.
Trap is B 'identification of vulnerabilities' — primarily risk assessment.
Trap is C 'listing of threats' — primarily risk assessment.
BIA's distinguishing output: acceptable downtime per process. Translates business impact into recovery time targets. Risk assessment doesn't define this.

questions.question: When reviewing a hardware maintenance program, an information systems (IS) auditor should assess whether:

options.A: the schedule of all unplanned maintenance is maintained.
options.B: it is in line with historical trends.
options.C: it has been approved by the IS steering committee.
options.D: the program is validated against vendor specifications.

questions.correct_explanation: Although maintenance requirements vary based on complexity and performance workloads, a hardware maintenance schedule should be validated against the vendor-provided specifications.

wrong_explanations.A: Unplanned maintenance cannot be scheduled.
wrong_explanations.B: Hardware maintenance programs do not necessarily need to be in line with historic trends.
wrong_explanations.C: Maintenance schedules normally are not approved by the steering committee.

tips: Trap is A 'unplanned maintenance schedule' — unplanned isn't scheduled by definition.
Trap is B 'historical trends' — historical patterns may not match current needs.
Trap is C 'IS steering committee approval' — governance for major decisions, not maintenance specifics.
Hardware maintenance schedule should follow VENDOR specifications. Vendor knows the equipment best. Auditor verifies the program matches vendor recommendations.

questions.question: Enterprise governance oflT frameworks MAINLY helps organizations address business issues by:

options.A: aligning high-level strategic objectives with operational-level objectives, followed by direct work outcomes.
options.B: establishing a risk management capability to address business issues and preserve the value delivered to stakeholders.
