options.C: developing a roadmap to help fill in the gap between the current state (as-is) and the desired state (to-be).
options.D: conducting multiple meetings with different stakeholder groups to learn about their expectations.

questions.correct_explanation: The strategic alignment between business objectives and enterprise IT objectives is one of the most important advantages of applying enterprise governance of information and technology (EGIT) frameworks because it helps in achieving enterprise objectives and delivering value at a reasonable cost.

wrong_explanations.B: Establishing risk management practices and processes as part of EGIT frameworks is much more effective after aligning the objectives of enterprise IT with the strategic direction of the organization, better preserving the value delivered to stakeholders.
wrong_explanations.C: Conducting assessments and developing roadmaps comes after establishing strategic alignment between enterprise IT and business strategies.
wrong_explanations.D: Such meetings are a good tool to develop successful enterprise IT strategies but should be done after understanding the business strategies and aligning enterprise IT with them.

tips: Trap is B 'risk management capability' — output of governance, not the addressing approach.
Trap is C 'roadmap from current to desired' — implementation tactic.
Trap is D 'stakeholder meetings' — input, not the addressing approach.
EGIT addresses business issues by ALIGNING strategic objectives with operational outcomes. Top-down alignment cascade: strategy → operations → results. Coherent translation through the org.

questions.question: The PRIMARY purpose of an enterprise architecture is to:

options.A: respond to the increasing complexity of IT and modern organizations.
options.B: align IT with the business strategy and ensure that IT investments deliver real returns.
options.C: facilitate understanding, management and planning for IT investments.
options.D: develop roadmaps to enable safe and successful change from the current state to the desired state.

questions.correct_explanation: The main purpose of EA is to enable the enterprise to most effectively achieve its mission, business strategy and goals through successful alignment between IT and the strategic direction of the business.

wrong_explanations.A: The current focus of enterprise architecture (EA) is to respond to the increasing complexity of IT and modern organizations.
wrong_explanations.C: EA involves documenting an organization's IT assets in a structured manner to facilitate understanding, management and planning for IT investments to facilitate the alignment of IT with the business.
wrong_explanations.D: The development of IT strategies and roadmaps comes after establishing strategic alignment between the IT objectives and the business strategies.

tips: Trap is A 'respond to IT complexity' — context, not purpose.
Trap is C 'understanding/management/planning' — outcome of EA, not its primary purpose.
Trap is D 'roadmaps for change' — tactic, not purpose.
EA's PRIMARY purpose: align IT investments with business strategy so investments deliver real business value. Without alignment, IT spending is disconnected from business outcomes.

questions.question: Business units are concerned about the performance of a newly implemented system. Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor recommend?

options.A: Develop a baseline and monitor system usage.
options.B: Define alternate processing procedures.
options.C: Prepare the maintenance manual.
options.D: Implement the changes users have suggested.

questions.correct_explanation: An information systems (IS) auditor should recommend the development of a performance baseline and monitor the system's performance against the baseline to develop empirical data upon which decisions for modifying the system can be made.

wrong_explanations.B: Alternate processing procedures will not alter a system's performance, and no changes should be made until the reported issue has been examined more thoroughly.
wrong_explanations.C: A maintenance manual will not alter a system's performance or address the user concerns.
wrong_explanations.D: Implementing changes without knowledge of the cause(s) for the perceived poor performance may not result in a more efficient system.

tips: Trap is B 'alternate processing procedures' — bypass, doesn't address performance.
Trap is C 'maintenance manual' — documentation, doesn't fix performance.
Trap is D 'implement user-suggested changes' — premature without baseline.
Performance complaints need objective measurement. Establish baseline first; then monitoring identifies if there's actually a problem and where. Decisions based on data, not perception.

questions.question: The MAIN purpose of service level management (SLM) is to:

options.A: set expectations between users and providers.
options.B: ensure that services are managed to deliver the highest achievable level of availability.
options.C: keep the costs associated with any service at a minimum.
options.D: monitor and report any legal noncompliance to business management.

questions.correct_explanation: The objective of service level management (SLM) is to negotiate, document and manage (i.e., provide and monitor) the services in the manner in which the customer requires those services.

wrong_explanations.B: SLM does not necessarily ensure that services are delivered at the highest achievable level of availability (e.g., redundancy and clustering). Although maximizing availability might be necessary for some critical services, it cannot be applied as a general rule of thumb.
wrong_explanations.C: SLM cannot ensure that costs for all services will be kept at a low or minimum level because costs associated with a service will directly reflect the customer's requirements.
wrong_explanations.D: Monitoring and reporting legal noncompliance is not a primary objective of SLM.

tips: Trap is B 'highest achievable availability' — too aggressive; SLM negotiates appropriate level, not maximum.
Trap is C 'minimize cost' — cost concern, not the primary purpose.
Trap is D 'monitor legal noncompliance' — narrow regulatory focus.
SLM's main purpose: align user expectations with provider capability through a documented agreement. Both sides know what to expect; performance is measurable against agreement.

questions.question: Which of the following would be a MAJOR concern for an information systems (IS) auditor reviewing a business continuity plan (BCP)?

options.A: The plan is approved by the chief information officer.
options.B: The plan contact lists have not been updated.
options.C: Test results are not adequately documented.
options.D: The training schedule for recovery personnel is not included.

questions.correct_explanation: The effectiveness of a BCP can best be determined through tests. If results of tests are not documented, then there is no basis for feedback, updates, etc.

wrong_explanations.A: Ideally, the board of directors should approve the plan to ensure acceptability, but it is possible to delegate approval authority to the chief information officer. Pragmatically, lack of documenting test results can have more significant consequences.
wrong_explanations.B: The contact lists are an important part of the business continuity plan (BCP); however, they are not as important as documenting the test results.
wrong_explanations.D: If test results are documented, a need for training will be identified and the BCP will be updated.

tips: Trap is A 'approved by CIO' — typically appropriate; CIO has BCP authority.
Trap is B 'contact lists not updated' — operational issue, addressable.
Trap is D 'no training schedule' — important but BCP can include training plans separately.
Test results not documented = no learning, no improvement, no proof of effectiveness. The whole point of testing is to capture results that drive future updates. Test without documentation is wasted.

questions.question: Which of the following processes will be MOST effective in reducing the risk that unauthorized software on a backup server is distributed to the production server?

options.A: Manually copy files to accomplish replication.
options.B: Review changes in the software version control system.
options.C: Ensure that developers do not have access to the backup server.
options.D: Review the access control log of the backup server.

questions.correct_explanation: It is common practice for software changes to be tracked and controlled using version control software. An information systems (IS) auditor should review reports or logs from this system to identify the software that is promoted to production. Only moving the versions on the version control system program will prevent the transfer of development or earlier versions.

wrong_explanations.A: Even ifreplication is conducted manually with due care, there remains a risk to copying unauthorized software from one server to another.
wrong_explanations.C: If unauthorized code was introduced onto the backup server by developers, controls on the production server and the software version control system should mitigate this risk.
wrong_explanations.D: Review of the access log will identify staff access or the operations performed; however, it may not provide enough information to detect the release of unauthorized software.

tips: Trap is A 'manual file copy' — slow, error-prone, doesn't prevent unauthorized files.
Trap is C 'developers no access to backup' — preventive but bypasses normal version control.
Trap is D 'access control log review' — detective only.
Version control system tracks all changes with audit trail. Reviewing version control changes catches unauthorized files BEFORE they're released to production. Best preventive review.

questions.question: An organization recently installed a security patch that crashed the production server. To minimize the probability of this occurring again, an information systems (IS) auditor should:

options.A: apply the patch according to the patch's release notes.
options.B: ensure that a good change management process is in place.
options.C: thoroughly test the patch before sending it to production.
options.D: approve the patch after doing a risk assessment.

questions.correct_explanation: An IS auditor must review the change management process, including patch management procedures, and verify that the process has adequate controls and make suggestions accordingly.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor should not apply the patch. That is an administrator responsibility.
wrong_explanations.C: Testing of the patch is the responsibility of the development or production support team, not the auditor.
wrong_explanations.D: The IS auditor is not authorized to approve a patch. That is a responsibility of a steering committee.

tips: Trap is A 'apply patch per release notes' — tactical advice, doesn't ensure systematic prevention.
Trap is C 'thoroughly test before production' — testing matters but is part of change management.
Trap is D 'risk assessment for patches' — same; part of change management.
Change management process is the systemic answer. Includes testing, approval, rollback planning, deployment timing. The auditor reviews the framework, not just one element.

questions.question: In a relational database with referential integrity, the use of which of the following keys would prevent deletion of a row from a customer table if the customer number of that row is stored with live orders on the orders table?

options.A: Foreign key
options.B: Primary key
options.C: Secondary key
options.D: Public key

questions.correct_explanation: In a relational database with referential integrity, the use of foreign keys would prevent events such as primary key changes and record deletions, resulting in orphaned relations within the database.

wrong_explanations.B: It should not be possible to delete a row from a customer table when the customer number (primary key) of that row is stored with live orders on the orders table (the foreign key to the customer table). A primary key works in one table so it is not able to provide/ referential integrity by itself.
wrong_explanations.C: Secondary keys that are not foreign keys are not subject to referential integrity checks.
wrong_explanations.D: A public key is related to encryption and not linked in any way to referential integrity.

tips: Trap is B 'primary key' — uniquely identifies rows but doesn't enforce inter-table relationships.
Trap is C 'secondary key' — alternate identifier, not relationship.
Trap is D 'public key' — cryptography, unrelated.
Foreign key creates dependency between tables. Database refuses to delete a row that other tables reference. Maintains referential integrity automatically.

questions.question: The PRIMARY objective of testing a business continuity plan (BCP) is to:

options.A: familiarize employees with the business continuity plan (BCP).
options.B: ensure that all residual risk is addressed.
options.C: exercise all possible disaster scenarios.
options.D: identify limitations of the BCP.

questions.correct_explanation: Testing the BCP provides the best evidence of any limitations that may exist.

wrong_explanations.A: Familiarizing employees with the business continuity plan (BCP) is a secondary benefit of a test.
wrong_explanations.B: It is not cost-effective to address all residual risk in a BCP.
wrong_explanations.C: It is not practical to test all possible disaster scenarios.

tips: Trap is A 'familiarize employees' — training benefit, not the primary objective.
Trap is B 'all residual risk addressed' — impossible; some residual always remains.
Trap is C 'exercise all scenarios' — not feasible; testing covers selected scenarios.
Test purpose: identify limitations and gaps in the plan. What works, what doesn't, what's missing. Continuous improvement of the plan based on test discoveries.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor examining the security configuration of an operating system (OS) should review the:

options.A: transaction logs.
options.B: authorization tables.
options.C: parameter settings.
options.D: routing tables.

questions.correct_explanation: Configuration parameters allow a standard piece of software to be customized for diverse environments and are important in determining how a system runs. The parameter settings should be appropriate to an organization's workload and control environment. Improper implementation and/or monitoring of OSs can result in undetected errors and corruption of the data being processed, and lead to unauthorized access and inaccurate logging of system usage.

wrong_explanations.A: Transaction logs are used to track and analyze transactions related to an application or system interface, but that is not the primary source of audit evidence in an operating system (OS) audit.
wrong_explanations.B: Authorization tables are used to verify implementation of logical access controls and will not be of much help when reviewing control features of an OS.
wrong_explanations.D: Routing tables do not contain information about the OS and, therefore, provide no information to aid in the evaluation of controls.

tips: Trap is A 'transaction logs' — operational, not security configuration.
Trap is B 'authorization tables' — application-level, not OS configuration.
Trap is D 'routing tables' — network configuration.
OS security configuration is captured in PARAMETER SETTINGS — security policies, password rules, account lockouts, audit settings. Direct review of security parameters.

questions.question: While reviewing the IT infrastructure, an information systems (IS) auditor notices that storage resources are continuously being added. The IS auditor should:

options.A: recommend the use of disk mirroring.
options.B: review the adequacy of offsite storage.
options.C: review the capacity management process.
options.D: recommend the use of a compression algorithm.

questions.correct_explanation: Capacity management is the planning and monitoring of computer resources to ensure that available IT resources are used efficiently and effectively. This looks at capacity from a strategic viewpoint and allows a plan to forecast and purchase additional equipment in a planned manner.

wrong_explanations.A: A disk mirroring solution increases storage requirements. This is not advisable until a proper capacity management plan is in place.
wrong_explanations.B: Offsite storage is unrelated to the problem.
wrong_explanations.D: Although data compression may save disk space, it can affect system performance. This is not the first choice-the auditor should recommend more investigation into the increased demand for storage before providing any recommended solutions.

tips: Trap is A 'disk mirroring' — protects against failure, not capacity issue.
Trap is B 'offsite storage' — backup concern, separate.
Trap is D 'compression algorithm' — saves space but doesn't address growth pattern.
Continuous storage growth = capacity management gap. Underlying issue: who's planning for growth, monitoring trends, and acquiring capacity ahead of need? Process review uncovers root cause.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY risk of using reciprocal agreements for disaster recovery between two business units in an organization?

options.A: The documents lack legal sufficiency.
options.B: Both entities are vulnerable to the same incident.
options.C: IT systems have non-identical configurations.
options.D: One party experiences more frequent disruptions than the other.

questions.correct_explanation: The use of reciprocal disaster recovery is based on the probability that both organizations will not suffer a disaster at the same time.

wrong_explanations.A: Inadequate agreements between two business units is a risk, but generally a lesser one than the risk that both organizations will suffer a disaster at the same time.
wrong_explanations.C: Although incompatible IT systems can create problems, it is a less significant risk than both organizations suffering from the same disaster at the same time.
wrong_explanations.D: Although one party may use the other's resources more frequently, this can be addressed by contractual provisions and is not a major risk.

tips: Trap is A 'documents lack legal sufficiency' — formal arrangement; legal validity is manageable.
Trap is C 'IT systems different' — operational concern, addressable.
Trap is D 'one party more disruptions' — unfair but recoverable.
Two business units within ONE organization face SAME risks (shared infrastructure, building, supply chain, workforce). Single incident affects both — defeating the reciprocal arrangement.

questions.question: When determining the acceptable time period for the resumption of critical business processes:

options.A: only downtime costs need to be considered.
options.B: recovery operations should be analyzed.
options.C: both downtime costs and recovery costs need to be evaluated.
options.D: indirect downtime costs should be ignored.

questions.correct_explanation: Downtime costs and recovery costs need to be evaluated in determining the acceptable time period before the resumption of critical business processes. The outcome of the business impact analysis should be a recovery strategy that represents the optimal balance.

wrong_explanations.A: Downtime costs cannot be looked at in isolation. The quicker information assets can be restored and business processing resumed, the smaller the downtime costs. However, the expenditure needed to have the redundant capability that is required to rapidly recover information resources might be prohibitive for nonessential business processes.
wrong_explanations.B: Recovery operations alone do not determine the acceptable time period for the resumption of critical business processes, and indirect downtime costs should be considered in addition to the direct cash outflows incurred due to business disruption.
wrong_explanations.D: The indirect costs of a serious disruption to normal business activity ( e.g., loss of customer and supplier goodwill and loss of market share) may actually be more significant than direct costs over time, thus reaching the point where business viability is threatened. e C,"11flodt,,lo,m,llon , Sr1ttm Aulfllm' DOMAIN 4-INFORMATION SYSTEMS OPERATIONS AND BUSINESS RESILIENCE (26%) 1.11MU:,,w.."

tips: Trap is A 'only downtime costs' — too narrow; ignores what recovery costs.
Trap is B 'only recovery operations' — too narrow; ignores downtime impact.
Trap is D 'ignore indirect costs' — incomplete picture; indirect costs (reputation, customer loss) are real.
Acceptable downtime balances DOWNTIME COSTS (rising) against RECOVERY COSTS (rising for shorter recovery). The optimal point minimizes the sum.

questions.question: Which of the following should the information systems (IS) auditor review to ensure the correct version of a data file is used for a production run?

options.A: Incident or error reports related to the production run
options.B: Schedules detailing the tasks performed by operators
options.C: Logs containing relevant system activity and events
options.D: Reports documenting the distribution of the produced output

questions.correct_explanation: System logs and analysis programs can be used by an information systems (IS) auditor to ensure that the correct file version was used for a production run.

wrong_explanations.A: Operator problem reports may provide information about errors or issues encountered during the production run, which can be useful for identifying potential data file version problems.
wrong_explanations.B: Operator work schedules are not directly re_levant to verifying the correct version of a data file for a production run.
wrong_explanations.D: Output distribution reports primarily focus on identifying and distributing application reports and may not directly contribute to verifying the correct version of a data file used for a production run.

tips: Trap is A 'incident reports' — covers problems, not version selection verification.
Trap is B 'operator schedules' — task assignment, not file content verification.
Trap is D 'output distribution reports' — output, not input.
System logs record file access events with timestamps and identifiers. Reviewing logs verifies which file version was actually used during the run.

questions.question: The MOST effective audit procedure in determining if unauthorized changes have been made to production code is to:

options.A: examine the change control system records and trace them forward to object code files.
options.B: review access control permissions operating within the production program libraries.
options.C: examine object code to find instances of changes and trace them back to change control records.
options.D: review change approved designations established within the change control system.

questions.correct_explanation: The procedure of examining object code files to establish instances of code changes and tracing these back to change control system records is a substantive test that directly addresses the risk of unauthorized code changes.

wrong_explanations.A: Examining the change control system records can help identify authorized changes, but it may not directly address the detection of unauthorized changes.
wrong_explanations.B: Reviewing access control permissions can help prevent unauthorized changes, but it may not detect changes that have already occurred.
wrong_explanations.D: Reviewing change approved designations can help identify authorized changes, but it may not directly detect unauthorized changes.

tips: Trap is A 'change control records → object code' — forward direction; assumes records are complete.
Trap is B 'access control review' — preventive but doesn't detect unauthorized changes.
Trap is D 'review approved designations' — process review, doesn't verify actual code.
Backward trace: examine ACTUAL CODE changes, then verify each had approval. Catches changes made WITHOUT going through change control — the unauthorized ones. Substantive test.

questions.question: During a database review, an information systems (IS) auditor notices that some tables in the database are not normalized. The IS auditor should next:

options.A: recommend that the database be normalized.
options.B: review the conceptual data model.
options.C: review the stored procedures.
options.D: review the justification.

questions.correct_explanation: If the database is not normalized, the IS auditor should review the justification because, in some situations, denormalization is recommended for performance reasons.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor should not immediately recommend normalizing the database until further investigation and analysis takes place.
wrong_explanations.B: Reviewing the conceptual data model may not directly provide information about normalization or the justification for the level of normalization.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing the stored procedures may not directly provide information about normalization.

tips: Trap is A 'recommend normalization' — premature; denormalization may be intentional.
Trap is B 'review conceptual data model' — design review, not the priority.
Trap is C 'review stored procedures' — SQL code, not design rationale.
Denormalization is sometimes intentional for performance reasons. Review the JUSTIFICATION first; if there's good reason, no finding. If no justification, then it's a finding.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST important for an information systems (IS) auditor to verify while conducting a business continuity audit?

options.A: Data backups are performed on a timely basis.
options.B: A recovery site is contracted for and available as needed.
options.C: Human safety procedures are in place.
options.D: Insurance coverage is adequate and premiums are current.

questions.correct_explanation: The most important element in any business continuity process is the protection of human life. This takes precedence over all other aspects of the plan.

wrong_explanations.A: performing data backups is necessary for a business continuity plan, but the information systems (IS) auditor will always be most concerned with human safety.
wrong_explanations.B: A recovery site is important for business continuity, but life safety is always the first priority.
wrong_explanations.D: Insurance coverage is not as important as life safety.

tips: Trap is A 'data backups timely' — important but data is recoverable; people are not.
Trap is B 'recovery site contracted' — facility concern; people first.
Trap is D 'insurance coverage' — financial protection; people first.
Human safety is ALWAYS the first priority in business continuity. Evacuation procedures, accounting for personnel, medical response. Foundational principle of BCP.

questions.question: The application systems of an organization using open-source software have no single recognized developer producing patches. Which of the following is the MOST secure way of updating open-source software?

options.A: Rewrite the patches and apply them.
options.B: Review the code and application of available patches.
options.C: Develop in-house patches.
options.D: Identify and test suitable patches before applying them.

questions.correct_explanation: Suitable patches from the existing developers should be selected and tested before applying them.

wrong_explanations.A: Rewriting the patches and applying them requires skilled resources and time to rewrite the patches, making it less practical and secure.
wrong_explanations.B: Code review is possible, but thorough testing is necessary before applying the patches.
wrong_explanations.C: Developing in-house patches may not be the most secure option if the IT department lacks the necessary skills and resources.

tips: Trap is A 'rewrite the patches' — overkill; original community usually has more expertise.
Trap is B 'review code and apply' — partial; testing is essential.
Trap is C 'develop in-house patches' — high cost, duplication of effort.
Open-source patching: identify suitable patches from the community, test in your environment, then apply. Same testing discipline as commercial software; the source matters less than the test.

questions.question: During the audit of a database server, which of the following poses the GREATEST security risk?

options.A: The password on the administrator account does not expire.
options.B: Default global security settings for the database remain unchanged.
options.C: Old data have not been purged.
options.D: Database activity is not fully logged.

questions.correct_explanation: Default security settings for the database can allow issues such as blank user passwords or passwords that are the same as the username. This poses the greatest security risk.

wrong_explanations.A: A nonexpiring password is a risk and an exposure but not as serious a risk as a weak password or the continued use of default settings.
wrong_explanations.C: Failure to purge old data may present a performance issue and data management concern but is not an immediate security concern.
wrong_explanations.D: Incomplete logging of database activity is a potential risk but not as serious a risk as default settings.

tips: Trap is A 'admin password doesn't expire' — security concern but specific to one account.
Trap is C 'old data not purged' — data lifecycle issue, not core security risk.
Trap is D 'database activity not logged' — auditing gap, but logging absence is detective.
Default global security settings = publicly known. Default passwords (sa/sa, admin/admin) are in attacker tool kits. Without changing defaults, the database is essentially open.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor discovers that developers have operator access to the command line of a production environment operating system. Which of the following controls would BEST mitigate the risk of undetected and unauthorized program changes to the production environment?

options.A: Commands typed on the command line are logged.
options.B: Hash keys are calculated periodically for programs and matched against hash keys calculated for the most recent authorized versions of the programs.
options.C: Access to the operating system command line is granted through an access restriction tool with preapproved rights.
options.D: Software development tools and compilers have been removed from the production environment.

questions.correct_explanation: Periodically matching hash keys enables the detection of changes to tiles.

wrong_explanations.A: Having a log alone is not a control; reviewing the log for command line activities is a control.
wrong_explanations.C: Although access restriction through an access control tool may provide some level of control, the fact that developers already have command line access suggests that this control may be bypassed.
wrong_explanations.D: Removing the tools from the production environment may limit the ability to make unauthorized changes, but it does not address the risk of undetected changes or changes made through other means.

tips: Trap is A 'log commands' — detective only; logs don't prevent or detect software changes.
Trap is C 'access restriction tool' — preventive but assumes pre-approval; ad-hoc access still allowed.
Trap is D 'remove dev tools and compilers' — narrows attack surface but doesn't detect changes.
Hash key comparison detects ANY modification to programs. Independent of access controls; detects unauthorized changes regardless of how they happened. Best detective control for code integrity.

questions.question: A new application has been purchased from a vendor and is about to be implemented. Which of the following choices is a key consideration when implementing the application?

options.A: Preventing the compromise of the source code during the implementation process.
options.B: Ensuring that vendor default accounts and passwords have been disabled.
options.C: Removing the old copies of the program from escrow to avoid confusion.
options.D: Verifying that the vendor is meeting support and maintenance agreements.

questions.correct_explanation: Disabling vendor default accounts and passwords is a critical part of implementing a new application.

wrong_explanations.A: Protecting the executable or object code during the implementation process is essential to prevent compromise, rather than solely focusing on the source code.
wrong_explanations.C: Because this is a new application, there should not be any problem with older versions in escrow, making this consideration Jess relevant.
wrong_explanations.D: Although support and maintenance agreements are important, they may not be a key consideration during the initial implementation phase.

tips: Trap is A 'prevent source code compromise' — vendor's product, not customer concern.
Trap is C 'remove old escrow copies' — escrow strategy, not implementation.
Trap is D 'verify maintenance agreement' — operational concern, addressable.
Default vendor accounts (admin/admin, default passwords) are publicly documented. First action on any new application: disable defaults. Foundational security hardening step.

questions.question: The MAIN criterion for determining the severity level of a service disruption incident is:

options.A: cost of recovery.
options.B: negative public opinion.
options.C: geographic location.
options.D: downtime.

questions.correct_explanation: The longer the period of time a client cannot be serviced, the greater the severity (impact) of the incident.

wrong_explanations.A: The cost of recovery can be minimal, yet the service downtime can have a major impact.
wrong_explanations.B: Negative public opinion is a symptom of an incident; it is a factor in determining impact but not the most important one.
wrong_explanations.C: Geographic location does not determine the severity of the incident.

tips: Trap is A 'cost of recovery' — financial impact, secondary.
Trap is B 'negative public opinion' — reputational, real but not the primary metric.
Trap is C 'geographic location' — affects scope, not severity.
Severity = impact × duration. The longer service is disrupted, the worse. Downtime is the most direct measurable severity input.

questions.question: Doing which of the following during peak production hours can result in unexpected downtime?

options.A: Performing data migration
options.B: Performing preventive maintenance on electrical systems
options.C: Promoting applications from development to the staging environment
options.D: Reconfiguring a standby router in the data center

questions.correct_explanation: Preventive maintenance activities should be scheduled for nonpeak times of the day, and preferably during a maintenance window time period. A mishap or incident caused by a maintenance worker can result in unplanned downtime.

wrong_explanations.A: Performing data migration may impact performance but does not cause downtime.
wrong_explanations.C: Promoting applications into a staging environment (not production) should not affect system operations in any significant manner.
wrong_explanations.D: Reconfiguring a standby router should not cause unexpected downtime because the router is not operational and any problems should not affect network traffic.

tips: Trap is A 'data migration' — risky but planned and reversible if needed.
Trap is C 'promoting to staging' — not production; safe.
Trap is D 'reconfiguring standby router' — standby; production unaffected.
Electrical maintenance can fail unexpectedly; mistakes during peak hours = production outage. Maintenance = nonpeak windows, scheduled, with rollback. Peak production = no risk activities.

questions.question: During an HR audit, an information systems (IS) auditor is informed that there is a verbal agreement between the IT and HR departments about the level of IT services expected. In this situation, what should the IS auditor do FIRST?

options.A: Postpone the audit until the agreement is documented.
options.B: Report the existence of the undocumented agreement to senior management.
options.C: Confirm the content of the agreement with both departments.
options.D: Draft a service level agreement for the two departments.

questions.correct_explanation: An information systems (IS) auditor should first confirm and understand the current practice before making any recommendations. Part of this is to ensure that both parties agree with the terms of the agreement.

wrong_explanations.A: There is no reason to postpone an audit because a service agreement is not documented, unless that is all that is being audited. The agreement can be documented after it has been established that there is an agreement in place.
wrong_explanations.B: Reporting to senior management is not necessary at this stage of the audit because this is not a serious immediate vulnerability.
wrong_explanations.D: Drafting a service level agreement is not the IS auditor's responsibility.

tips: Trap is A 'postpone audit' — overreaction; audit can proceed with information gathering.
Trap is B 'report to senior management' — premature without confirmation.
Trap is D 'draft an SLA' — auditor doesn't draft business agreements.
Auditor's first job: understand current state. Confirm what the verbal agreement actually says with both parties. Then evaluate adequacy. Recommendations follow understanding.

questions.question: A database administrator (DBA) has identified a performance problem with some tables, which can be solved through denormalization. This situation will increase the risk of:

options.A: concurrent access.
options.B: deadlocks.
options.C: unauthorized access to data.
options.D: a loss of data integrity.

questions.correct_explanation: Denormalization compromises the structure that ensures data integrity, leading to an increased risk of data inconsistency and loss of data integrity.

wrong_explanations.A: Denormalization may impact other aspects of database performance or data consistency, but it does not directly increase the risk of concurrent access issues.
wrong_explanations.B: Although denormalization may have performance implications, it is not directly linked to an increased risk of deadlocks.
wrong_explanations.C: Unauthorized access to data is primarily addressed through access controls and security mechanisms, and denormalization does not directly impact this risk.

tips: Trap is A 'concurrent access' — performance/locking concern; denormalization may even reduce contention.
Trap is B 'deadlocks' — locking concern; denormalization typically reduces multi-table locking.
Trap is C 'unauthorized access' — access control concern; unrelated to schema design.
Denormalization stores duplicate data across tables. Update one copy, miss another = inconsistent data. Without strong update controls, integrity erodes.

questions.question: Which of the following processes should an information systems (IS) auditor recommend to assist in the recording of baselines for software releases?

options.A: user acceptance testing (UAT)
options.B: Backup and recovery
options.C: Incident management
options.D: Configuration management

questions.correct_explanation: The configuration management process may include automated tools that provide an automated recording of software release baselines. If the new release fails, the baseline will provide a point to which to return.

wrong_explanations.A: Although conducting user acceptance testing (UAT) is an important process in software development and release, it is not directly related to the recording of baselines for software releases. UAT may occur after the baselines have been established and serve as a validation step to ensure that the software meets the desired criteria.
wrong_explanations.B: Backup and recovery of the configuration are important, but not used to create the baseline.
wrong_explanations.C: Incident management will determine how to respond to an adverse event but is not related to recording baseline configurations.

tips: Trap is A 'UAT' — pre-release validation, not baseline recording.
Trap is B 'backup and recovery' — preserves data, not configuration baselines.
Trap is C 'incident management' — handles disruptions, not version recording.
Configuration management tracks WHAT was deployed, including baselines. Automated tools record release versions for rollback. Foundational for change control.

questions.question: The BEST method for assessing the effectiveness of a business continuity plan (BCP) is to review the:

options.A: plans and compare them to appropriate standards.
options.B: results from previous tests.
options.C: emergency procedures and employee training.
options.D: offsite storage and environmental controls.

questions.correct_explanation: Previous test results provide evidence of the effectiveness of the BCP.

wrong_explanations.A: Comparisons to standards gives some assurance that the plan addresses the critical aspects of a business continuity plan (BCP) but does not reveal anything about its effectiveness.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing emergency procedures provides insight into some aspects of the plan but falls short of providing assurance of the plan's overall effectiveness.
wrong_explanations.D: Reviewing offsite storage and environmental controls provide insight into some aspects of the plan but fall short of providing assurance of the plan overall effectiveness.

tips: Trap is A 'compare to standards' — checks adequacy on paper, not effectiveness.
Trap is C 'review emergency procedures' — examines documents, not actual performance.
Trap is D 'review offsite storage' — physical/environmental check, not BCP effectiveness.
Test results = empirical evidence. Did the BCP actually work? What failed? What worked? Tests are the only objective measure of effectiveness.

questions.question: With respect to business continuity strategies, an information systems (IS) auditor interviews key stakeholders in an organization to determine whether they understand their roles and responsibilities. The IS auditor is attempting to evaluate the:

options.A: clarity and simplicity of the business continuity plans (BCPs).
options.B: adequacy of the BCPs.
options.C: effectiveness of the BCPs.
options.D: ability of IS and end-user personnel to respond effectively in emergencies.

questions.correct_explanation: The information systems (IS) auditor should interview key stakeholders to evaluate how well they understand their roles and responsibilities. When all stakeholders have a detailed understanding of their roles and responsibilities in the event of a disaster, an IS auditor can deem the business continuity plan to be clear and simple.

wrong_explanations.B: To evaluate adequacy, the IS auditor should review the plans and compare them to appropriate standards and the results of tests of the plan.
wrong_explanations.C: To evaluate effectiveness, the IS auditor should review the results from previous tests or incidents. This is the best determination for the evaluation of effectiveness. An understanding of roles and responsibilities by key stakeholders will assist in ensuring the BCP is effective.
wrong_explanations.D: To evaluate the response, the IS auditor should review results of continuity tests. This will provide the IS auditor with assurance that target and recovery times are met. Emergency procedures and employee training need to be reviewed to determine whether the organization has implemented plans to allow for an effective response.

tips: Trap is B 'adequacy' — assessed by reviewing plans against standards, not interviewing.
Trap is C 'effectiveness' — assessed via test results.
Trap is D 'response ability' — assessed through actual exercises.
Stakeholder understanding tests CLARITY. If stakeholders can articulate their roles and responsibilities, the BCP communicates clearly. Confused stakeholders = unclear plan.

questions.question: During the design of a business continuity plan (BCP), the business impact analysis (BIA) identifies critical processes and supporting applications. This will PRIMARILY influence the:

options.A: responsibility for maintaining the BCP.
options.B: criteria for selecting a recovery site provider.
options.C: recovery strategy.
options.D: responsibilities of key personnel.

questions.correct_explanation: The most appropriate strategy is selected based on the relative risk level, timelines and criticality identified in the business impact analysis (BIA).

wrong_explanations.A: The responsibility for maintaining the business continuity plan (BCP) is decided after the selection or design of the appropriate recovery strategy and development of the plan.
wrong_explanations.B: The criteria for selecting a recovery site provider are decided after the selection or design of the appropriate recovery strategy.
wrong_explanations.D: The responsibilities of key personnel are depided after the selection or design of the appropriate recovery strategy during the plan development phase.

tips: Trap is A 'BCP maintenance responsibility' — operational concern, comes after strategy.
Trap is B 'recovery site provider' — implementation detail, follows strategy.
Trap is D 'key personnel responsibilities' — assignment, follows strategy.
BIA quantifies criticality and recovery timelines. Strategy decides HOW to recover (hot/warm/cold/reciprocal/cloud) based on those numbers. Strategy choice is BIA-driven.

questions.question: During a review of a business continuity plan (BCP), an information systems (IS) auditor noticed that the point at which a situation is declared to be a crisis has not been defined. The MAJOR risk associated with this is that:

options.A: response and recovery actions are initiated too early.
options.B: activating the appropriate response and recovery actions are delayed during a crisis.
options.C: crisis situations may be underestimated or overlooked.
options.D: the BCP may become too rigid.

questions.correct_explanation: The absence of a clear definition for declaring a situation as a crisis creates the risk of delays in activating the appropriate response and recovery actions. Without a predefined threshold or criteria for identifying a crisis, there is uncertainty and potential confusion about when to escalate the response, mobilize resources and implement critical measures. This can lead to valuable time being lost, ineffective decision-making, and delays in mitigating the impacts of the crisis.

wrong_explanations.A: Without a defined threshold for declaring a crisis, there is a possibility that response and recovery actions may be initiated prematurely, resulting in unnecessary costs and disruptions. However, the likelihood of initiating actions too early is not as critical as the risk of delayed response in the absence of a clear crisis declaration.
wrong_explanations.C: In the absence of a defined point for declaring a crisis, there is a risk that crisis situations may be underestimated or overlooked. However, it is not as significant a concern as delayed reactions.
wrong_explanations.D: Without a defined crisis declaration point, there is a risk that the business continuity plan (BCP) may become too rigid. This can lead to unnecessary delays and inefficiencies in responding to incidents, because the plan may require adherence to predefined steps without considering the actual severity and impact of the situation. However, this risk is not as significant as the risk of delayed response.

tips: Trap is A 'response initiated too early' — opposite; vague threshold causes hesitation, not premature action.
Trap is C 'crisis underestimated' — possible but downstream of activation delay.
Trap is D 'BCP too rigid' — vagueness creates flexibility, not rigidity.
Without a defined trigger, decision-makers hesitate. Should we activate? Is it bad enough? Time wasted = more damage. Clear thresholds enable quick activation when warranted.

questions.question: An organization has just completed its annual risk assessment. Regarding the business continuity plan (BCP), what should an information systems (IS) auditor recommend as the next step for the organization?

options.A: Review and evaluate the BCP for adequacy.
options.B: Perform a full simulation of the BCP.
options.C: Train and educate employees regarding the BCP.
options.D: Notify critical contacts in the BCP.

questions.correct_explanation: The business continuity plan (BCP) should be reviewed every time a risk assessment is completed for the organization.

wrong_explanations.B: Performing a simulation should be completed after the BCP has been deemed adequate for the organization.
wrong_explanations.C: Training of the employees should be performed after the BCP has been deemed adequate for the organization.
wrong_explanations.D: There is no reason to notify the BCP contacts at this time.

tips: Trap is B 'full simulation' — premature; review adequacy first.
Trap is C 'train and educate' — operational, follows BCP review.
Trap is D 'notify critical contacts' — emergency action, not annual maintenance.
Annual risk assessment may surface new risks the BCP doesn't address. Review BCP adequacy first; update before testing or training. Plan must reflect current risk landscape.

questions.question: Which of the following database controls ensure that the integrity of transactions is maintained in an online transaction processing system's database?

options.A: Authentication controls
options.B: Data normalization controls
options.C: Read/write access log controls
options.D: Commitment and rollback controls

questions.correct_explanation: Commitment and rollback controls are directly relevant to integrity. These controls ensure that database operations that form a logical transaction unit will be completed entirely or not at all (i.e., if, for some reason, a transaction cannot be fully completed, then incomplete inserts/updates/deletes are rolled back so that the database returns to its pretransition state).

wrong_explanations.A: Authentication controls ensure that only authorized personnel can make changes but do not ensure the integrity of the changes.
wrong_explanations.B: Data normalization is not used to protect the integrity of online transactions.
wrong_explanations.C: Log controls are a detective control but do not ensure the integrity of the data in the database.

tips: Trap is A 'authentication controls' — confidentiality, not transaction integrity.
Trap is B 'data normalization' — design optimization, not transactional integrity.
Trap is C 'access log controls' — detective audit trail, not integrity.
Commitment and rollback controls implement atomicity: transaction completes fully or doesn't happen. Database stays consistent across the transaction boundary. Foundational for OLTP integrity.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds that the data warehouse query performance decreases significantly at certain times of the day. Which of the following controls are MOST relevant for the IS auditor to review?

options.A: Permanent table-space allocation
options.B: Commitment and rollback controls
options.C: User spool and database limit controls
options.D: Read/write access log controls

questions.correct_explanation: User spool limits restrict the space available for running user queries. This prevents poorly formed queries from consuming excessive system resources and impacting general query performance. Limiting the space available to users in their own databases prevents them from building excessively large tables. This helps to control space utilization, which itself acts to help performance by maintaining a buffer between the actual data volume stored and the physical device capacity. Additionally, it prevents users from consuming excessive resources in ad hoc table builds (as opposed to scheduled production loads that often can run overnight and are optimized for performance purposes). In a data warehouse, because online transactions are not being run, commitment and rollback does not have an impact on performance.

wrong_explanations.A: Table-space allocation does not affect performance at different times of the day.
wrong_explanations.B: Commitment and rollback only apply to errors or failures and will not affect performance at different times of the day.
wrong_explanations.D: Read/write access log controls do not affect performance at different times of the day.

tips: Trap is A 'permanent table-space allocation' — storage layout, not query performance.
Trap is B 'commitment/rollback' — transactional, not query throttling.
Trap is D 'access log controls' — detective auditing, not performance.

User spool limits cap how much space individual queries can consume. Without limits, one bad query can starve others. Time-of-day performance pattern often comes from heavy users running unconstrained queries.

questions.question: In a small organization, developers may release emergency changes directly to production. Which of the following will BEST control the risk in this situation?

options.A: Approve and document the emergency changes promptly after release.
options.B: Implement a segregated environment for production access and restrict developer access outside of specific time frames.
options.C: Implement a defined emergency change management process that includes secondary approval.
options.D: Implement strict access controls and permissions on the production machine to prevent unauthorized changes.

questions.correct_explanation: It may be appropriate to allow programmers to make emergency changes if they are documented and approved after the fact.

wrong_explanations.B: Limiting developer access to production within specific time frames may help establish some controls, but it does not directly address the risk of unauthorized or unapproved emergency changes.
wrong_explanations.C: Obtaining secondary approval before releasing to production is not as critical in an emergency situation as documenting the changes promptly.
wrong_explanations.D: Disabling the compiler option in the production machine is not directly related to controlling the risk of emergency changes. It is more focused on preventing unauthorized code modifications. Although access controls are important, they should be implemented alongside proper change management processes.

tips: Trap is B 'segregated environment + restricted developer time' — operationally complex; doesn't address the post-release approval gap.
Trap is C 'emergency change process with secondary approval' — pre-approval would defeat 'emergency' nature.
Trap is D 'strict access controls' — preventive but means emergency changes can't happen at all.
Emergency changes by definition skip pre-approval. Compensating control: rigorous post-release approval and documentation. Captures what was done; ensures justification exists.

questions.question: Of the following alternatives, the FIRST approach to developing a disaster recovery strategy is to assess whether:

options.A: all threats can be completely removed.
options.B: a cost-effective, built-in resilience can be implemented.
options.C: the recovery time objective (RTO) can be optimized.
options.D: the cost of recovery can be minimized.

questions.correct_explanation: It is critical to initially identify information assets that can be made more resilient to disasters (e.g., diverse routing, alternate paths or multiple communication carriers). Preventing a problem is always better than planning to address a problem when it happens.

wrong_explanations.A: It is impossible to remove all existing and future threats.
wrong_explanations.C: The optimization of the recovery time objective (RTO) comes later in the development of the disaster recovery strategy.
wrong_explanations.D: Efforts to minimize the cost of recovery come later in the development of the disaster recovery strategy.

tips: Trap is A 'remove all threats' — impossible; threats can't all be eliminated.
Trap is C 'optimize RTO' — comes after determining baseline resilience.
Trap is D 'minimize recovery cost' — efficiency goal, follows from resilience design.

DRP strategy starts with: can we make the infrastructure naturally resilient? Diverse routing, redundancy, geographic distribution prevent disasters from happening. Built-in resilience is cheaper than recovery.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor determined that the IT manager recently changed the vendor that is responsible for performing maintenance on critical computer systems to cut costs. Although the new vendor is less expensive, the new maintenance contract specifies a change in incident resolution time specified by the original vendor. Which of the following should be the GREATEST concern to the IS auditor?

options.A: Disaster recovery plans (DRPs) may be invalid and need to be revised.
options.B: Transactional business data may be lost in the event of system failure.
options.C: The new maintenance vendor is not familiar with the organization's policies.
options.D: Application owners were not informed of the change.

questions.correct_explanation: The greatest risk of making a change to the maintenance of critical systems is that the change can have an adverse impact on a critical business process. Although there is a benefit in selecting a less expensive maintenance vendor, the resolution time must be aligned with the needs of the business.

wrong_explanations.A: Disaster recovery plans (DRPs) must support the needs of the business, but the greater risk is that application owners are not aware of the change in resolution time.
wrong_explanations.B: Transactional business data loss is determined by data backup frequency and, consequently, the backup schedule.
wrong_explanations.C: The vendor must abide by the terms of the contract and those should include compliance with the privacy policies of the organization, but the lack of application owner involvement is the most important concern.

tips: Trap is A 'DRP needs revision' — true but recoverable through document update.
Trap is B 'transactional data may be lost' — backup-related, addressable.
Trap is C 'vendor unfamiliar with policies' — operational training issue.

Application owners weren't informed = they couldn't assess whether new resolution time meets their critical-system needs. Decision made unilaterally about systems with business owners — governance failure.

questions.question: In the event of a data center disaster, which of the following is the MOST appropriate strategy to enable a complete recovery of a critical database?

options.A: Daily data backup to a remote site
options.B: Real-time replication to a remote site
options.C: Hard disk mirroring to a local server
options.D: Real-time data backup to the local storage area network

questions.correct_explanation: With real-time replication to a remote site, data are updated simultaneously in two separate locations; therefore, a disaster in one site does not damage the information located in the remote site. This assumes that both sites are not affected by the same disaster.

wrong_explanations.A: Daily backup recovery can result in the loss of data from a day's work of data.
wrong_explanations.C: Hard disk mirroring to a local server takes place in the same data center and can possibly be affected by the same disaster.
wrong_explanations.D: Real-time data backup to the local storage area network takes place in the same data center and can possibly be affected by the same disaster.

tips: Trap is A 'daily data backup to remote site' — daily lag = up to 24 hours of data loss.
Trap is C 'hard disk mirroring local server' — local; doesn't survive data center disaster.
Trap is D 'real-time backup to local SAN' — local; same vulnerability as the data center.
Real-time replication to a REMOTE site = up-to-second data preserved at geographically separate location. Survives data center disaster with no data loss.

questions.question: If the recovery time objective (RTO) increases:

options.A: the disaster tolerance increases.
options.B: the cost of recovery increases.
options.C: a cold site cannot be used.
options.D: the data backup frequency increases.

questions.correct_explanation: The longer the recovery time objective (RTO), the higher the disaster tolerance. The disaster tolerance is the amount of time the business can afford to be disrupted before resuming critical operations.

wrong_explanations.B: The longer the RTO, the lower the recovery cost.
wrong_explanations.C: It cannot be concluded that a cold site is inappropriate; with a longer RTO, the use of a cold site may become feasible.
wrong_explanations.D: RTO is not related to the frequency of data backups; it is related to recovery point objective.

tips: Trap is B 'cost increases' — opposite; longer RTO allows cheaper recovery (cold site, slower restore).
Trap is C 'cold site cannot be used' — opposite; longer RTO ENABLES cold sites.
Trap is D 'backup frequency increases' — RTO is about recovery time, not backup frequency.
RTO = time the business can wait for recovery. Longer RTO = business is more tolerant of disruption = higher disaster tolerance. Direct relationship.

questions.question: When developing a disaster recovery plan (DRP), what criteria should be considered when determining the acceptable downtime?

options.A: Annual loss expectancy
options.B: Service delivery objective
options.C: Quantity of orphan data
options.D: Maximum tolerable outage (MTO)

questions.correct_explanation: Recovery time objective (RTO) is determined based on the acceptable downtime in the case of a disruption of operations. It indicates the maximum tolerable outage (MTO) that an organization considers to be acceptable before a system or process must resume following a disaster.

wrong_explanations.A: The acceptable downtime is not determined by the annual loss expectancy (ALE); ALE is related to risk management calculations, not disaster recovery.
wrong_explanations.B: The service delivery objective is relevant to business continuity, but it is not determined by acceptable downtime.
wrong_explanations.C: The quantity of orphan data is relevant to business continuity, but it is not determined by acceptable downtime.

tips: Trap is A 'annual loss expectancy' — financial measure, not downtime.
Trap is B 'service delivery objective' — describes service level during recovery, not duration.
Trap is C 'orphan data quantity' — data quality concern, not downtime measure.
Maximum tolerable outage (MTO) = the absolute maximum the business can endure. RTO must be ≤ MTO. MTO is the foundational input for downtime decisions.

questions.question: When reviewing an enterprise's preventive maintenance process for systems at a data center, what is the MOST important practice that should be in place for an information systems (IS) auditor to be able to ensure that adequate maintenance is being performed on all critical computing, power and cooling systems?

options.A: Proper background checks on all service personnel are conducted.
options.B: Service personnel are escorted at all times when performing their work.
options.C: Maintenance is scheduled during noncritical processing times.
options.D: Verification of maintenance being performed is done independently.

questions.correct_explanation: Independent verification confirms documented maintenance activities, ensuring their effectiveness in sustaining critical systems. It provides assurance and detects any maintenance process gaps or deficiencies.

wrong_explanations.A: Although the trustworthiness of the service personnel is important, it is normal practice for these individuals to be escorted and supervised by the data center personnel. It is also expected that the service provider performs this background check, not the customer.
wrong_explanations.B: Escorting service personnel is common and a good practice, but the greater risk in this case is if work is performed during critical processing times.
wrong_explanations.C: The biggest risk to normal operations in a data center is if an incident or mishap were to happen during critical peak processing times; therefore, it is prudent to ensure that no type of system maintenance is performed at these critical times.

tips: Trap is A 'background checks on personnel' — HR control, doesn't verify maintenance work.
Trap is B 'escort service personnel' — physical control, doesn't verify maintenance happened.
Trap is C 'noncritical processing times' — scheduling control.
Independent verification of maintenance work = objective assurance that maintenance was actually performed. Vendor reports alone are self-attestation; independent verification catches gaps.

questions.question: Which of the following backup techniques is the MOST appropriate when an organization requires extremely granular data restore points, as defined in the recovery point objective (RPO)?

options.A: Virtual tape libraries
options.B: Disk-based snapshots
options.C: Continuous data backup
options.D: Disk-to-tape backup

questions.correct_explanation: Recovery point objective (RPO) is based on the acceptable data loss in the case of a disruption. In this scenario, the organization needs a short RPO and continuous data backup is the best option.

wrong_explanations.A: Virtual tape libraries require time to complete the backup, while continuous data backup happens online (in real time).
wrong_explanations.B: Disk-based snapshots require time to complete the backup and lose some data between the times of the backup and the failure, while continuous data backup happens online (in real time).
wrong_explanations.D: Disk-to-tape backup requires time to complete the backup, while continuous data backup happens online (in real time).

tips: Trap is A 'virtual tape libraries' — improves tape backup but typically scheduled, not granular.
Trap is B 'disk-based snapshots' — scheduled snapshots, time-interval granularity.
Trap is D 'disk-to-tape backup' — slower medium, scheduled.
Continuous data backup captures every change as it happens. Restore point can be any moment in time = maximum granularity. Required when RPO must be very low.

questions.question: A lower recovery time objective (RTO) results in:

options.A: higher disaster tolerance.
options.B: higher cost.
options.C: reduced system interruptions.
options.D: more permissive data loss.

questions.correct_explanation: recovery time objective (RTO) is based on the acceptable down time in case of a disruption of operations. The lower the RTO, the higher the cost of recovery strategies.

wrong_explanations.A: Disaster tolerance relates to the length ohime that critical business processes can be interrupted. A higher disaster tolerance allows for a longer outage and, therefore, longer recovery time.
wrong_explanations.C: The lower the disaster tolerance, the narrower the interruption window. The interruption window is the length of the outage of critical processes.
wrong_explanations.D: Pennissive data loss relates to recovery point objective (RPO), not disaster tolerance.

tips: Trap is A 'higher disaster tolerance' — opposite; lower RTO = lower tolerance.
Trap is C 'reduced interruptions' — recovery speed doesn't reduce interruption frequency.
Trap is D 'more permissive data loss' — that's RPO concern, not RTO.
Faster recovery = more expensive infrastructure (hot sites, real-time replication, dedicated capacity). The cost curve rises sharply for very low RTOs.

questions.question: During an implementation review of a recent application deployment, it was determined that several incidents were assigned incorrect priorities and, because of this, failed to meet the business service level agreement (SLA). What is the GREATEST concern?

options.A: The support model was not approved by senior management.
options.B: The incident resolution of time specified in the SLA is not realistic.
options.C: There are inadequate resources to support the applications.
options.D: The support model was poorly developed and implemented contributing to inaccurate prioritization and SLA failures.

questions.correct_explanation: The greatest concern for the information systems (IS) auditor is that the support model was not developed and implemented correctly to prevent or react to potential outages. Incidents can cost the business a significant amount of money and a support model should be implemented with the project. This should be a step within the system development life cycle (SDLC) and procedures and, if it is missed on one project, it may be a symptom of an overall breakdown in process.

wrong_explanations.A: Although senior management involvement is important, the more critical issue is whether the support model was not properly developed and implemented.
wrong_explanations.B: Although the incident resolution time specified in the service level agreement (SLA) may not always be attainable, the more critical issue is whether the support model was not properly developed and implemented.
wrong_explanations.C: Although adequate support resources are important, the more critical issue is whether the support model was not properly developed and implemented.

tips: Trap is A 'support model not approved by senior management' — governance gap, not the central problem.
Trap is B 'SLA resolution time unrealistic' — possible cause but not necessarily the issue.
Trap is C 'inadequate resources' — capacity concern, not prioritization design.
Support model design determines how incidents get prioritized. Faulty design = consistent prioritization errors = SLA failures across many incidents. Systemic cause.

questions.question: What is the BEST backup strategy for a large database with data supporting online sales?

options.A: Weekly full backup with daily incremental backup
options.B: Daily full backup
options.C: Clustered servers
options.D: Mirrored hard disks

questions.correct_explanation: Mirrored hard disks ensure that all data are backed up to more than one disk so that a failure of one disk will not result in loss of data,

wrong_explanations.A: Weekly full backup and daily incremental backup is a poor backup strategy for online transactions. Because this system supports online sales, it can be difficult to recreate lost data and this solution may result in a loss of up to one day's worth of data.
wrong_explanations.B: A full backup normally requires a couple of hours, and, therefore, it can be impractical to conduct a full backup every day.
wrong_explanations.C: Clustered servers provide a redundant processing capability but are not a backup.

tips: Trap is A 'weekly full + daily incremental' — restore involves replaying daily increments; slow.
Trap is B 'daily full backup' — operationally infeasible for large databases.
Trap is C 'clustered servers' — high availability but not backup; failure of cluster = no backup.
Mirrored hard disks = real-time data duplication. Both disks have current data; loss of one disk doesn't lose data. Best for large always-online databases.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor notes during an audit that an organization's business continuity plan (BCP) does not adequately address information confidentiality during the recovery process. The IS auditor should recommend that the plan be modified to include:

options.A: the level of information security required when business recovery procedures are invoked.
options.B: information security roles and responsibilities in the crisis management structure.
options.C: information security resource requirements.
options.D: change management procedures for information security that can affect business continuity arrangements.

questions.correct_explanation: Clearly define the level of information security required when invoking business recovery procedures to ensure confidentiality is maintained.

wrong_explanations.B: During a time of crisis, the security needs of the organization may increase because many usual controls such as segregation/separation of duties (SoD) are missing. Having security roles in the crisis management plan is important, but that is not the best answer to this scenario.
wrong_explanations.C: Identifying the resource requirements for information security, as part of the business continuity plan (BCP), is important, but it is more important to set out the security levels that are required for protected information.
wrong_explanations.D: Change management procedures can help keep a BCP up to date but are not relevant to this scenario.

tips: Trap is B 'roles in crisis management' — staffing concern, not security level.
Trap is C 'security resource requirements' — operational, not the BCP gap.
Trap is D 'change management procedures' — process, not the recovery security level.
BCP must specify the LEVEL of security required during recovery. Otherwise, recovery shortcuts may compromise confidentiality. Define security expectations before declaring recovery complete.

questions.question: During a disaster recovery test, an information systems (IS) auditor observes that the performance of the disaster recovery site's server is slow. To find the root cause of this, the IS auditor should FIRST review the:

options.A: event error log generated at the disaster recovery site.
options.B: disaster recovery test plan.
options.C: disaster recovery plan (DRP).
options.D: configurations and alignment of the primary and disaster recovery sites.

questions.correct_explanation: Because the configuration of the system is the most probable cause, the IS auditor should review that first.

wrong_explanations.A: If the issue cannot be clarified, the information systems (IS) auditor should then review the event error log.
wrong_explanations.B: The disaster recovery test plan does not identify any issues related to system performance unless the test was poorly designed and inefficient, but that would come after checking the configuration.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing the disaster recovery plan (DRP) is unlikely to provide any information about system performance issues.

tips: Trap is A 'event error log' — useful but symptomatic; configuration issue may not show in errors.
Trap is B 'DR test plan' — describes what to test, doesn't diagnose performance.
Trap is C 'DRP itself' — too broad; doesn't isolate performance.
Performance differences between primary and DR sites usually trace to configuration differences. Comparing configurations finds the discrepancy that's slowing the DR site.

questions.question: What is the GREATEST risk associated with inadequate management of storage growth in a critical file server?

options.A: Backup time steadily increases.
options.B: Backup operational costs significantly increase.
options.C: Storage operational costs significantly increase.
options.D: Server recovery work may not meet the recovery time objective (RTO).

questions.correct_explanation: In case of a crash, recovering a server with an extensive amount of data can require a significant amount of time. If the recovery cannot meet the RTO, there will be a discrepancy in IT strategies. It is important to ensure that server restoration can meet the RTO.

wrong_explanations.A: Backup time may increase, but that can be managed. The most important issue is the time taken to recover the data.
wrong_explanations.B: The backup cost issues are not as significant as not meeting the recovery time objective (RTO).
wrong_explanations.C: The storage cost issues are not as significant as not meeting the RTO.

tips: Trap is A 'backup time increases' — operational concern, manageable.
Trap is B 'backup costs increase' — financial concern, predictable.
Trap is C 'storage costs increase' — same; predictable financial impact.
Uncontrolled storage growth means recovery TIME grows. Eventually, recovery exceeds RTO; the system can't be recovered fast enough. Strategic capacity gap.

questions.question: An organization has a business process with a recovery time objective (RTO) equal to zero and a recovery point objective (RPO) close to one minute. This implies that the process can tolerate:

options.A: a data loss of up to one minute, but the processing must be continuous.
options.B: a one-minute processing interruption but cannot tolerate any data loss.
options.C: a processing interruption of one minute or more.
options.D: both a data loss and processing interruption longer than one minute.

questions.correct_explanation: The recovery time objective (RTO) measures organization tolerance for downtime, and the recoverypoint objective (RPO) measures how much data loss can be accepted.

wrong_explanations.B: A processing interruption of one minute exceeds the zero RTO set by the organization.
wrong_explanations.C: A processing interruption of one minute or more exceeds the continuous availability requirements of an RTO of zero.
wrong_explanations.D: An RPO of one minute only allows data loss of one minute.

tips: Trap is B 'one-minute interruption, no data loss' — RTO=0 means no interruption tolerated.
Trap is C 'interruption of one minute or more' — same; RTO=0 forbids interruption.
Trap is D 'data loss AND interruption longer than one minute' — both forbidden.
RTO=0 means processing must continue without break. RPO=1 minute means up to 1 minute of data can be lost. Continuous processing + small recoverable data window.

questions.question: Which of the following issues should be the GREATEST concern to the information systems (IS) auditor when reviewing an IT disaster recovery test?

options.A: Due to the limited test time window, only the most essential systems were tested, and other systems were tested separately during the rest of the year.
options.B: During the test, some of the backup systems were defective or not working, causing the test of these systems to fail.
options.C: The procedures to shut down and secure the original production site before starting the backup site required far more time than planned.
options.D: Every year, the same employees perform the test, and the recovery plan documents are not used because every step is well known by all participants.

questions.correct_explanation: The purpose of the test is to test the backup plan. When the backup systems are not working, then the plan cannot be counted on in a real disaster. This is the most serious problem.

wrong_explanations.A: This is not a concern because over the course of the year, all the systems were tested.
wrong_explanations.C: In a real disaster, there is no need for a clean shutdown of the original production environment because the first priority is to bring the backup site up.
wrong_explanations.D: A disaster recovery test should test the plan, processes, people and IT systems. Therefore, if the plan is not used, its accuracy and adequacy cannot be verified. Disaster recovery should not rely on key staff because a disaster can occur when they are not available. However, the fact that the test works is less serious than the failure of the systems and infrastructure that the recovery plan counts on. Good practice rotates different people through the test and ensures that the plan itself is followed and tested.

tips: Trap is A 'limited test window' — manageable through phased testing throughout the year.
Trap is C 'shutdown procedures take longer than planned' — process issue, addressable.
Trap is D 'same employees test, plan not used' — concerning but plan still works.
Defective backup systems = recovery is impossible regardless of plan quality. Defeats the purpose of backup. Most serious test finding because it means real recovery would fail.

questions.question: What component requires frequent updating to ensure the continued effectiveness of a disaster recovery plan (DRP)?

options.A: Contact information of key personnel
