options.B: Server inventory documentation
options.C: Individual roles and responsibilities
options.D: Procedures for declaring a disaster

questions.correct_explanation: In the event of a disaster, it is important to have a current updated list of personnel who are key to the operation of the plan.

wrong_explanations.B: Asset inventory is important and should be linked to the change management process of the organization, but having access to key people may compensate for outdated records.
wrong_explanations.C: Individual roles and responsibilities are important, but, in a disaster, many people can fill different roles depending on their experience.
wrong_explanations.D: The procedures for declaring a disaster are important because they can affect response, customer perception and regulatory issues, but not as important as having the right people there when needed.

tips: Trap is B 'server inventory' — should be linked to change management; not as time-sensitive as people.
Trap is C 'roles and responsibilities' — relatively stable; less frequent changes.
Trap is D 'declaration procedures' — designed once; doesn't change frequently.
Personnel turnover is constant. Contact info goes stale fastest. In a real disaster, outdated phone numbers = inability to reach key people. Most urgent maintenance item.

questions.question: A live test of a mutual agreement for IT system recovery was carried out, including a four-hour test of intensive usage by the business units. The test was successful, but gives only partial assurance that the:

options.A: system and the IT operations team can sustain operations in the emergency environment.
options.B: resources and the environment can sustain the transaction load.
options.C: connectivity to the applications at the remote site meets response time requirements.
options.D: workflow of actual business operations can use the emergency system in case of a disaster.

questions.correct_explanation: The live test of the mutual agreement for IT system recovery, including the intensive usage by business units, only partially ensures that the workflow of actual business operations can use the emergency system in case of a disaster.

wrong_explanations.A: The applications have been operated intensively, but the capability of the system and the IT operations team to sustain and support this environment (ancillary operations, batch closing, error corrections, output distribution, etc.) is only partially tested.
wrong_explanations.B: Because the test involved intensive usage, the backup seems to be able to handle the transaction load.
wrong_explanations.C: Because users were able to connect to and use the system, the response time must have been satisfactory.

tips: Trap is A 'IT operations sustains operations' — partially tested through usage simulation.
Trap is B 'resources sustain transaction load' — tested through intensive usage.
Trap is C 'connectivity meets response time' — tested through usage.
4-hour intensive test simulates business workload but DOESN'T fully verify the workflow. Real disasters expose workflow gaps that usage tests miss. Live test gives PARTIAL — not complete — assurance.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important consideration when defining recovery point objectives (RPOs)?

options.A: Minimum operating requirements
options.B: Acceptable data loss
options.C: Mean time between failures
options.D: Acceptable time for recovery

questions.correct_explanation: Recovery point objectives (RPOs) are the level of data Joss/reworking an organization is willing to accept.

wrong_explanations.A: Minimum operating requirements help define recovery strategies.
wrong_explanations.C: Mean time between failures helps define likelihood of system failure.
wrong_explanations.D: Recovery time objectives (RTOs) are the acceptable time delay in availability of business operations.

tips: Trap is A 'minimum operating requirements' — capacity concern, not data preservation.
Trap is C 'mean time between failures' — reliability metric, not recovery point.
Trap is D 'acceptable time for recovery' — that's RTO, not RPO.
RPO directly measures acceptable data loss in time. Defines how recent the recovered data must be. Foundational input for backup strategy and RPO selection.

questions.question: To address an organization's disaster recovery requirements, backup intervals should not exceed the:

options.A: service level objective.
options.B: recovery time objective (RTO).
options.C: recovery point objective (RPO).
options.D: maximum acceptable outage (MAO).

questions.correct_explanation: The maximum acceptable outage (MAO) is the maximum amount of system downtime that is tolerable. It can be used as a synonym for maximum tolerable period of disruption or maximum allowable downtime. However, the RTO denotes an objective/target, while the MAO constitutes a vital necessity for an organization's survival.

wrong_explanations.A: Organizations try to set service level objective to meet established business targets. The resulting time for the service level agreement (SLA) relates to recovery of services, not to recovery of data.
wrong_explanations.B: The recovery time objective (RTO) defines the time period after the disaster in which normal business functionality needs to be restored.
wrong_explanations.C: Recovery point objective (RPO) defines the point in time to which data must be restored after a disaster to resume processing transactions. Backups should be performed in a way that the latest backup is no older than this maximum time frame. If the backups are not done frequently enough, then too much data are likely to be lost.

tips: Trap is A 'service level objective' — service-quality goal, not data-preservation interval.
Trap is B 'RTO' — recovery time, not data preservation.
Trap is C 'RPO' — close, but RPO is the data-loss target; backups may need to be more frequent to meet it.
MAO = absolute maximum downtime tolerable. Backups must complete more often than this; if backup interval > MAO, the org can't recover within tolerance window. Hard ceiling.

questions.question: The FIRST step in the execution of a problem management mechanism should be:

options.A: issue analysis.
options.B: exception ranking.
options.C: exception reporting.
options.D: root cause analysis.

questions.correct_explanation: The reporting of operational issues is normally the first step in tracking problems.

wrong_explanations.A: Analysis and resolution are performed after logging and triage have been performed.
wrong_explanations.B: Exception ranking can only be performed after the exceptions have been reported.
wrong_explanations.D: Root cause analysis is performed after the exceptions have been identified and is not normally the first part of problem management.

tips: Trap is A 'issue analysis' — comes after reporting.
Trap is B 'exception ranking' — comes after reporting.
Trap is D 'root cause analysis' — comes after analysis.
Problem management starts with VISIBILITY. Exception reports identify what went wrong. Without reports, problems don't enter the management process. Reporting is step one.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST supports 24/7 availability?

options.A: Daily backup
options.B: Offsite storage
options.C: Mirroring
options.D: Periodic testing

questions.correct_explanation: Mirroring of critical elements is a tool that facilitates immediate (failover) recoverability.

wrong_explanations.A: Daily backup implies that it is reasonable for restoration to take place within a number of hours but not immediately.
wrong_explanations.B: Offsite storage does not, itself, support continuous availability.
wrong_explanations.D: Periodic testing of systems does not, itself, support continuous availability.

tips: Trap is A 'daily backup' — doesn't help during the day; downtime occurs.
Trap is B 'offsite storage' — protects data, doesn't ensure availability.
Trap is D 'periodic testing' — verifies recovery, doesn't prevent downtime.
Mirroring = real-time copy with automatic failover. If primary fails, secondary takes over instantly. Foundation of 24/7 availability.

questions.question: The PRIMARY purpose of implementing redundant array of inexpensive disks (RAID) level 1 in a file server is to:

options.A: achieve performance improvement.
options.B: provide user authentication.
options.C: ensure availability of data.
options.D: ensure the confidentiality of data.

questions.correct_explanation: RAID level 1 provides disk mirroring. Data written to one disk are also written to another disk. Users in the network access data on the first disk; if disk one fails, the second disk takes over. This redundancy ensures the availability of data.

wrong_explanations.A: redundant array of inexpensive disks (RAID) level 1 does not improve performance. It writes the data to two separate disk drives.
wrong_explanations.B: RAID level 1 has no relevance to authentication.
wrong_explanations.D: RAID level 1 does nothing to provide for data confidentiality.

tips: Trap is A 'performance improvement' — RAID 1 doesn't improve write performance.
Trap is B 'user authentication' — RAID has nothing to do with authentication.
Trap is D 'confidentiality' — RAID doesn't encrypt or hide data.
RAID 1 = disk mirroring. Same data on two disks. Disk failure doesn't lose data; the second disk continues. Availability is RAID 1's primary purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important criterion when selecting a location for an offsite storage facility for information systems (IS) backup files? The offsite facility must be:

options.A: physically separated from the data center and not subject to the same risk.
options.B: given the same level of protection as that of the computer data center.
options.C: outsourced to a reliable third party.
options.D: equipped with surveillance capabilities.

questions.correct_explanation: It is important that there is an offsite storage location for information systems (IS) files and that it is in a location not subject to the same risk as the primary data center.

wrong_explanations.B: The offsite location may be shared with other organizations and, therefore, have an even higher level of protection than the primary data center.
wrong_explanations.C: An offsite location may be owned by a third party or by the organization itself.
wrong_explanations.D: Physical protection is important but not as important as not being affected by the same crisis.

tips: Trap is B 'same protection level as data center' — desirable but not the most important criterion.
Trap is C 'outsourced to third party' — operational choice, not selection criterion.
Trap is D 'surveillance capabilities' — security feature, secondary.
Offsite storage's PURPOSE is to protect against the same disaster that hits the data center. Physical separation + different risk exposure = the offsite location actually serves its function.

questions.question: If a database is restored using before-image dumps, where should the process begin following an interruption?

options.A: Before the last transaction
options.B: After the last transaction
options.C: At the first transaction after the latest checkpoint
options.D: At the last transaction before the latest checkpoint

questions.correct_explanation: When using before images, it is important to note that the last transaction in the dump may not have updated the database before the dump was taken.

wrong_explanations.B: The last transaction will not have updated the database and must be reprocessed.
wrong_explanations.C: Program checkpoints are irrelevant in this situation. Checkpoints are used in application failures.
wrong_explanations.D: Program checkpoints are irrelevant in this situation. Checkpoints are used in application failures.

tips: Trap is B 'after the last transaction' — last transaction may not have committed; would skip it.
Trap is C 'first transaction after latest checkpoint' — checkpoint logic for forward recovery, not before-image.
Trap is D 'last transaction before latest checkpoint' — too far back; redo more than necessary.
Before-image recovery: the last transaction in the dump may not have committed. Restart BEFORE it to ensure data integrity. Conservative choice; redo if necessary.

questions.question: In addition to the backup considerations for all systems, which of the following is an important consideration in providing backup for online systems?

options.A: Maintaining system software parameters
options.B: Ensuring periodic dumps of transaction logs
options.C: Ensuring grandfather-father-son file backups
options.D: Maintaining important data at an offsite location

questions.correct_explanation: Regular transaction log dumps are vital to preserving timely data in online systems, acting as a crucial backup to prevent data loss. Given the high activity volume in online systems, the traditional backup method may not be feasible.

wrong_explanations.A: Maintaining system software parameters is important for all systems, not just online systems.
wrong_explanations.C: Having generations of backups is a good practice for all systems.
wrong_explanations.D: All backups should consider offsite storage at a location that is accessible but not likely to be affected by the same disaster.

tips: Trap is A 'system software parameters' — configuration management, applies to all systems.
Trap is C 'grandfather-father-son backups' — backup rotation strategy, applies to all systems.
Trap is D 'data offsite' — offsite storage, applies to all systems.
Online systems have continuous transactions. Periodic transaction log dumps capture what's happened since the last full backup. Without log dumps, online systems lose recent transactions in recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following disaster recovery testing techniques is the MOST efficient way to determine the effectiveness of the plan?

options.A: Preparedness tests
options.B: Paper tests
options.C: Full operational tests
options.D: Actual service disruption

questions.correct_explanation: Preparedness tests involve simulation of the entire environment (in phases) at a relatively low cost and help the team to better understand and prepare for the actual test scenario.

wrong_explanations.B: Paper tests in a walk-through test the entire plan, but there is no simulation and less is learned. It also is difficult to obtain evidence that the team has understood the test plan.
wrong_explanations.C: Full operational tests require approval from management, are not easy or practical to test in most scenarios and may trigger a real disaster.
wrong_explanations.D: An actual service disruption is not recommended in most cases unless required by regulation or policy.

tips: Trap is B 'paper tests' — discussion only; no actual simulation.
Trap is C 'full operational tests' — most thorough but expensive and disruptive.
Trap is D 'actual service disruption' — disruptive; tests in real conditions but at high risk.
Preparedness tests simulate the entire DR scenario in phases at relatively low cost. Effective at finding gaps without the disruption of full operational testing. Best efficiency per insight.

questions.question: Online banking transactions are being posted to the database when processing suddenly comes to a halt. The integrity of the transaction processing is BEST ensured by:

options.A: database integrity checks.
options.B: validation checks.
options.C: input controls.
options.D: database commits and rollbacks.

questions.correct_explanation: Database commits save completed transaction processing, while rollback reverses partially completed transaction processing if the transaction fails.

wrong_explanations.A: Database integrity checks are important to ensure database consistency and accuracy. These include isolation, concurrency and durability controls, but the most important issue here is atomicity-the requirement for transactions to complete entirely and commit, or else roll back to the last known good point.
wrong_explanations.B: Validation checks prevent introduction of corrupt data but do not address system failure.
wrong_explanations.C: Input controls are important to protect the integrity of input data but do not address system failure.

tips: Trap is A 'database integrity checks' — runs periodically; doesn't address mid-transaction failures.
Trap is B 'validation checks' — input validation, not transactional integrity.
Trap is C 'input controls' — processing controls, not transaction completion.
Database commits + rollbacks ensure transaction atomicity: either complete and persist, or roll back. Mid-processing halt triggers rollback; integrity preserved.

questions.question: Which of the following security measures BEST ensures the integrity of information stored in a data warehouse?

options.A: Validated daily backups
options.B: Change management procedures
options.C: Data dictionary maintenance
options.D: A read-only restriction

questions.correct_explanation: Applying read-only restriction to a data warehouse prevents data manipulation, because most of the data stored there are historical and do not require changes.

wrong_explanations.A: Backups address availability, not integrity. Validated backups ensure that the backup will work when needed.
wrong_explanations.B: Adequate change management procedures protect the data warehouse and the systems with which the data warehouse interfaces from unauthorized changes but are not usually concerned with the data.
wrong_explanations.C: Data dictionary maintenance procedures provide for the definition and structure of data that are input to the data warehouse. This will not affect the integrity of data already stored.

tips: Trap is A 'validated daily backups' — protects against loss but not against modification.
Trap is B 'change management procedures' — controls intentional changes, doesn't prevent unauthorized modification.
Trap is C 'data dictionary maintenance' — metadata documentation, not integrity.
Data warehouse stores HISTORICAL data for analysis. Read-only restriction prevents any modification = preserves integrity by design. No write means no integrity violations.

questions.question: Which of the following ensures the availability of transactions in the event of a disaster?

options.A: Send hourly backups containing transactions offsite.
options.B: Send daily backups containing transactions offsite.
options.C: Capture transactions to multiple storage devices.
options.D: Transmit transactions offsite in real time.

questions.correct_explanation: The only way to ensure the availability of all transactions is to perform a real-time transmission to an offsite facility.

wrong_explanations.A: Sending hourly backups containing transactions offsite is not in real time and, therefore, can result in the loss of one hour of transactional data.
wrong_explanations.B: Sending daily backups containing transactions offsite is not in real time and, therefore, can result in the loss of one day's worth of transactional data.
wrong_explanations.C: Capturing transactions to multiple storage devices does not ensure availability at an offsite location.

tips: Trap is A 'hourly backups offsite' — up to 1 hour of transactions could be lost.
Trap is B 'daily backups offsite' — up to 24 hours could be lost.
Trap is C 'capture to multiple storage devices' — local redundancy; doesn't protect against site disaster.
Real-time offsite transmission = transactions exist at offsite location simultaneously with primary. Site disaster doesn't cause transaction loss. Maximum availability assurance.

questions.question: IT management has decided to install a level 1 redundant array of inexpensive disks (RAID) system in all servers to compensate for the elimination of offsite backups. The information systems (IS) auditor should recommend:

options.A: upgrading to a level 5 redundant array of inexpensive disks (RAID).
options.B: increasing the frequency of onsite backups.
options.C: reinstating the offsite backups.
options.D: establishing a cold site in a secure location.

questions.correct_explanation: A RAID system, at any level, does not protect against a natural disaster. The problem will not be alleviated without offsite backups.

wrong_explanations.A: Upgrading to level 5 RAID does not address the problem of catastrophic failure of the data center housing all the data.
wrong_explanations.B: Increasing the frequency of onsite backups is not relevant to RAID 1 because all data are being mirrored already.
wrong_explanations.D: A cold site is an offsite recovery location but does not provide for data recovery, because a cold site is not used to store data.

tips: Trap is A 'upgrade to RAID 5' — better RAID; still doesn't survive disasters.
Trap is B 'increase onsite backup frequency' — onsite; same disaster impact.
Trap is D 'establish cold site' — recovery facility, but no data without offsite backups.

RAID protects against disk failure, not site disasters. Eliminating offsite backups eliminates the only disaster-recovery data path. Reinstate offsite immediately; RAID is complementary, not a substitute.

questions.question: Contractual provisions for a hot, warm or cold site should PRIMARILY cover which of the following considerations?

options.A: Physical security measures
options.B: Total number of subscribers
options.C: Number of subscribers permitted to use a site at one time
options.D: References by other users

questions.correct_explanation: The contract should specify the number of subscribers permitted to use the site at any one time. The contract can be written to give preference to certain subscribers.

wrong_explanations.A: Physical security measures are not always part of the contract, although they are an important consideration when choosing a third-party site.
wrong_explanations.B: The total number of subscribers is a consideration, but more important is whether the agreement limits the number of subscribers in a building or in a specific area. It is also good to know if other subscribers are competitors.
wrong_explanations.D: The references that other users can provide are a consideration taken before signing the contract; they are not part of the contractual provisions.

tips: Trap is A 'physical security measures' — operational concern, generally specified.
Trap is B 'total subscribers' — useful info but doesn't constrain availability.
Trap is D 'references' — qualitative, not contractual specification.

Recovery sites have limited capacity. If too many subscribers invoke recovery simultaneously, site can't serve them all. Contract must specify subscriber limits AND priorities to ensure availability when needed.

questions.question: Which of the following reports is the MOST appropriate source of information for an information systems (IS) auditor to validate that an (internet service provider (ISP)) has been complying with an enterprise service level agreement for the availability of outsourced telecommunication services?

options.A: Downtime reports on the telecommunication services generated by the ISP
options.B: A utilization report of automatic failover services generated by the enterprise
options.C: A bandwidth utilization report provided by the ISP
options.D: Downtime reports on the telecommunication services generated by the enterprise

questions.correct_explanation: The enterprise should use internally generated downtime reports to monitor the service provided by the ISP and, as available, to compare with the reports provided by the ISP.

wrong_explanations.A: The internet service provider (ISP)-generated downtime reports are produced by the same entity that is being monitored. As a result, it will be necessary to review these reports for possible bias and/or errors against other data.
wrong_explanations.B: The information provided by these reports is indirect evidence of the extent that the backup telecommunication services were used. These reports may not indicate compliance with the service level agreement, just that the failover systems had been used.
wrong_explanations.C: Utilization reports are used to measure the usage of bandwidth, not uptime.

tips: Trap is A 'ISP-generated downtime reports' — vendor self-reporting; biased.
Trap is B 'failover utilization report' — secondary view; failover isn't downtime.
Trap is C 'bandwidth utilization' — capacity metric, not availability.
Internally-generated downtime reports = independent measurement. Compare to ISP reports for verification. Trust but verify; internal data is the verification baseline.

questions.question: Integrating the business continuity plan (BCP) into IT project management aids in:

options.A: the testing of the business continuity requirements.
options.B: the development of a more comprehensive set of requirements.
options.C: the development of a transaction flowchart.
options.D: ensuring the application meets the users' needs.

questions.correct_explanation: Integrating the BCP into the development process ensures complete coverage of the requirements through each phase of the project.

wrong_explanations.A: Testing the business continuity plan's (BCP) requirements is not related to IT project management.
wrong_explanations.C: A transaction flowchart aids in analyzing an application's controls but does not affect business continuity.
wrong_explanations.D: A BCP will not directly address the detailed processing needs of the users.

tips: Trap is A 'BCP testing' — testing concern, not requirements.
Trap is C 'transaction flowchart' — design artifact, narrow.
Trap is D 'application meets user needs' — UAT concern.
Integrating BCP into project management surfaces continuity requirements early. Result: applications designed FROM THE START to support recovery. Comprehensive requirements coverage.

questions.question: An enterprise uses privileged accounts to process configuration changes for mission-critical applications. Which of the following is the BEST and appropriate control to limit the risk in such a situation?

options.A: Ensure that audit trails are accurate and specific.
options.B: Ensure that personnel have adequate training.
options.C: Ensure that personnel background checks are performed for critical personnel.
options.D: Ensure that supervisory approval and review are performed for critical changes.

questions.correct_explanation: Supervisory approval and review of critical changes by accountable managers are necessary to prevent and detect unauthorized changes. They ensure separation of duties and safeguard against unauthorized attempts by employees.

wrong_explanations.A: Audit trails are a detective control and, in many cases, can be altered by those with privileged access.
wrong_explanations.B: Staff proficiency is important and good training may be somewhat of a deterrent, but supervisory approval and review is the best choice.
wrong_explanations.C: Performing background checks is a very basic control and will not effectively prevent or detect errors or malfeasance.

tips: Trap is A 'audit trails accurate' — detective control, doesn't prevent unauthorized changes.
Trap is B 'adequate training' — capability, doesn't enforce SoD.
Trap is C 'background checks' — preventive HR control.
Privileged accounts + supervisory approval = SoD enforcement. The privileged person makes the change; the supervisor confirms it was authorized. Separates execution from authorization.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor observed that multiple applications are hosted on the same server. The recovery time objective (RTO) for the server is:

options.A: based on the application with the longest RTO.
options.B: based on the application with the shortest RTO.
options.C: based on the mean of each application's RTO.
options.D: independent of the RTO and based on the criticality of the application.

questions.correct_explanation: When several applications are hosted on a server, the server's RTO must be determined by taking the RTO of the most critical application, which is the shortest RTO.

wrong_explanations.A: The longest recovery time objective (RTO) is determined for noncritical applications, which does not help in meeting the objectives for critical systems.
wrong_explanations.C: The mean value is higher than the RTO for a critical application.
wrong_explanations.D: Critical applications usually have the shortest RTOs. The RTO of the server cannot be independent of the application RTO.

tips: Trap is A 'longest RTO' — slowest application drives recovery; critical apps wouldn't recover in time.
Trap is C 'mean RTO' — averaging masks the critical-app constraint.
Trap is D 'independent of RTO' — false; server availability impacts all hosted apps.
Multi-app server recovery is bound by the SHORTEST RTO. The most critical app sets the recovery deadline; faster RTO = stricter constraint. Server inherits the strictest requirement.

questions.question: During an application audit, the information systems (IS) auditor finds several problems related to corrupt data in the database. Which of the following is a corrective control that the IS auditor should recommend?

options.A: Define the standards, and closely monitor them for compliance.
options.B: Ensure that only authorized personnel can update the database.
options.C: Establish controls to handle concurrent access problems.
options.D: Proceed with restore procedures.

questions.correct_explanation: Proceeding with restore procedures is a corrective control. Restore procedures can be used to recover databases to their last-known archived version.

wrong_explanations.A: Establishing standards is a preventive control, and monitoring for compliance is a detective control.
wrong_explanations.B: Ensuring that only authorized personnel can update the database is a preventive control.
wrong_explanations.C: Establishing controls to handle concurrent access problems is a preventive control.

tips: Trap is A 'standards + monitor compliance' — preventive control.
Trap is B 'authorized personnel update only' — preventive access control.
Trap is C 'concurrent access controls' — preventive control.
Restore procedures = corrective control. They restore the database to a known-good state from before the corruption. Fixes the damage; doesn't prevent it.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios provides the BEST disaster recovery plan (DRP) to implement for critical app Ii cations?

options.A: Daily data backups that are stored offsite and a hot site located 140 km from the main data center.
options.B: Daily data backups that are stored onsite in a fireproof safe.
options.C: Real-time data replication between the main data center and the hot site located 500 m from the main site.
options.D: Daily data backups that are stored offsite with a warm site located 70 km from the main data center.

questions.correct_explanation: The absence of real-time backups may pose a challenge depending on the recovery point objective (RPO).

wrong_explanations.B: Having data backups is necessary, but not having a replication site would be insufficient for the critical application.
wrong_explanations.C: Depending on the type of disaster, a hot site should normally be located more than 500 meters from the main facility. Having real-time backups may be the best option, depending on the data RPO.
wrong_explanations.D: A warm site may take days to recover, and, therefore, it may not be a suitable solution.

tips: Trap is B 'onsite fireproof safe' — same site as data center; same disaster impact.
Trap is C 'real-time replication, hot site 500m away' — too close; one disaster could affect both.
Trap is D 'daily backup, warm site 70km' — warm site = activation delay; daily backup = up to 24 hours data loss.
Daily backup offsite + hot site 140km away = data preservation + ready recovery + sufficient geographic separation. Best balance of cost and protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST indicator of the effectiveness of backup and restore procedures while restoring data after a disaster?

options.A: Members of the recovery team were available.
options.B: Recovery time objectives (RTOs) were met.
options.C: Inventory of backup media was properly maintained.
options.D: Backup media was completely restored at an alternate site.

questions.correct_explanation: Effective backup and restore procedures are ensured by meeting recovery time objectives (RTOs), which are defined during the business impact analysis (BIA) stage with input from business process owners.

wrong_explanations.A: The availability of key personnel does not ensure that backup and restore procedures will work effectively.
wrong_explanations.C: The inventory of the backup media is only one element of the successful recovery.
wrong_explanations.D: The restoration of backup media is a critical success, but only if they were able to be restored within the time frames set by the RTO.

tips: Trap is A 'recovery team available' — staffing concern, not procedure effectiveness.
Trap is C 'inventory of backup media' — operational tracking, not effectiveness.
Trap is D 'media restored at alternate site' — partial; restoration without meeting RTO is failure.
RTO measurement = empirical evidence of effectiveness. Did the recovery actually meet business-defined targets? RTO met = procedures work as designed.

questions.question: Which of the following would be the MOST appropriate recovery strategy for a sensitive system with a high recovery time objective (RTO)?

options.A: Warm site
options.B: Hot site
options.C: Cold site
options.D: Mobile recovery site

questions.correct_explanation: Sensitive systems having a high RTO can be performed manually at a tolerable cost for an extended period of time. The cold site is the most cost-effective solution for such a system.

wrong_explanations.A: Although a warm site may be a good solution, it is not the most appropriate, because it is more expensive than a cold site.
wrong_explanations.B: A hot site is used for those systems classified as critical that have a low recovery time objective (RTO).
wrong_explanations.D: A mobile recovery site is not as cost-effective as a cold site and is not appropriate for systems with high RTOs.

tips: Trap is A 'warm site' — over-provisioned; high RTO doesn't need warm capabilities.
Trap is B 'hot site' — way over-provisioned for high RTO scenarios.
Trap is D 'mobile recovery site' — situational; not the typical sensitive-system answer.
High RTO = lots of recovery time available = cheapest viable option. Cold site has lowest cost; sufficient when business can wait for recovery to complete.

questions.question: Which of the following should an incident response team address FIRST after a major incident in an information processing facility (IPF)?

options.A: Restoration at the facility
options.B: Documentation of the facility
options.C: Containment at the facility
options.D: Monitoring of the facility

questions.correct_explanation: The first priority (after addressing life safety) is the containment of the incident at the facility so that spread of the damage is minimized. The incident team must gain control of the situation.

wrong_explanations.A: Restoration ensures that the affected systems or services are restored to a condition specified in the restore point objective. This action will be possible only after containment of the damage.
wrong_explanations.B: Documentation of the facility should be prepared to inform management of the incident; however, damage must be contained first.
wrong_explanations.D: Monitoring of the facility is important, although containment must take priority to avoid spread of the damage.

tips: Trap is A 'restoration' — comes after containment; trying to restore in an uncontained incident risks reinfection.
Trap is B 'documentation' — important for forensics, but containment takes priority.
Trap is D 'monitoring' — useful but doesn't stop the spread.
Containment FIRST: stop the spread, isolate the affected systems, prevent further damage. Without containment, the incident grows. Stop the bleeding before treating the wound.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor discovers that some hard drives disposed of by an enterprise were not sanitized in a manner that would reasonably ensure that the data cannot be recovered. In addition, the enterprise does not have a written policy on data disposal. The IS auditor should FIRST:

options.A: draft an audit finding and discuss it with the auditor in charge.
options.B: determine the sensitivity of the information on the hard drives.
options.C: discuss with the IT manager good practices in data disposal.
options.D: develop an appropriate data disposal policy for the enterprise.

questions.correct_explanation: Although a policy is not available, the information systems (IS) auditor should determine the nature of the information on the hard drives to quantify, as much as possible, the risk.

wrong_explanations.A: Drafting a finding without a quantified risk is premature.
wrong_explanations.C: It would be premature to discuss good practices with the IT manager until the extent of the incident has been quantified.
wrong_explanations.D: An IS auditor should not develop policies.

tips: Trap is A 'draft audit finding' — premature without understanding the data sensitivity.
Trap is C 'discuss good practices' — operational consulting, not auditor's first action.
Trap is D 'develop a policy' — auditor doesn't write organization policies (independence violation).
Risk-based audit response: quantify the risk first. Sensitivity of disposed data determines impact. Public marketing data ≠ medical records ≠ trade secrets. Sensitivity drives finding severity.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is assessing services provided by an internet service provider (ISP) during an IS compliance audit of a nationwide corporation that operates a governmental program. Which of the following is MOST important?

options.A: Review the request for proposal.
options.B: Review monthly performance reports generated by the ISP.
options.C: Review the service level agreement (SLA).
options.D: Research other clients of the ISP.

questions.correct_explanation: An SLA provides the basis for an adequate assessment of the degree to which the provider is meeting the level of agreed-on service.

wrong_explanations.A: Because the request for proposal is not the contracted agreement, it is more relevant to review the terms of the service level agreement (SLA).
wrong_explanations.B: The reports from the (internet service provider (ISP)) are indirect evidence that may require further review to ensure accuracy and completeness.
wrong_explanations.D: The services provided to other clients of the ISP are irrelevant to the information systems (IS) auditor.

tips: Trap is A 'review RFP' — historical document, doesn't bind ongoing performance.
Trap is B 'monthly performance reports by ISP' — vendor self-reports, biased.
Trap is D 'research other clients' — informational, not contractual.
SLA is the contractual instrument that defines what was promised. Compliance audit measures actual performance against SLA commitments. Foundation of provider audit.

questions.question: During an audit of a small enterprise, the information systems (IS) auditor noted that the IS director has superuser-privilege access that allows the director to process requests for changes to the application access roles (access types). Which of the following should the IS auditor recommend?

options.A: Implement a properly documented process for application role change requests.
options.B: Hire additional staff to provide a separation of duties for application role changes.
options.C: Implement an automated process for changing application roles.
options.D: Document the current procedure in detail and make it available on the enterprise intranet.

questions.correct_explanation: The information systems (IS) auditor should recommend implementation of a process that can prevent or detect improper changes from being made to the major application roles. The application role change request process should start and be approved by the business owner; then, the IS director can make the changes to the application.

wrong_explanations.B: Although it is preferred that a strict separation of duties be adhered to and that additional staff be recruited, this practice is not always possible in small enterprises. The IS auditor must look at recommended alternative processes.
wrong_explanations.C: An automated process for managing application roles may not be practical to prevent improper changes being made by the IS director, who also has the most privileged access to the application.
wrong_explanations.D: Making the existing process available on the enterprise intranet would not provide any value to protect the system.

tips: Trap is B 'hire additional staff' — small enterprise constraint; impractical.
Trap is C 'automated process for role changes' — automation without governance just speeds up problems.
Trap is D 'document on intranet' — visibility doesn't equal control.
Documented process for role change requests = approval workflow + records. Even with the IS director executing changes, requests come through the process. Compensating control via process discipline.

questions.question: While observing a full simulation of the business continuity plan (BCP), an information systems (IS) auditor notices that the notification systems within the organizational facilities can be severely impacted by infrastructure damage. The BEST recommendation that the IS auditor can provide to the organization is to ensure that:

options.A: the salvage team is trained to use the notification system.
options.B: the notification system provides for the recovery of the backup.
options.C: redundancies are built into the notification system.
options.D: the notification systems are stored in a vault.

questions.correct_explanation: if the notification system has been severely impacted by the damage, redundancy is the best control.

wrong_explanations.A: The salvage team would not be able to use a severely damaged notification system, even if they are trained to use it.
wrong_explanations.B: The recovery of the backups has no bearing on the notification system.
wrong_explanations.D: Storing the notification system in a vault is of little value if the building is damaged.

tips: Trap is A 'salvage team trained' — operational training, doesn't fix the system.
Trap is B 'recover the backup' — recovery is reactive; redundancy is preventive.
Trap is D 'storage in a vault' — physical protection but doesn't ensure availability during disasters.

Notification system needs redundancy because it's the lifeline during incidents. Multiple paths (cellular + email + landline + satellite) ensure messages get through even when infrastructure is damaged.

questions.question: To ensure structured disaster recovery, it is MOST important that the business continuity plan (BCP) and disaster recovery plan (DRP) are:

options.A: stored at an alternate location.
options.B: communicated to all users.
options.C: tested regularly.
options.D: updated regularly.

questions.correct_explanation: if the BCP is tested regularly, the BCP and disaster recovery plan (DRP) team are adequately aware of the process and that helps in structured disaster recovery.

wrong_explanations.A: Storing the business continuity plan (BCP) at an alternate location is useful in the case of complete site outage; however, the BCP is not useful during a disaster without adequate tests.
wrong_explanations.B: Communicating to users is not of much use without actual tests.
wrong_explanations.D: Even if the plan is updated regularly, it is ofless use during an actual disaster if it is not adequately tested.

tips: Trap is A 'stored at alternate location' — protection of plan documents, doesn't ensure plan effectiveness.
Trap is B 'communicated to all users' — awareness, doesn't ensure preparedness.
Trap is D 'updated regularly' — currency without testing isn't enough; updates may not work.
Regular testing exercises the plan AND the team. Discovers gaps, builds muscle memory, validates procedures. Without testing, the plan exists only on paper — its effectiveness is theoretical.

questions.question: The PRIMARY purpose of a business impact analysis (BIA) is to:

options.A: define recovery strategies.
options.B: identify the alternate site.
options.C: improve recovery testing.
options.D: calculate the annual loss expectancy.

questions.correct_explanation: One of the primary outcomes of a business impact analysis (BIA) is the recovery time objective (RTO)e and the recovery point objective (RPO), which help in defining the recovery strategies.

wrong_explanations.B: A BIA, itself, does not help in identifying the alternate site. That is determined during the recovery strategy phase of the project.
wrong_explanations.C: A BIA, itself, does not help improve recovery testing. That is done during the implementation and testing phase of the project.
wrong_explanations.D: The annual loss expectancy of critical business assets and processes is determined during risk assessment and is reviewed in the BIA, but this is not the primary advantage.

tips: Trap is B 'identify alternate site' — implementation choice driven by recovery strategy.
Trap is C 'improve recovery testing' — testing improvement follows from BIA-defined RTO/RPO.
Trap is D 'calculate annual loss expectancy' — financial metric, downstream of BIA.
BIA's primary outputs: RTO, RPO, criticality ranking. These directly drive recovery strategy choices: hot vs cold site, backup frequency, prioritization. BIA is the strategy foundation.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST helps define disaster recovery strategies?

options.A: Annual loss expectancy and exposure factor
options.B: Maximum tolerable downtime and data loss
options.C: Existing server and network redundancies
options.D: Data backup and offsite storage requirements

questions.correct_explanation: Two of the key outcomes of the business impact analysis are the recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO)-maximum tolerable downtime and data loss-that further help in identifying the recovery strategies.

wrong_explanations.A: Annual loss expectancy and exposure factor are more related to risk in general.
wrong_explanations.C: Existing server and network redundancies are good to know, but the RTO and RPO are needed to design the right recovery strategies.
wrong_explanations.D: Data backup and off site storage requirements are an important aspect of a business continuity plan (BCP), but these alone will not help in defining the disaster recovery strategies.

tips: Trap is A 'ALE and exposure factor' — risk metrics, not recovery strategy drivers.
Trap is C 'existing redundancies' — current state, doesn't drive future strategy.
Trap is D 'backup and offsite requirements' — implementation detail, follows strategy.
Maximum tolerable downtime (RTO) and maximum tolerable data loss (RPO) define the recovery strategy. Hot site for short RTO, real-time replication for short RPO. RTO/RPO drive everything.

questions.question: After a disaster declaration, the media creation date at a warm recovery site is based on the:

options.A: recovery point objective (RPO)
options.B: recovery time objective (RTO)
options.C: service delivery objective (SDO)
options.D: maximum tolerable outage (MTO)

questions.correct_explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) defines the acceptable data loss in a disruption, indicating the earliest acceptable data recovery point. It quantifies the permissible data loss in case of interruption. The media creation date reflects the RPO for data restoration.

wrong_explanations.B: The recovery time objective (RTO) is the amount of time allowed for the recovery of a business function or resource after a disaster occurs.
wrong_explanations.C: The service delivery objective (SDO) is directly related to the business needs and is the level of service to be reached during the alternate process mode until the normal situation is restored.
wrong_explanations.D: The maximum tolerable outage (MTO) is the maximum time that an organization can support processing in alternate mode.

tips: Trap is B 'RTO' — defines time to recovery, not data preservation point.
Trap is C 'SDO' — service level during recovery, not the data point.
Trap is D 'MTO' — maximum tolerable outage, related to RTO.
Media creation date defines the data point at warm site = RPO concern. RPO defines acceptable data loss; backup media must be no older than the RPO interval.

questions.question: The activation of an enterprise's business continuity plan (BCP) should be based on predetermined criteria that address the:

options.A: duration of the outage.
options.B: type of outage.
options.C: probability of the outage.
options.D: cause of the outage.

questions.correct_explanation: The initiation of a business continuity plan (BCP) (action) should primarily be based on the maximum period for which a business function can be disrupted before the disruption threatens the achievement of organizational objectives.

wrong_explanations.B: The type of outage is not as important to the activation of the plan as the length or duration of the outage.
wrong_explanations.C: The probability of the outage is relevant to the frequency of incidents, not the need to activate the plan. The plan is designed to be activated after an event of a certain duration occurs.
wrong_explanations.D: The cause of the outage may affect the response plan to be activated, but not the decision to activate the plan. The plan will be activated any time an event of a predetermined duration occurs.

tips: Trap is B 'type of outage' — relevant to response approach but not activation criteria.
Trap is C 'probability' — applies to risk assessment, not BCP activation.
Trap is D 'cause' — root cause comes after; activation is duration-driven.
BCP activation is duration-based: how long can the business be disrupted? When duration exceeds threshold, activate. Type and cause may inform response, but activation timing is set by duration.

questions.question: During an audit of a small organization that provides medical transcription services, an information systems (IS) auditor observes several issues related to the backup and restore process. Which of the following should be the auditor's GREATEST concern?

options.A: Restoration testing for backup media is not performed; however, all data restore requests have been successful.
options.B: The policy for data backup and retention has not been reviewed by the business owner for the past three years.
options.C: The organization stores transcription backup media offsite using a third-party service provider that inventories backups annually.
options.D: Failed backup alerts for the marketing department data files are not followed up on or resolved by the IT administrator.

questions.correct_explanation: Losing a backup medium is a major incident for an organization handling confidential patient data. Privacy laws impose severe penalties, and mandated reporting requirements can harm the organization's reputation. To ensure proper backup handling, the organization should conduct audit tests, including frequent physical inventories and evaluating controls at the third-party provider.

wrong_explanations.A: Lack of restoration testing does not increase the risk of unauthorized leakage of information. Not performing restoration tests on backup media poses a risk; however, this risk is somewhat mitigated because past data restore requests have been successful.
wrong_explanations.B: Lack ofreview of the data backup and retention policy may be a concern if systems and business processes have changed in the past three years. The information systems (1S) auditor should perform additional procedures to verify the validity of existing procedures. In addition, lack of this control does not introduce a risk of unauthorized leakage of information.
wrong_explanations.D: Failed backup alerts that are not followed up on and resolved imply that certain data or files are not backed up. This is a concern if the files/data being backed up are critical in nature, but, typically, marketing data files are not regulated in the same way as medical transcription files. Lack of this control does not introduce a risk of unauthorized leakage of sensitive information.

tips: Trap is A 'no restoration testing but successful restores' — concerning but operationally functional.
Trap is B 'policy not reviewed in 3 years' — currency concern, addressable.
Trap is D 'failed marketing backup alerts' — non-PHI data; lower regulatory exposure.
Medical transcription = PHI. Storing PHI offsite with annual inventory only = potential to lose PHI without notice. Privacy laws mandate stricter controls. Greatest concern in healthcare scenarios.

questions.question: Determining the service delivery objective (SDO) should be based PRIMARILY on:

options.A: the minimum acceptable operational capability.
options.B: the cost-effectiveness of the restoration process.
options.C: meeting the recovery time objectives (RTOs).
options.D: the allowable interruption window.

questions.correct_explanation: The service delivery objective (SDO) is the level of service to be reached during the alternate process mode until the normal situation is restored. This is directly related to the business needs.

wrong_explanations.B: The cost-effectiveness of the restoration process is not the main consideration of determining the SDO.
wrong_explanations.C: Meeting the recovery time objective (RTO) may be one of the considerations in determining the SOO, but it is a secondary factor.
wrong_explanations.D: The allowable interruption window may be one of the factors secondary to determining the SOO.

tips: Trap is B 'cost-effectiveness of restoration' — financial concern, secondary.
Trap is C 'meeting RTO' — RTO is recovery time, not service level.
Trap is D 'allowable interruption window' — time concept, not service level.
SDO defines minimum acceptable service level during alternate operations. Below this level, business can't function. Set based on what business absolutely needs to function, even degraded.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing the application change management process for a large multinational organization should be MOST concerned when:

options.A: test systems run different configurations than production systems.
options.B: change management records are paper based.
options.C: the configuration management database is not maintained.
options.D: the test environment is installed on the production server.

questions.correct_explanation: The configuration management database (CMDB) is used to track configuration item (Cl) and the dependencies between them. An out-of-date CMDB in a large multinational organization can result in incorrect approvals being obtained or leave out critical dependencies during the test phase.

wrong_explanations.A: Although, ideally, production and test systems should be configured identically, there may be reasons why this does not occur. The more significant concern is whether the configuration management database was not maintained.
wrong_explanations.B: Paper-based change management records are inefficient to maintain and not easy to review in large volumes; however, they do not present a concern from a control point of view if they are properly and diligently maintained.
wrong_explanations.D: Although it is not ideal to have the test environment installed on the production server, it is not a control-related concern. If the test and production environments are kept separate, they can be installed on the same physical server(s).

tips: Trap is A 'test ≠ production configuration' — concerning but not the highest priority.
Trap is B 'paper-based change records' — manageable through process discipline.
Trap is D 'test on production server' — concerning isolation issue, but configuration tracking is more critical.

Configuration management database (CMDB) maps configuration items and dependencies. In a multinational org, missing CMDB = changes without dependency awareness = unintended downstream impacts. Critical for change safety.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor can verify that an organization's business continuity plan (BCP) is effective by reviewing the:

options.A: alignment of the BCP with industry good practices.
options.B: results of business continuity tests performed by information systems (IS) and end-user personnel.
options.C: offsite facility, its contents, security and environmental controls.
options.D: annual financial cost of the BCP activities versus the expected benefit of the implementation of the plan.

questions.correct_explanation: The effectiveness of the BCP can best be evaluated by reviewing the results from previous business continuity tests for thoroughness and accuracy in accomplishing their stated objectives.

wrong_explanations.A: Alignment of the business continuity plan (BCP) with industry good practices does not provide the assurance of the effectiveness of the BCP.
wrong_explanations.C: The offsite facility, its contents, security and environmental controls do not provide assurance of the effectiveness of the BCP. Only testing will provide an accurate assessment of the effectiveness of the BCP.
wrong_explanations.D: The annual financial cost of the BCP activities versus the expected benefit of implementation of the plan does not provide assurance of the effectiveness of the BCP. Only testing will provide an accurate assessment of the effectiveness of the BCP.

tips: Trap is A 'alignment with industry good practices' — paper review, doesn't verify effectiveness.
Trap is C 'review offsite facility' — physical/environmental check, narrow scope.
Trap is D 'cost vs benefit' — financial analysis, doesn't measure effectiveness.
Test results = empirical evidence of BCP effectiveness. Did people, processes, and infrastructure actually work? Tests are the only objective measure.

questions.question: It is MOST appropriate to implement an incremental backup scheme when:

options.A: there is limited recovery time for critical data.
options.B: online disk-based media are preferred.
options.C: there is limited media capacity.
options.D: a random selection of backup sets is required.

questions.correct_explanation: In an incremental backup, after the full backup, only the files that have changed are backed up, thus minimizing media storage.

wrong_explanations.A: A full backup or differential backup is preferred in this situation.
wrong_explanations.B: Incremental backup could be used irrespective of the media adopted.
wrong_explanations.D: A random selection of backup sets may not be possible with an incremental backup scheme because only fragments of the data are backed up on a daily basis.

tips: Trap is A 'limited recovery time' — incremental requires LONG recovery (replay all incrementals).
Trap is B 'online disk-based media' — media type doesn't dictate backup type.
Trap is D 'random selection of backup sets' — incremental can't be randomly accessed.
Incremental backup only stores changes since last backup. Minimal storage = ideal for limited media capacity. Tradeoff: longer restore time.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST mitigates the risk arising from using reciprocal agreements as a recovery alternative?

options.A: Perform disaster recovery exercises annually.
options.B: Ensure that partnering organizations are separated geographically.
options.C: Regularly perform a business impact analysis (BIA).
options.D: Select a partnering organization with similar systems.

questions.correct_explanation: If the two partnering organizations are in close geographic proximity, this can lead to both organizations being subjected to the same environmental disaster, such as an earthquake.

wrong_explanations.A: Although disaster recovery exercises are important but difficult to perform in a reciprocal agreement, the greater risk is geographic proximity.
wrong_explanations.C: A business impact analysis (BIA) will help both organizations identify critical applications, but separation is a more important consideration when entering reciprocal agreements.
wrong_explanations.D: Selecting a partnering organization with similar systems is a good idea, but separation is a more important consideration when entering reciprocal agreements.

tips: Trap is A 'annual DR exercises' — testing frequency, doesn't address geographic risk.
Trap is C 'regular BIA' — analysis, doesn't change reciprocal vulnerability.
Trap is D 'partner with similar systems' — compatibility good, but doesn't address co-disaster risk.
Reciprocal agreements fail when both partners face the same disaster (regional events, hurricanes, earthquakes). Geographic separation is the critical risk mitigator.

questions.question: During the review of an in-house developed application, the GREATEST concern to an information systems (IS) auditor is if a:

options.A: user raises a change request and tests it in the test environment.
options.B: programmer codes a change in the development environment and tests it in the test environment.
options.C: manager approves a change request and then reviews it in production.
options.D: manager initiates a change request and subsequently approves it.

questions.correct_explanation: Initiating and approving a change request by the same person violates the principle of separation of duties, because one should not approve their own requests.

wrong_explanations.A: Having a user involved in testing changes is common practice.
wrong_explanations.B: Having a programmer code a change in development and then separately test the change in a test environment is a good practice and preferable over testing in production.
wrong_explanations.C: Having a manager review a change to make sure it was done correctly is an acceptable practice.

tips: Trap is A 'user raises and tests change' — appropriate; user owns business need and validates.
Trap is B 'programmer codes and tests in test env' — appropriate; tests in non-production.
Trap is C 'manager approves and reviews in production' — appropriate; review is post-deployment.
Same person initiating AND approving = SoD violation. Approver must be independent of requester. Self-approval is the foundational control failure.

questions.question: In a disaster recovery situation, which of the following is the MOST important metric to ensure that data are synchronized between critical systems?

options.A: recovery point objective (RPO)
options.B: recovery time objective (RTO)
options.C: recovery service resilience
options.D: recovery service scalability

questions.correct_explanation: Establishing a common recovery point objective (RPO) is most critical for ensuring that interdependencies between systems are properly synchronized. It ensures that systems do not contain data from different points in time that may result in accounting transactions that cannot be reconciled and a loss of referential integrity.

wrong_explanations.B: recovery time objectives (RTOs) are not as important to synchronize because they normally vary depending on the level of effort and resources required to restore a system.
wrong_explanations.C: Recovery service resilience measures the fault tolerance due to data exceptions and ability to restart and recover from internal failures.
wrong_explanations.D: Recovery service scalability refers to the capacity constraints and limitations that a recovery solution may have relative to the original system configuration.

tips: Trap is B 'RTO' — recovery time, doesn't affect data synchronization.
Trap is C 'service resilience' — operational quality, not data sync.
Trap is D 'service scalability' — capacity concept, not sync.
Common RPO across critical systems = same data point at recovery. If RPOs differ, recovered data is from different times → inconsistent state across systems. Synchronization requires common RPO.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST mitigates the risk of backup media containing irreplaceable information being lost or stolen while in transit?

options.A: Ensure that media are encrypted.
options.B: Maintain a duplicate copy.
options.C: Maintain chain of custody.
options.D: Ensure that personnel are bonded.

questions.correct_explanation: Sensitive data should always be fully backed up before being transmitted or moved. Backups of sensitive information should be treated with the same control considerations as the actual data.

wrong_explanations.A: Although strong encryption protects against disclosure, it will not mitigate the loss of irreplaceable data.
wrong_explanations.C: Chain of custody is an important control, but it will not mitigate a loss if a locked area is broken into and media removed or if media are lost while in an individual's custody.
wrong_explanations.D: Bonded security, although good for preventing theft, will not protect against accidental loss or destruction.

tips: Trap is A 'encryption' — protects against unauthorized access to lost media; doesn't replace lost data.
Trap is C 'chain of custody' — tracks who handled it, doesn't replace lost data.
Trap is D 'personnel bonded' — financial liability for losses, doesn't replace data.
Backup of the backup = redundancy. Even if media is lost or stolen, the duplicate ensures data isn't lost. Most direct mitigation for irreplaceable information loss.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the change management process for an enterprise resource planning application. Which of the following is the BEST method for testing program changes?

options.A: Select a sample of change tickets and review them for authorization.
options.B: Perform a walk-through by tracing a program change from start to finish.
options.C: Trace a sample of modified programs to support change tickets.
options.D: Use query software to analyze all change tickets for missing fields.

questions.correct_explanation: Tracing modified programs to change tickets is the best way to test change management controls and detect undocumented changes.

wrong_explanations.A: Selecting a sample of change tickets and reviewing them for authorization helps test for authorization controls; however, it does not identify program changes that were made without supporting change tickets.
wrong_explanations.B: Performing a walk-through assists the information systems (IS) auditor in understanding the process but does not ensure that all changes adhere to the normal process.
wrong_explanations.D: Using query software to analyze all change tickets for missing fields does not identify program changes that were made without supporting change tickets.

tips: Trap is A 'sample change tickets, review authorization' — verifies authorized changes; misses unauthorized ones.
Trap is B 'walk-through change start to finish' — process review, single instance.
Trap is D 'query all tickets for missing fields' — admin completeness check.
Tracing actual modified programs back to tickets catches changes WITHOUT documentation. Substantive test of completeness — finds the gaps where changes happened without authorization.

questions.question: Emergency changes that bypass the normal change control process are MOST acceptable if:

options.A: management reviews and approves the changes after they have occurred.
options.B: the changes are reviewed by a peer at the time of the change.
options.C: the changes are documented in the change control system by the operations department.
options.D: management has preapproved all emergency changes.

questions.correct_explanation: Because management cannot always be available when a system failure occurs, it is acceptable for changes to be reviewed and approved within a reasonable time period after they occur.

wrong_explanations.B: Although peer review provides some accountability, management should review and approve all changes, even if that review and approval must occur after the fact.
wrong_explanations.C: Documenting the event does not replace the need for a review and approval process to occur.
wrong_explanations.D: It is not a good control practice for management to ignore its responsibility by preapproving all emergency changes in advance without reviewing them. Unauthorized changes can then be made without management knowledge.

tips: Trap is B 'reviewed by peer at time of change' — peer review without management oversight.
Trap is C 'documented by operations' — documentation alone without review.
Trap is D 'preapproved all emergency changes' — defeats the 'emergency' nature.
Emergency changes are unavoidable. Acceptable practice: change occurs, then management reviews/approves within reasonable timeframe. Captures audit trail; ensures retroactive justification.

questions.question: To optimize an organization's business continuity plan, an information systems (IS) auditor should recommend a business impact analysis to determine:

options.A: the business processes that generate the most financial value for the organization and, therefore, must be recovered first.
options.B: the priorities and order for recovery to ensure alignment with the organization's business strategy.
options.C: the business processes that must be recovered following a disaster to ensure the organization's survival.
options.D: the priorities and order of recovery, which will recover the greatest number of systems in the shortest time frame.

questions.correct_explanation: To ensure the organization's survival following a disaster, it is important to recover the most critical business processes first.

wrong_explanations.A: It is a common mistake to overemphasize financial value rather than urgency. For example, although the processing of incoming mortgage loan payments is important from a financial perspective, it can be delayed for a few days in the event of a disaster. Wiring funds to close on a loan, although not generating direct revenue, is far more critical because of the possibility ofregulatory problems, customer complaints and reputation issues.
wrong_explanations.B: The business strategy (which is often a long-term view) does not have a direct impact at this point in time.
wrong_explanations.D: The mere number of recovered systems does not have a direct impact at this point in time. The important action is to recover systems that would impact business survival.

tips: Trap is A 'most financial value' — important but financial impact ≠ survival.
Trap is B 'order for business strategy alignment' — strategic but not survival-focused.
Trap is D 'recover greatest number of systems' — quantity over criticality.
BCP's primary purpose: organizational survival. BIA identifies which processes MUST recover for the organization to survive. Survival-critical processes get top priority.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST efficient strategy for the backup of large quantities of mission-critical data when the systems need to be on line to take sales orders 24 hours a day?

options.A: Implementing a fault-tolerant disk-to-disk backup solution.
options.B: Making a full backup weekly and an incremental backup nightly.
options.C: Creating a duplicate storage area network (SAN) and replicating the data to a second SAN.
options.D: Creating identical server and storage infrastructure at a hot site.

questions.correct_explanation: Disk-to-disk backup involves writing the primary backup to disk instead of tape. This allows for later copying, cloning or migration to tape. It ensures minimal system performance impact, enables fast backups of large data volumes and offers immediate transfer to an alternate disk set in case of failure.

wrong_explanations.B: Although a backup strategy is valid, because many computer systems must be taken offline so that backups can be performed, there is the need to create a backup window, typically during each night. This does not enable the system to be available 24/7. For a system that must remain online at all times, the only feasible way to back up the data is to either duplicate the data to a server that gets backed up to magnetic media or deploy a disk-to-disk solution, which is effectively the same thing.
wrong_explanations.C: Although creating a duplicate storage area network (SAN) and replicating the data to a second SAN provides some redundancy and data protection, this is not really a backup solution. lfthe two systems are at the same site, there is a risk that an incident such as a fire or flood in the data center can lead to data loss.
wrong_explanations.D: Although creating an identical server and storage infrastructure at a hot site provides a great deal of redundancy and availability to enable the system to stay operational, it does not address the need for long-tenn data storage. There is still the need to create an efficient method of backing up data.

tips: Trap is B 'weekly full + nightly incremental' — backup window required; conflicts with 24/7.
Trap is C 'duplicate SAN replication' — redundancy but doesn't backup; loses data on logical errors.
Trap is D 'identical hot site infrastructure' — high availability but expensive without backup capability.
Disk-to-disk fault-tolerant backup runs continuously without backup windows. Minimal performance impact, fast restore. Best fit for 24/7 mission-critical scenarios.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST ensures uninterrupted operations in an organization with IT operation centers in several countries?

options.A: Distribution of key procedural documentation
options.B: Reciprocal agreement between business partners
options.C: Strong senior management leadership
options.D: Employee training on the BCP

questions.correct_explanation: During a disaster, the chain of command might be interrupted. Therefore, it is important that employees know their roles in the BCP, including where to report and how to perform their job functions. Employee training on the plan is especially important for businesses with offices that are geographically separated because there is a greater chance of communication disruption.

wrong_explanations.A: Procedural documentation should always be up-to-date and distributed to major locations. However, documents alone are insufficient if employees do not know their role in the plan.
wrong_explanations.B: A reciprocal agreement is an emergency processing agreement between two or more enterprises with similar equipment or applications. Typically, participants of a reciprocal agreement promise to provide processing time to each other when an emergency arises. Although it is integral to business continuity to have a location for business operations, it does not necessarily need to be a reciprocal agreement. For example, in some cases, business operations may be carried out from each employee's home.
wrong_explanations.C: Senior management may not be readily available to provide leadership during a disaster. Therefore, it is most important that employees fully understand their roles in the business continuity plan (BCP).

tips: Trap is A 'distribute documentation' — visibility, doesn't ensure response capability.
Trap is B 'reciprocal agreements' — between business partners; not for internal multi-country ops.
Trap is C 'strong leadership' — important but not the operational continuity factor.

Multi-country IT centers face communication/coordination disruptions during disasters. Trained employees know their roles independently. Decentralized capability survives chain-of-command interruption.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST ensures that users have uninterrupted access to a critical, heavily used web-based application?

options.A: Disk mirroring
options.B: redundant array of inexpensive disks (RAID)
options.C: Dynamic domain name system (DNS)
options.D: Load balancing

questions.correct_explanation: Load balancing distributes traffic across multiple servers, ensuring uninterrupted system availability and consistent response time for web applications. It also redirects traffic to functional servers if a server fails.

wrong_explanations.A: Disk mirroring provides real-time replication of disk drives but does not ensure uninterrupted system availability in the event a server crashes.
wrong_explanations.B: redundant array of inexpensive disks (RAID) technology improves resiliency but does not protect against failure of a network interface card or central processing unit processor failure.
wrong_explanations.C: Dynamic domain name system (DNS) is a method used to assign a host name to an Internet Protocol address that is dynamic. This is a useful technology but does not help ensure availability.

tips: Trap is A 'disk mirroring' — protects data, doesn't load-balance traffic.
Trap is B 'RAID' — disk-level redundancy, not application access.
Trap is C 'dynamic DNS' — name resolution, doesn't distribute load.
Load balancing distributes traffic across multiple servers. Heavy use ≠ slow response. If one server fails, load shifts to others. Foundation of high-availability web applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST method to ensure that critical IT system failures do not reoccur?

options.A: Invest in redundant systems.
options.B: Conduct a follow-up audit.
options.C: Monitor system performance.
options.D: Perform root cause analysis.

questions.correct_explanation: Root cause analysis determines the key reason an incident has occurred and allows for appropriate corrections that will help prevent the incident from recurring.

wrong_explanations.A: Redundancy may be a solution; however, a root cause analysis enables an educated decision to address the origin of the problem instead of simply assuming that system redundancy is the solution.
wrong_explanations.B: Although an audit may discover the root cause of the problem, an audit is not a solution to an operational problem. Identifying the origins of operational failures needs to be part of day-to-day IT processes and owned by the IT department.
wrong_explanations.C: Monitoring tools are a means to gather data and can contribute to root cause analysis, but they alone do not help prevent an existing problem from recurring.

tips: Trap is A 'redundant systems' — bandage; doesn't prevent root cause from recurring.
Trap is B 'follow-up audit' — verification, doesn't drive prevention.
Trap is C 'monitor performance' — detection, doesn't address cause.

Root cause analysis = treat the disease, not the symptom. Identify what underlying issue caused the failure. Address the cause; the failure won't recur. Foundational principle of reliability engineering.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST important when an operating system (OS) patch is to be applied to a production environment?

options.A: Successful regression testing by the developer
options.B: Approval from the information asset owner
options.C: Approval from the security officer
options.D: Patch installation at alternate sites

questions.correct_explanation: It is most important that information owners approve any changes to production systems to ensure that no serious business disruption takes place as the result of the patch release.

wrong_explanations.A: Although testing is important for any patch, in this case, it should be assumed that the operating system (OS) vendor tested the patch before releasing it. Before this OS patch is put into production, the organization should do system testing to ensure that no issues will occur.
wrong_explanations.C: The security officer does not normally need to approve every OS patch.
