questions.question: Which of the following is the PRIMARY objective of the business continuity plan (BCP) process?

options.A: To provide assurance to stakeholders that business operations will continue in the event of disaster.
options.B: To establish an alternate site for IT services to meet predefined recovery time objectives (RTOs).
options.C: To manage risk while recovering from an event that adversely affected operations.
options.D: To meet the regulatory compliance requirements in the event of natural disaster.

questions.correct_explanation: The BCP process primarily focuses on managing and mitigating risk during recovery of operations due to an event that affected operations.

wrong_explanations.A: The business continuity plan (BCP) does not provide assurance of continuing operations; however, it helps the organization to respond to disruptions to critical business processes.
wrong_explanations.B: Establishment of an alternate site is more relevant to disaster recovery than the BCP.
wrong_explanations.D: The regulatory compliance requirements may help establish the recovery time objective (RTO) requirements.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Recovery decisions (RTO, RPO, hot vs warm site) flow from the business impact analysis — never pick a recovery strategy before the BIA is done.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST helps to detect errors in data processing?

options.A: Programmed edit checks
options.B: Well-designed data entry screens
options.C: Separation of duties
options.D: Hash totals

questions.correct_explanation: The use of hash totals is an effective method to reliably detect errors in data processing. A hash total indicates an error in data integrity.

wrong_explanations.A: Automated controls, such as programmed edit checks, are preventive controls.
wrong_explanations.B: Automated controls, such as well-designed data entry screens, are preventive controls.
wrong_explanations.C: Enforcing separation of duties primarily ensures that a single individual does not have the authority to both create and approve a transaction; this is not considered to be a method to detect errors, but a method to help prevent errors.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST critical to the quality of data in a data warehouse?

options.A: Accuracy of the source data
options.B: Credibility of the data source
options.C: Accuracy of the extraction process
options.D: Accuracy of the data transformation

questions.correct_explanation: Accuracy of source data is a prerequisite for the quality of the data in a data warehouse. Inaccurate source data will corrupt the integrity of the data in the data warehouse.

wrong_explanations.B: Credibility of the data source is important but would not change inaccurate data into quality (accurate) data.
wrong_explanations.C: Accurate extraction processes are important but would not change inaccurate data into quality (accurate) data.
wrong_explanations.D: Accurate transformation routines are important but would not change inaccurate data into quality (accurate) data.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: A clerk changed the interest rate for a loan on a master file. The rate entered is outside the normal range for such a loan. Which of the following controls is MOST effective in providing reasonable assurance that the change was authorized?

options.A: The system will not process the change until the clerk's manager confirms the change by entering an approval code.
options.B: The system generates a weekly report listing all rate exceptions and the report is reviewed by the clerk's manager.
options.C: The system requires the clerk to enter an approval code.
options.D: The system displays a warning message to the clerk.

questions.correct_explanation: Requiring an approval code by a manager prevents or detects the use of an unauthorized interest rate.

wrong_explanations.B: A weekly report informs the manager after the fact that a change was made, thereby making it possible for transactions to use an unauthorized rate prior to management review. Although this control provides visibility into rate exceptions, it does not prevent or enforce authorization in real time. By relying solely on periodic review, there is no immediate assurance that the change was authorized before it was processed.
wrong_explanations.C: Having a clerk enter an approval code does not provide separation of duties and does not prevent the clerk from entering an unauthorized rate change.
wrong_explanations.D: A warning message alerts the clerk in case the change was being made in error but does not prevent the clerk from entering an unauthorized rate change.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: The GREATEST advantage of using web services for the exchange of information between two systems is:

options.A: secure communication.
options.B: improved performance.
options.C: efficient interfacing.
options.D: enhanced documentation.

questions.correct_explanation: Web services facilitate the interoperable exchange of information between two systems regardless of the operating system or programming language used.

wrong_explanations.A: Communication is not necessarily more secure using web services.
wrong_explanations.B: The use of web services does not necessarily increase performance.
wrong_explanations.D: There is no documentation benefit in using web services.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is a prevalent risk in the development of end-user computing applications?

options.A: Applications may not be subject to testing and IT general controls.
options.B: Development and maintenance costs may be increased.
options.C: Application development time may be increased.
options.D: Decision-making may be impaired due to diminished responsiveness to requests for information.

questions.correct_explanation: End-user computing is defined as the ability of end users to design and implement their own information system using computer software products. End-user developed applications may not be subjected to an independent outside review by systems analysts and frequently are not created in the context of a formal development methodology. These applications may lack appropriate standards, controls, quality assurance procedures and documentation. A risk of end­user applications is that management may rely on them as much as traditional applications.

wrong_explanations.B: End-user computing systems typically result in reduced application development and maintenance costs.
wrong_explanations.C: End-user computing systems typically result in a reduced development cycle time.
wrong_explanations.D: End-user computing systems normally increase flexibility and responsiveness to management's information requests because the system is being developed directly by the user community.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds out-of-range data in some tables of a database. Which of the following controls should the IS auditor recommend to avoid this situation?

options.A: Log all table update transactions
options.B: Implement integrity constraints in the database
options.C: Implement before and after image reporting
options.D: Use tracing and tagging

questions.correct_explanation: Implementing integrity constraints in the database is a preventive control because data are checked against predefined tables or rules, which prevents any undefined data from being entered.

wrong_explanations.A: Logging all table update transactions provides audit trails and is a detective control but will not prevent the introduction of inaccurate data.
wrong_explanations.C: Before and after image reporting makes it possible to trace the impact that transactions have on computer records and is a detective control.
wrong_explanations.D: Tracing and tagging is used to test application systems and controls but is not a preventive control that can avoid out-of-range data.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: A new database is being set up in an overseas location to provide information to the general public and to increase the speed at which the information is made available. The overseas database is to be housed at a data center and will be updated in real time to mirror the information stored locally. Which of the following areas of operations should be considered as having the HIGHEST risk?

options.A: Confidentiality of the information stored in the database
options.B: The hardware being used to run the database application
options.C: Backups of the information in the overseas database
options.D: Remote access to the backup database

questions.correct_explanation: The business objective is to make the information available to the public in a timely manner. Because the database is physically located overseas, hardware failures that are left unfixed can reduce the availability of the system to users.

wrong_explanations.A: Confidentiality of the information stored in the database is not a major concern, because the information is intended for public use.
wrong_explanations.C: Backups of the information in the overseas database are not a major concern, because the overseas database is a mirror of the local database; thus, a backup copy exists locally.
wrong_explanations.D: Remote access to the backup database does not impact availability.

tips: RTO measures downtime tolerance; RPO measures data-loss tolerance. Lower numbers cost more — match them to business criticality, not gut feel.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST effective when determining the correctness of individual account balances migrated from one database to another?

options.A: Compare the hash total before and after the migration.
options.B: Verify that the number ofrecords is the same for both databases.
options.C: Perform sample testing of the migrated account balances.
options.D: Compare the control totals of all of the transactions.

questions.correct_explanation: Performing sample testing of the migrated account balances involves the comparison of a selection of individual transactions from the database before and after the migration.

wrong_explanations.A: The hash total only validates the data integrity at a batch level rather than at a transaction level.
wrong_explanations.B: Databases are composed of records that can contain multiple fields. The number ofrecords does not allow an information systems (IS) auditor to ascertain whether some of these fields have been successfully migrated.
wrong_explanations.D: Comparing the control totals does not imply that the records are complete or that individual values are accurate.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: During the review of data file change management controls, which of the following BEST helps to decrease the research time needed to investigate exceptions?

options.A: One-for-one checking
options.B: Data file security
options.C: Transaction logs
options.D: File updating and maintenance authorization

questions.correct_explanation: Transaction logs generate an audit trail by providing a detailed list of date of input, time of input, user ID, terminal location, etc. Research time can be reduced in investigating exceptions because the review can be performed on the logs rather than on the entire transaction file. Transaction logs also help to determine which transactions have been posted to an account-by a particular individual during a particular period.

wrong_explanations.A: One-for-one checking is a control procedure in which an individual document agrees with a detailed listing of documents processed by the system. It would take a long time to complete the research using this procedure.
wrong_explanations.B: Data file security controls prevent access by unauthorized users in their attempt to alter data files. This would not help identify the transactions posted to an account.
wrong_explanations.D: File updating and maintenance authorization is a control procedure to update the stored data and ensure accuracy and security of stored data. This does provide evidence regarding the individuals who update the stored data; however, it is not effective in the given situation to determine transactions posted to an account.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Production changes require: documented request → impact analysis → approval → tested change → back-out plan → post-change verification. Skipping any step is a finding.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing a monthly accounts payable transaction register using audit software. Why would the auditor be interested in using a check digit?

options.A: To detect data transposition errors
options.B: To ensure that transactions do not exceed predetermined amounts
options.C: To ensure that data entered are within reasonable limits
options.D: To ensure that data entered are within a predetermined range of values

questions.correct_explanation: A check digit is a numeric value added to data to ensure that original data are correct and have not been altered.

wrong_explanations.B: Ensuring that data have not exceeded a predetermined amount is a limit check.
wrong_explanations.C: Ensuring that data entered are within predetermined reasonable limits is a reasonableness check.
wrong_explanations.D: Ensuring that data entered are within a predetermined range of values is a range check.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: A hard disk containing confidential data was damaged beyond repair. If the goal is to ensure with certainty that access to the data by anyone else is prevented, what should be done to the hard disk before it is discarded?

options.A: Overwriting
options.B: Low-level formatting
options.C: Degaussing
options.D: Destruction

questions.correct_explanation: Physically destroying the hard disk is the most effective way to ensure that data cannot be recovered.

wrong_explanations.A: Rewriting data is impractical because the hard disk is damaged and offers less assurance than physical destruction even when done successfully.
wrong_explanations.B: Low-level formatting is impractical because the hard disk is damaged and offers less assurance than physical destruction even when done successfully.
wrong_explanations.C: Degaussing is highly effective but offers less assurance than physical destruction.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Authorizing access to application data is the responsibility of the:

options.A: data custodian.
options.B: application administrator.
options.C: data owner.
options.D: security administrator.

questions.correct_explanation: Data owners have authority to grant or withhold access to the data and applications for which they are responsible.

wrong_explanations.A: Data custodians are responsible only for storing and safeguarding the data according to the direction provided by the data owner.
wrong_explanations.B: An application administrator is responsible for managing the application itself, not determining who is authorized to access the data that it contains.
wrong_explanations.D: The security administrator may lead investigations and is responsible for implementing and maintaining information security policy, but not for authorizing data access.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds that a database administrator (DBA) has read-and-write access to production data. The IS auditor should:

options.A: accept the DBA access as a common practice.
options.B: assess the controls relevant to the DBA function.
options.C: recommend the immediate revocation of the DBA access to production data.
options.D: review user access authorizations approved by the DBA.

questions.correct_explanation: When reviewing privileged accounts, the auditor should look for compensating controls that may address a potential exposure.

wrong_explanations.A: Although granting access to production data to the database administrator (DBA) may be a common practice, the information systems (IS) auditor should evaluate the relevant controls.
wrong_explanations.C: The DBA should have access based on the principle of least privilege; unless care is taken to validate what access is required, revocation may remove access positively at the DBA requires to do their job.
wrong_explanations.D: Granting user authorizations is the responsibility of the data owner, not the DBA, and access to production data is not generally associated with user access authorizations.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST effective method for disposing of magnetic media that contains confidential information?

options.A: Degaussing
options.B: Defragmenting
options.C: Erasing
options.D: Destroying

questions.correct_explanation: Destroying magnetic media is the only way to assure that confidential information cannot be recovered.

wrong_explanations.A: Degaussing or demagnetizing is a good control, but not sufficient to fully erase highly confidential information from magnetic media.
wrong_explanations.B: The purpose of defragmentation is to improve efficiency by eliminating fragmentation in file systems; it does not remove information.
wrong_explanations.C: Erasing or deleting magnetic media does not remove the information; this method simply changes a file's indexing information.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
RTO measures downtime tolerance; RPO measures data-loss tolerance. Lower numbers cost more — match them to business criticality, not gut feel.

questions.question: Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor recommend for the protection of specific sensitive information stored in a data warehouse?

options.A: Implement column-and row-level permissions.
options.B: Enhance user authentication via strong passwords.
options.C: Organize the data warehouse into subject matter-specific databases.
options.D: Log user access to the data warehouse.

questions.correct_explanation: Column-and row-level permissions control what information users can access. Column-level security prevents users from seeing one or more attributes on a table. With row-level security, a certain grouping of information on a table is restricted (e.g., if a table held details of employee salaries, then a restriction can be put in place to ensure that, unless specifically authorized, users cannot view the salaries of executive staff). Column-and row-level security can be achieved in a relational database by allowing users to access logical representations of data (views) rather than physical tables. This fine-grained security model is likely to offer the best balance between information protection while still supporting a wide range of analytical and reporting uses.

wrong_explanations.B: Enhancing user authentication via strong passwords is a security control that should apply to all users of the data warehouse and does not specifically address protection of specific sensitive data.
wrong_explanations.C: Organizing a data warehouse into subject-specific databases is a potentially useful practice but, alone, does not adequately protect sensitive data. Database-level security is normally too coarse of a level to efficiently and effectively protect information. For example, one database may hold information that needs to be restricted, such as employee salary and customer profitability details, while other information, such as employee department, may need to be legitimately accessed by a large number of users. Organizing the data warehouse into subject-matter-specific databases is similar to user access in that this control should generally apply. Extra attention can be devoted to reviewing access to tables with sensitive data, but this control is not sufficient without strong preventive controls at the column and row level.
wrong_explanations.D: Logging user access is important, but it is only a detective control that does not provide adequate protection to sensitive information.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: The responsibility for authorizing access to a business application system belongs to the:

options.A: data owner.
options.B: security administrator.
options.C: IT security manager.
options.D: requestor's immediate supervisor.

questions.correct_explanation: When a business application is developed, a good practice is to assign an information or data owner to the application. The information owner should be responsible for authorizing access to the application itself or to back-end databases for queries.

wrong_explanations.B: The security administrator normally does not have responsibility for authorizing access to business applications.
wrong_explanations.C: The IT security manager normally does not have responsibility for authorizing access to business applications.
wrong_explanations.D: The requestor's immediate supervisor may share the responsibility for approving user access to a business application system; however, the final responsibility should go to the information owner.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: What is the MOST effective control for enforcing accountability among database users who are accessing sensitive information?

options.A: Implement a log management process.
options.B: Implement a two-factor authentication.
options.C: Use table views to access sensitive data.
options.D: Separate database and application servers.

questions.correct_explanation: Accountability means knowing what is being done by whom. The best way to enforce the principle is to implement a log management process that creates and stores logs with pertinent information, such as username, type of transaction and hour.

wrong_explanations.B: Implementing a two-factor authentication prevents unauthorized access to the database but does not record the activity of the user when using the database.
wrong_explanations.C: Using table views restricts users from seeing data that they should not be able to see but does not record what users did with data that they were allowed to see.
wrong_explanations.D: Separating database and application servers may help with better administration or even in implementing access controls but does not address the accountability issues.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: While auditing an ecommerce architecture, an information systems (IS) auditor notes that customer master data are stored on the web server for six months after the transaction date and then purged due to inactivity. Which of the following is the PRIMARY concern for the IS auditor?

options.A: Availability of customer data
options.B: Integrity of customer data

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is asked to audit the change management process for all IT operational systems. Which of the following documents will BEST aid the auditor in defining the scope for the audit project?

options.A: Enterprise architecture (EA)
options.B: Control catalog
options.C: Risk register
options.D: IT organizational chart

questions.correct_explanation: The enterprise architecture (EA) document provides the IT-environment information that the information systems (IS) auditor needs to be able to define the scope of the audit on the change management process for all IT systems.

wrong_explanations.B: The control catalog is required for an auditor to be able to plan the testing of controls, which is the next step after defining scope.
wrong_explanations.C: The risk register helps the IS auditor to determine the systems to audit, based on the priority of their associated risk and is useful during audit planning but not in defining the scope of the audit.
wrong_explanations.D: The IT organizational chart helps the IS auditor to understand the process flow, which is useful during audit planning but is not the most helpful in defining the scope of the audit.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: In a distributed system, which of the following BEST allows different components or modules to communicate and coordinate their activities?

options.A: Message queue interface
options.B: Application programming interface (API)
options.C: Remote procedure call
options.D: Communication infrastructure interface

questions.correct_explanation: An application programming interface (API) allows components or modules in a distributed system to communicate and coordinate their activities. An API defines a set of rules and protocols that enable the interaction and exchange of data between software components.

wrong_explanations.A: A message queue interface is a specific type of interface that is used for asynchronous communication between applications through message queues, but it is not a general-purpose interface for coordinating activities in a distributed system.
wrong_explanations.C: A Remote Procedure Call (RPC) is a communication protocol that allows a program to execute a procedure or function in a different address space, but it is not specifically focused on coordinating activities in a distributed system.
wrong_explanations.D: Communication infrastructure interface is an interface between the application platform and the communication infrastructure.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which interface allows different software applications to access and manipulate a relational database management system (RDBMS)?

options.A: Application programming interface (API)
options.B: Structured query language (SQL)
options.C: Object-relational mapping
options.D: Java database connectivity

questions.correct_explanation: An application programming interface (API) allows different software applications to access and manipulate a relational database management system (RDBMS). The API provides a set of functions, methods or protocols that enable developers to interact with the database, perform queries and manage data.

wrong_explanations.B: Structured Query Language (SQL) is a programming language specifically designed for managing and manipulating relational databases, but it is not an interface. SQL is typically used with an API to interact with the database.
wrong_explanations.C: Object-relational mapping is a technique that allows developers to map between objects in an application and relational database tables, but it is not an interface for accessing the RDBMS.
wrong_explanations.D: Java database connectivity is a Java API that provides methods for connecting to and interacting with a database using the Java programming language, but it is specific to Java and not a general-purpose interface.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following allows software systems or applications to access and interact with a cloud-based infrastructure or service provider?

options.A: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP)
options.B: Remote procedure call
options.C: Circuit-level gateway
options.D: Application programming interface (API)

questions.correct_explanation: An application programming interface (API) allows software systems or applications to access and interact with a cloud-based infrastructure or service provider. APls provide a set of rules and protocols that enable developers to integrate their applications with cloud services, access resources and perform various operations.

wrong_explanations.A: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a network management protocol used for monitoring and managing network devices, but it is not designed specifically for accessing cloud-based infrastructure or service providers.
wrong_explanations.B: A Remote Procedure Call (RPC) is a communication protocol that allows a program to execute a procedure or function in a different address space, but it is not designed specifically for accessing cloud-based infrastructure or service providers.
wrong_explanations.C: A circuit-level gateway is a telecommunication gateway for transferring data from different networks but is not designed specifically for accessing cloud-based infrastructure or service providers.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST useful for effective security log management?

options.A: Implementing automated tools to collect, analyze and retain logs
options.B: Archiving and storing logs indefinitely to ensure historical data availability
options.C: Collecting all logs from all systems, databases, devices and tools
options.D: Security manager reviewing logs daily to detect and respond to security incidents

questions.correct_explanation: Effective security log management involves automated tools and processes to collect, analyze and retain logs from various systems and devices within an organization's IT infrastructure. Automated log management solutions help streamline the log collection process, centralize logs from different sources, apply real-time analysis techniques to identify security incidents and retain logs for an appropriate period based on regulatory and compliance requirements. Automated tools can process large volumes of log data and identify abnormal patterns or suspicious activities that a human analyst might miss. These tools can also generate alerts in real time when they detect potential security incidents.

wrong_explanations.B: Storing logs indefinitely is not feasible due to storage limitations and may not align with enterprise and regulatory data retention policies.
wrong_explanations.C: It is important to identify the types and nature of logs to be collected for analysis and from which systems, databases, devices and tools they should be collected. All logs may not be collected.
wrong_explanations.D: Having a security officer review logs daily may be tiresome, time-consuming and impractical for enterprises with a large volume of logs. Automated systems may ease the work of detecting incidents.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Which of the following is a KEY benefit of using version control systems in configuration and release management?

options.A: Manages complexity in code management
options.B: Eases collaboration with multiple developers
options.C: Limits accessibility for developers
options.D: Provides ability to track and revert changes

questions.correct_explanation: Using version control systems enables the tracking of code changes, including who made the changes, when they were made and what modifications were implemented. This functionality allows for easy identification of issues, collaboration among developers and the ability to revert to previous versions if needed, promoting better configuration and release management.

wrong_explanations.A: Version control systems provide structure and organization to code repositories, making it easier to manage changes, track versions and collaborate effectively; however, tracking changes is the key benefit of using version control systems in configuration and release management.
wrong_explanations.B: Version control systems facilitate collaboration among multiple developers by providing a centralized platform for code sharing, version tracking and merging changes. They enable concurrent development, branching and merging of code, enhancing collaboration rather than making it difficult. However, tracking changes is essential in case of operational issues detected later.
wrong_explanations.C: Version control systems offer access controls so developers cannot arbitrarily access code libraries and make untraceable changes. It is complementary to tracking code changes.

tips: Production changes require: documented request → impact analysis → approval → tested change → back-out plan → post-change verification. Skipping any step is a finding.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST helps an information systems (IS) auditor to detect the problems encountered by application executions during IT operations?

options.A: Operating system logs
options.B: Incident reports
options.C: Exception reports
options.D: Computer operator logs

questions.correct_explanation: Exception reports are automated reports that list the problems encountered by the application during execution.

wrong_explanations.A: Operating system logs help in identifying problems encountered by operating systems and may not report application-related problems.
wrong_explanations.B: Application execution problems may not be reported as incidents and would not appear in incident reports unless the interruption is significant enough to be considered an incident.
wrong_explanations.D: Computer operator logs are manually entered by the operator during operations; these logs may or may not identify specific problems with applications.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Treat symptoms only after you've identified the root cause — quick fixes without root-cause analysis tend to recur and mask deeper issues.

questions.question: Which of the following is a MAIN benefit of monitoring operational logs?

options.A: It provides early warnings of possible risk materialization.
options.B: It helps information systems (IS) auditors in detecting problems encountered during operations.
options.C: It gives insight into the health and performance of the IT infrastructure.
options.D: It provides audit trails for transactions processed during operations.

questions.correct_explanation: Operational log monitoring primarily helps in providing insight about the IT infrastructure and provides data to build performance metrics for various IT resources (e.g., central processing unit (CPU) performance, storage capacity usage, network bandwidth usage and maximum number of transactions).

wrong_explanations.A: Monitoring operational logs provides early warnings about possible risk materialization before it becomes an incident; however, all operational logs do not provide such information.
wrong_explanations.B: Auditors use sampling methods to review logs that are identified by certain criteria (e.g., operation termination, login to sensitive accounts and transactions beyond defined thresholds). Monitoring such operational logs helps in detecting problems in the identified area, but the logs are limited and provide limited benefit.
wrong_explanations.D: Audit trails are more useful for ensuring appropriate processing of a transaction and they may not identify problems in processing.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST helps an information systems (IS) auditor in ensuring that automated data conversion from an old system to a new system has been completed successfully?

options.A: Operator reports
options.B: Exception reports
options.C: Control totals
options.D: Application logs

questions.correct_explanation: Exception reports are automated reports that identify errors encountered during processing, including transactions that are not converted automatically.

wrong_explanations.A: Operator reports are manual logs of errors identified by the computer operator.
wrong_explanations.C: Control totals help in ensuring that data has been converted completely but may not identify a specific record that was not converted.
wrong_explanations.D: Application logs provide errors encountered during application execution.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is a MAJOR challenge in implementing a log management system?

options.A: Complexity of the IT infrastructure
options.B: Multiple formats of logs collected
options.C: Cost of storage due to the volume of logs
options.D: Addressing false-positive alerts

questions.correct_explanation: Addressing the complexity of the IT resources that generate logs is a major challenge because the performance of many resources deteriorates when logging is enabled. Therefore, it is necessary to determine the type of logs to be captured from each resource.

wrong_explanations.B: The multiplicity of log formats can be challenging; however, this can be addressed using appropriate parsing techniques.
wrong_explanations.C: Storage cost is a comparatively lesser challenge and can be managed with appropriate budget and retention periods.
wrong_explanations.D: Addressing false positives during the initial periods of implementation can be addressed by appropriate planning and implementing tools in a phased manner.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
